title: Bornholm Energy Island link moves closer after government approval
content:
Bornholm Energy Island link moves closer after government approval TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
Bornholm Energy Island link moves closer after government approval
Denmark’s Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities has approved a project
that will allow Bornholm’s electricity grid to be connected to the planned
Bornholm Energy Island. The decision follows a political agreement reached
in February 2026.
“Our analyses show that the solution is both technically feasible and
can contribute to a robust electricity supply," says Klaus Winther,
Vice President of System Operations at Energinet.
Energinet and TREFOR Elnet Øst are now progressing preparations for the
connection. The project aims to strengthen Bornholm’s long-term electricity
supply as demand is expected to rise through electrification, the green
transition and new business opportunities.
Bornholm is currently supplied mainly through an electricity cable to Sweden,
which is expected to remain in service until 2035. The island’s peak electricity
demand is around 50 MW, while upgrades to the Swedish connection are expected
to increase available capacity to 57 MW.
According to the announcement the project includes three new transformers
and associated facilities as part of the energy island’s electricity infrastructure.
Construction is currently expected to begin in 2027.

title: Submarine cable installation begins for Sicily-Calabria power connection
content:
Submarine cable installation has begun on the "Bolano-Annunziata"
power line, a project that will connect Sicily and Calabria through a 380
kV AC electricity connection.
According to Terna the link is expected to increase electricity exchange
capacity between the island and mainland Italy to 2,000 MW, supporting
greater integration of renewable energy into the grid.
The project includes the installation of three submarine cables, each measuring
7.5 km in length and laid at depths of up to 250 metres.
According to the announcement, the project marks the first time 380 kV
alternating current submarine cables with XLPE insulation have been installed
on Italy’s national transmission grid.
Two underground cable links are also being constructed to connect the submarine
cable landings with the Annunziata and Bolano substations. The onshore
routes will extend approximately 3 km in Sicily and 500 metres in Calabria.
Construction is also progressing on the new Annunziata substation and the
expansion of the Bolano substation.
The project represents a key milestone in strengthening electricity transmission
infrastructure between Sicily and mainland Italy while enabling the continued
expansion of renewable energy capacity.

title: Welsh businesses invited to support Erebus floating wind project
content:
Blue Gem Wind’s Erebus
has invited Welsh businesses to play a role in the floating offshore wind
industry following the launch of its procurement strategy.
The milestone marks a significant step for the project, strengthening their
presence in Wales while supporting the development of the local offshore
wind supply chain.
According to the announcement, the procurement strategy will support the
delivery of the consented 100 MW Erebus test and demonstration project,
located off the Pembrokeshire coast.
Cabinet Minister for Economy, Connectivity and Energy Adam Price said:
“Offshore wind can bring real economic benefits to Wales, driving innovation,
creating new opportunities for businesses, and regenerating our coastal
communities.”
Construction of the project is expected to generate 700 direct jobs and
800 indirect jobs across a range of roles, including manufacturing, fabrication,

and operations and maintenance.
Opportunities are available to businesses already established in the offshore
energy sector, as well as those with transferable skills in engineering,
construction, manufacturing, technology and logistics.

title: Japan’s GSA opens Swiss lab for next-gen battery recycling – Batteries International
content: Japanese chemical and green tech company Green Science Alliance has opened a laboratory dedicated to next-generation battery recycling in Switzerland. The lab, opened on October 19 at the Switzerland Innovation Park Biel/Bienne, operates in partnership with the Swiss Battery Technology Center. Work at the innovation park includes assessing regenerated materials, making electrodes and cells, testing performance, and evaluating industrial potential and scalability. GSA-developed materials for a more sustainable society include biomass-based alternatives to petroleum-derived products to rechargeable batteries, fuel cells and solar cells. GSA said it chose the Swiss site as its base for expanding in Europe and plans further collaborative R&D. The company aims to commercialise its technology in Europe with the help of the innovation park’s network of industrial partners, start-ups and research institutions across the battery value chain. If scaled up, the method could reduce the resources needed for recycling, lessen reliance on newly mined raw materials and support more resilient European battery supply chains, GSA said. Mechanically processing used lithium ion batteries produces a dark powder called black mass, which contains valuable electrode materials. Conventional recycling dissolves it with acids or bases to recover individual metals, which then need several more processing steps before reuse. GSA said its approach is to directly regenerate the cathode active materials so that they can go back into new batteries, without fully breaking them down into elements. This could cut recycling steps and resource use. Early results show that batteries made with regenerated cathode materials reached over 90% of the initial capacity of comparable batteries using commercial materials. title: Saft launches solid-state production lines in France – Batteries International
content: TotalEnergies-owned Saft has launched new production lines for solid-state batteries at its plant in France. The company said on October 19 the Bordeaux site will make Saft the first French manufacturer with the capacity to develop and produce solid-state batteries that use both sulfide and polymer electrolytes at room temperature. Saft did not disclose production capacities or investment costs, but said the technological combination offered increased safety in addition to energy density that is up to 50% higher than that of standard lithium ion batteries. The batteries are produced using a dry electrode process that Saft said is more environmentally responsible, claiming the process cuts CO 2 emissions from this stage of production by up to 40%. CEO Cedric Duclos said solid-state batteries are among the most promising innovations for meeting next-gen electrification needs. “These new production lines mark an important milestone for Saft, as we turn several years of research into real industrial capacity, a statement of our ambition to establish France and Europe as leading players in this strategic technology.” The announcement followed Saft’s October 6 confirmation that it had signed two contracts with Axpo, Switzerland’s largest producer of renewable energy, for the delivery of battery energy storage systems in France. Batteries International reported earlier this year that Saft planned to jointly develop next-gen sodium ion batteries under an agreement with Mana Battery. The firms announced on August 4 the agreement included validating the technology and paving the way for commercialisation — expanding cooperation on technical evaluation that began last year. Target markets for the collaboration include those such as defence and industry, which are already sectors served by lithium ion products from Saft. title: 7 Electric Motorcycles Worth a Look in 2026
content:
Automotive & Mobility
Design & Manufacturing
As major motorcycle brands went electric this year and smaller brands cut prices to compete, prospective riders now have plenty of strong models to choose from.
October 26, 2026
7 Slides

The Can-Am Pulse.
For most of the past two decades, electric motorcycles were not a viable option for most consumers. The main problem was that only small specialty manufacturers produced them. Large motorcycle manufacturers stayed out of the game and relegated their electric efforts to scooters and concept bikes.
As a result, many electric motorcycles from small companies had high prices, limited range, slow charging, and thin dealer networks. To make matters worse, several of these producers ran out of money before they could perfect their motorbikes.
Fortunately, recent years have seen motorcycle designers resolve many of the problems that plagued older models. For example, they began building liquid-cooled batteries to improve energy density and make the battery packs a structural part of the chassis to save weight. Designers also began adding Combined Charging System (CCS) connectors used by electric cars so riders could use public fast chargers on longer trips.
Related:
Rivian Adds Ghostbusters-Themed Trick Or Treat Mode To R1 & R2 Electric Vehicles For Halloween
This year, many large manufacturers used these innovations to produce their own electric motorcycles. Honda put its first full-size electric motorcycle in European dealerships over the summer, and Royal Enfield began delivering its first electric bike in June. Those launches put electric motorcycles behind large dealer and service organizations, which the specialists have struggled to build. Riders who skipped older electric motorcycles because of range, charging time, or price now have their pick of models that deliver on all three.
We've put together a list of seven electric motorcycles worth riding in 2026. Read on to learn about each one's batteries, range, and price.

title: Samsung SDI Signs 1-GWh ESS Deal, Expands Indiana Storage Push
content:
Battery News
Stationary Batteries
Battery Manufacturing
The agreement with Alpha Omega Power will be built at Kokomo's StarPlus Energy plant — a facility whose ownership future remains unresolved even as Samsung SDI leans harder into ESS.
October 26, 2026
4 Min Read
StarPlus Energy plant in Kokomo, IN.
Commercial Contracting Corporation
At a Glance
Samsung SDI and Alpha Omega Power sign a 1 GWh ESS supply deal, bringing their total agreements to 1.5 GWh.
The batteries will be built at Samsung SDI's StarPlus Energy plant in Kokomo, Indiana, using NCA prismatic cells.
The deal underscores Samsung SDI's pivot toward energy storage in Indiana as U.S. EV battery demand slows.
Samsung SDI is deepening its bet on US energy storage, announcing a
1 GWh supply agreement with Alpha Omega Power
(AOP), a utility-scale battery storage developer and independent power producer. Combined with an initial contract signed late last year, the two companies' agreements now total 1.5 GWh — all of it to be built at Samsung SDI's StarPlus Energy (SPE) plant in Kokomo, Indiana.
AOP plans to deploy the systems for large-scale projects in the WECC and ERCOT power markets, two regions where utilities and independent power producers are racing to add storage capacity to firm up renewables integration and meet surging demand tied to data centers and electrification. Construction is scheduled to begin next year.
The battery technology behind the deal
The agreement centers on Samsung SDI's Battery Box (SBB) 1.7, a fully integrated ESS solution built around high-nickel nickel cobalt aluminum (NCA) prismatic cells. The company says SBB 1.7 delivers 17% higher energy density than its predecessor, SBB 1.5, while keeping the same 20-foot footprint, and incorporates AI-driven algorithms for anomaly detection and battery life prediction across a 25-year design life. On the safety side, the system has secured NFPA 855 and UL 9540 certification and uses Samsung SDI's proprietary Enhanced Direct Injection technology, which pumps fire-suppressant directly into individual battery modules rather than relying on broader enclosure-level suppression.
Related:
Battery Breaking-News Headlines
Samsung SDI's Battery Box (SBB) 1.7. Credit: Samsung SDI
Samsung SDI is positioning the deal as proof of its differentiated standing in the market: the company says it remains the only non-Chinese supplier of prismatic ESS batteries in North America, and it is leaning on that distinction — along with prismatic cells' reputed durability and fire safety advantages over pouch-type designs — to win business from US developers facing increasingly strict safety requirements. "American-made ESS from SAMSUNG SDI will play an important role in AOP's continued growth," stated Paul Choi, CEO of Alpha Omega Power. Fabrice Hudry, President of the ESS Team at SAMSUNG SDI America, added that the company intends to "continue to expand our business foundation and strengthen our position in the North American ESS market" through its differentiated technology and local production.
Two Indiana plants have two different stories
The AOP agreement also offers a useful opportunity to clarify a point of potential confusion in Samsung SDI's Indiana footprint, since the company now operates two separate facilities in the state with very different ownership histories.
Related:
Michigan's Battery Bet Isn't Over Yet, Whitmer Tells Industry Leaders
StarPlus Energy, the Kokomo plant that will manufacture the AOP order, was founded in 2022 as a joint venture between Samsung SDI and Stellantis, originally intended to produce NCA lithium-ion EV batteries. As Battery Technology has previously reported, Stellantis was said in February 2026 to be exploring an exit from that venture amid more than €22 billion in company-wide losses tied to its EV strategy, and as of Samsung SDI's August 2026 statements, discussions over the future of StarPlus Energy remained ongoing with no resolution confirmed. Whether that ownership question has since been settled is not publicly clear. (bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-02-10/stellantis-seeks-to-exit-battery-venture-with-samsung-as-ev-losses-mount; electrive.com/2026/02/12/stellantis-likely-to-withdraw-from-battery-joint-venture-with-samsung-sdi; reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/stellantis-seeks-exit-battery-venture-with-samsung-ev-losses-mount-bloomberg-2026-02-10)
New Carlisle's SynergyCells plant has already changed hands
Kokomo is distinct from SynergyCells, the $3.5 billion, 27-GWh plant in New Carlisle, Indiana, that was previously a Samsung SDI–GM joint venture. As covered in
Battery Technology
's August 2026 feature,
Samsung SDI acquired GM's full 49.99% stake in that project
, making New Carlisle the company's first wholly owned North American cell site. Samsung SDI said at the time it would use the plant to "proactively respond to the fast-growing ESS market in the U.S.," even as it and GM separately agreed to co-develop next-generation prismatic EV cells for potential future use there. (batterytechonline.com/automotive-mobility/gm-exits-samsung-sdi-battery-venture-as-ohio-ultium-plant-restarts-production)
Related:
As Energy Storage Demand Explodes, The Battery Show North America Delivers Industry's Most Comprehensive Showcase
Taken together, the two moves describe a broader pattern: automaker partners stepping back from Indiana capacity originally earmarked for EV batteries, while Samsung SDI redirects that same manufacturing base toward stationary storage. That shift tracks with the wider slowdown in U.S. EV demand following the elimination of the federal $7,500 consumer tax credit in September 2025, which has pressured automakers and battery makers alike to rethink capacity commitments built for a faster EV ramp than materialized.
A pivot playing out industry-wide
Samsung SDI's Indiana reshuffling is not happening in isolation. GM has simultaneously revived its Ohio Ultium plant even as it exited the SynergyCells venture, and Ford and Stellantis have each been recalibrating their own U.S. battery manufacturing strategies this year. Against that backdrop, energy storage has emerged as the more reliable near-term growth market, driven by grid reliability needs, renewables buildout, and demand growth in markets like WECC and ERCOT that is less exposed to the policy volatility that has hit EV adoption.
Samsung SDI said it has secured a series of ESS supply deals with U.S. energy companies this year and is in discussions with additional customers, suggesting the AOP agreement is unlikely to be its last in the region. For a company now operating two large Indiana facilities with overlapping but distinct histories, the challenge going forward may be less about winning ESS contracts — demand for which appears robust — and more about resolving the ownership questions still hanging over at least one of those plants.

title: Giga Storage secures financing, grid connection for 1.4 GWh CATL BESS project in Germany - Energy Storage
content: Giga Storage has closed financing for its large-scale “Albatross” battery energy storage system near Neuenkirchen in Lower Saxony, Germany. A consortium of seven banks is providing the Dutch developer with €260 million ($281 million) in debt capital for the project. Construction is scheduled to begin in early 2027, while commissioning is planned for early 2029. The project will have a power output of 350 MW and capacity of 1.4 GWh, with a four-hour duration. The grid connection agreement with Amprion has also been signed. Commissioning is now scheduled for early 2029. The participating lenders in the financing round are ABN Amro, Hamburg Commercial Bank, ING, Rabobank, Siemens Financial Services via Siemens Bank, SMBC, and Société Générale. Giga Storage had previously announced in early October that the project had reached ready-to-build status. At that time, the company still expected the final investment decision in the fourth quarter, and commissioning was originally slated for 2028. Meanwhile, Giga Storage also signed a grid connection agreement with German transmission system operator (TSO) Amprion, and the agreement was concluded on October 14. Amprion stated that this marks the company’s first grid connection contract for a large-scale battery storage facility. The system will be connected directly to the 380 kV transmission grid at the Merzen substation. The storage facility will consist of 264 battery containers, 96 medium-voltage transformers, and two high-voltage transformers. According to Giga Storage, CATL will handle the engineering, construction, and maintenance of the facility, working alongside several European subcontractors. “Albatross” is Giga Storage’s first utility-scale storage project in Germany. Together with its “Leopard” project in the Netherlands and the “Green Turtle” project in Belgium, the company states that it currently has storage projects with a combined output of around 1.4 GW and a total capacity of 5.6 GWh under construction. title: Samsung SDI signs 1 GWh supply agreement for US-made NCA battery storage - Energy Storage
content: Samsung SDI has signed a deal to supply 1 GWh of nickel cobalt aluminum (NCA) battery storage to a single US customer, with all cells and modules to be manufactured in the United States. Under the agreement with utility and independent power producer Alpha Omega Power (APO), Samsung SDI is expected to deliver its Samsung Battery Box (SBB) 1.7 containerized energy storage to projects scheduled to being construction in 2027. These will include projects in the Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC) and Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) energy markets. All cells and modules for the  battery containers covered in the supply agreement will be manufactured at Samsung SDI’s StarPlus Energy (SPE) plant in Kokomo, Indiana, according to the manufacturer, with delivery expected before the end of 2026. In choosing Samsung SDI as a supplier, APO is putting significant investment into NCA chemistry battery storage in a global market where cells using lithium iron phosphate (LFP) based chemistry continue to lead. The investment also comes as the US government mulls further restrictions on imported power equipment. Samsung SDI reports that the SBB 1.7 uses a high-nickel NCA chemistry and delivers 17% higher energy density than its predecessor, the SBB 1.5, while maintaining the same 20-foot footprint. The manufacturer also highlights fire safety as a key feature of the design, noting the battery storage solution incorporates Samsung SDI’s proprietary Enhanced Direct Injection technology, which directly injects fire-extinguishing agents into individual battery modules. The latest agreement means Samsung SDI has been contracted to supply a total of 1.5 GWh of energy storage to APO, following an earlier supply contract signed in 2025. In a press release, Fabrice Hudry president ESS of Samsung SDI America, said the company’s “differentiated technology” and US production capabilities will see it continue to expand in the North American ESS market. title: Spain announces 27 renewable projects with 1.78 GW of BESS - Energy Storage
content: Spain published announcements for 27 renewable energy projects involving BESS in the third quarter of 2026, including standalone battery installations and projects combining storage with existing solar and wind farms. Among the largest projects is Jinko Power Energy’s proposed 150.8 MW BESS La Puebla 3 in Cerro de Andévalo, Huelva, which would be integrated with the existing La Puebla 3 solar park. FRV also submitted announcements for BESS Gaetana, a 108 MW battery system intended to be combined with a 166.4 MW solar plant in Badajoz to form a 180 MW hybrid installation, and BESS Aurea, a 117.6 MW battery system for an existing 171 MW solar plant in the same province. FRV’s other announcement covers the 49.94 MW BESS Camarreal project in Camargo. Several announcements concern battery systems being added to existing solar installations. Solaria’s projects include the 45 MW Maira Gamma battery system, paired with a 140.127 MW solar installation in Burgos; a 19.993 MW system at Solaria-Tordesillas II in Valladolid; and a 31 MW Pegaso battery system, also in Valladolid, intended for the 77.35 MW Pegaso Solar installation. Solaria also announced the 22.26 MW Talayuela II BESS project in Cáceres, which would be combined with an existing 44.55 MW solar plant to form a 66.81 MW hybrid installation. Bruc Energy’s announcements cover multiple battery systems in Seville province. These include the 39.6 MW Freya system, paired with an existing 44 MW solar park in Carmona; the 39.6 MW Artemisa and Elvisa systems, each intended for an existing 46.2 MW solar park in Alcalá de Guadaíra; the 28.37 MW Bianor system, paired with a 33 MW solar park in Utrera; and four further 39.6 MW systems named SES, Jade, Esmeralda and Heracles, each intended for an existing 46.2 MW solar park in Alcalá de Guadaíra. Other solar-linked projects include Opdenergy’s 24.04 MW OPDE Miramundo system in Puerto Real, Cádiz, for an existing 49.99 MW solar plant, and its 26.74 MW Hibridación Larral project in Zaragoza, intended for an existing 40 MW solar installation. Ignis announced the 21.6 MW MGE Almacenamiento Mulhacén system for a 70 MW solar plant in Toledo, as well as two battery systems at Azor Solar in the Madrid region, rated at 23.898 MW and 44.614 MW, for a 64.02 MW solar plant. Sonnedix’s 40 MW BESS Los Frailes project in Badajoz would be paired with a 40.25 MW solar plant. Additional announcements cover projects from Enel Green, X-Elio, Grenergy, Dargon Energy and other developers. Enel Green’s 41.58 MW BESS Mudéjar project in Teruel would be combined with the 66 MW Mudéjar-Millán Hernández Bonaga solar park; the same announcement also rejected preliminary administrative authorization for a proposed 75 MW San Jorge wind module. X-Elio’s 83.709 MW La Atalaya battery project in Villena, Alicante, is intended for the 96.884 MW La Atalaya solar plant. Grenergy’s announcements cover the 21.69 MW Aspe and Aitana battery systems, each intended for an existing 49.11 MW solar installation in Cuenca. Dargon Energy’s PHFV Castellet project is a 4.99 MW storage installation in Catalonia. Several projects would combine batteries with wind power or with existing hybrid renewable energy facilities. EDP’s 19.5 MW Castillo Garcimuñoz battery system in Cuenca would be integrated with an existing 25.5 MW wind farm and a 20.925 MW hybrid solar installation, forming a 30 MW hybrid facility. Iberdrola announced a 35 MW battery system for the 44.681 MW Virgen de Areños III solar plant in Palencia, as well as a 30.3 MW battery system for the 70.4 MW Iglesias wind farm in Burgos. RIC Energy’s 21.6 MW BESS system would be added to the 24.035 MW Greencar 3 hybrid installation in Carmona, Seville. Statkraft’s Talayuela II project is among the announcements for battery systems integrated with existing solar facilities. Elawan’s 20 MW Frontones Phase II storage project in Albacete would be added to an existing complex comprising a 50 MW wind farm, a 26.25 MW hybrid solar plant and a 4 MW storage installation, forming a hybrid facility with a stated capacity of 60 MW. Benbros announced the 49.738 MW BESS Solorzano project in Cantabria. The announcements cover different stages of the administrative process, including applications for preliminary administrative authorization and construction authorization, environmental assessment and declarations of public utility. Publication of an announcement does not necessarily mean that a project has secured all required permits or will proceed to construction. The published list identifies the initial promoters of the projects. Some may have since been sold or transferred. title: Trina Storage to supply 196 MWh battery system for Japan's Nozu project - Energy Storage
content: Trina Storage, the battery energy storage business of China’s Trinasolar, has been selected to supply battery storage systems for the 50 MW/196 MWh AEJ Nozu project in Oita Prefecture, Japan. The company announced the contract on October 14, with project completion scheduled for the third quarter of 2028. Located in Nishihata, Nozu Town, Usuki City, the grid-scale facility will have a nominal storage duration of approximately 3.9 hours. It is being developed by Nozomi Energy, a Japanese renewable energy platform backed by infrastructure investor Actis, through its project company AEJ Nozu Storage Power Plant Contract Company. The project secured a capacity contract in Japan’s fiscal 2023 Long-Term Decarbonization Auction, providing inflation-linked capacity payments over 20 years. Nozomi Energy reached financial close in September 2026 after securing non-recourse project financing from Japan’s Aozora Bank. The financing amount has not been disclosed. China Energy Engineering Shanxi Electric Power Engineering Co., Ltd. has separately secured the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract for the project’s balance-of-plant works. The company said the development had obtained key land and grid-connection permits. Trina Storage will supply its Elementa 2 Pro battery energy storage solution, built around standardized 5 MWh containerized units. According to the manufacturer’s technical documentation, the system uses its proprietary 314 Ah lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, with a nominal energy capacity of 5.015 MWh per container and a DC voltage architecture approaching 1,500 V. The system is housed in a standard 20-foot high-cube container and incorporates liquid cooling, battery monitoring and multiple layers of safety protection. Trina Storage says its thermal management design maintains cell temperature differences within 2.5 C, while the system features IP67-rated battery modules and an IP55-rated enclosure. Additional safety features include temperature and smoke monitoring, active ventilation and fire suppression systems. Trina Storage specifies a cell cycle life of up to 12,000 cycles for the product, although the company has not disclosed project-specific operating assumptions or performance guarantees for the Nozu installation. The manufacturer said its Japanese operations will support system configuration, technical consultation, delivery coordination and after-sales services, working with local project partners to address technical and regulatory requirements. “For Nozu and other projects in Japan, our focus is on combining advanced technology with strong local capabilities,” said Leo Zhao, head of energy storage for Asia-Pacific at Trina Storage. The contract adds to Trina Storage’s Japanese project portfolio, which includes a separate 160 MWh utility-scale BESS in the Kyushu region. In September, the company also signed a memorandum of understanding with Japanese developer AMP-lify covering approximately 1 GWh of potential grid-connected storage projects using its newer Elementa 3 series. Nozu is among the battery storage developments supported by Japan’s long-term decarbonization capacity mechanism, which is intended to encourage investment in low-carbon generation and flexible power resources. The project’s long-term contracted capacity revenue provides greater revenue visibility for its developer, while construction, equipment delivery and commissioning remain ahead of its planned 2028 completion. The value of Trina Storage’s supply contract and the project’s total investment cost have not been disclosed. title: All aboard! Massachusetts is getting 10 new electric transit trains
content:
Electric train
Public Transit
Jo Borrás
| Oct 26 2026 - 4:42 am PT
The Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (MBTA) board of directors voted unanimously Thursday to approve the purchase of a new generation of battery-powered public transit trains – and they can’t arrive soon enough.
“(MBTA) has, obviously, an immediate need for locomotives,”
explains William Wolfgang, the MBTA’s senior director of vehicle engineering
. The new machines will replace the oldest locomotives in the MBTA fleet, GP40s built more than 50 years ago and F40s that are well over 30 years old.
In a presentation to the MTBA board
, MTBA said 13 of the GP40s have, “exceeded their useful life,” while the F40s will reach the end of their life between 2029 and 2035.
The MBTA will put in an order for 20
Siemens-built
“Charger” locomotives; 10 Tier 4 diesel-powered hybrid electric units and 10 dual-mode battery/
catenary
electric units – and, beyond trackside power for charging the batteries, there are other challenges presented by going electric, most notably using existing cab cars to control the battery-electric units. “We’re going to have to work with railroad operations, engineering, and the Brotherhood of [
Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen
] to try and determine the best way to handle that,” adds Wolfgang. “That will be an upcoming change order once we get into the design review process.”
The total bill comes out to $310.4 million. A combination of state and federal funding will pay for the order,
including a recent $200 million transfer from the Massachusetts Department of Transportation
The contract includes an option for additional locomotives, although details were not discussed during the meeting. Delivery of the new Siemens Charger trains is set to begin in 2029, with all 20 set to be in service by the end of 2030. Siemens has delivered 440 Charger model hybrid- and battery-electric locomotives globally at the time of this writing.

title: Amflow launches two powerful new electric bikes, including its first SUV-style e-bike
content:
Micah Toll
| Oct 26 2026 - 1:01 am PT
Amflow, the electric bicycle brand that burst onto the scene with some of the most powerful and lightweight electric mountain bikes on the market, is expanding its lineup with two major releases. The company has announced global availability of its new Amflow TL Carbon, while also bringing its removable-battery Amflow PR Carbon series to the US for the first time.
Both models are powered by the latest Avinox mid-drive motor systems, which have quickly earned a reputation for delivering impressive power in surprisingly compact packages.
The biggest departure from
Amflow’s
roots is the new TL Carbon, which takes the company’s high-performance mountain biking DNA and applies it to a more versatile SUV-style electric bike. While less common in the US (ironically), SUV-style e-bikes are essentially a hybrid electric bicycle designed to act as an all-in-one, “do-it-all” vehicle combining the rugged build and off-road capability of an electric mountain bike with the practical, everyday utility of a city or trekking bike.
Rather than focusing exclusively on technical trails and aggressive mountain biking, the TL Carbon is designed to handle everything from daily commuting to touring and off-road adventures. And with Avinox’s RS800 battery featuring 800Wh of capacity, it’s got plenty of energy on board for diverse adventures.
The full-suspension bike uses the Avinox M2 motor, delivering up to 125 Nm of torque, which should provide more than enough grunt for steep climbs, heavy loads, and just about anything else riders can throw at it.
Avinox e-bike drive systems are known for many things, but chief among them is the
extremely high power and torque they offer
, eclipsing most other mid-drive motor systems on the market.
Despite that power and versatility, the TL Carbon weighs as little as 22.6 kg (49.8 lb). It also boasts an impressive maximum total weight capacity of 200 kg (441 lb), including the bike itself, rider, and cargo carried on its front and rear racks.
That’s a compelling combination for riders who want the performance of a premium electric mountain bike but need something practical enough to replace a car for everyday trips.
And perhaps most surprisingly, the price isn’t completely outrageous. The Amflow TL Carbon starts at $3,899 in the US and €3,499 in Germany, positioning it competitively against premium European trekking and SUV-style e-bikes.
Meanwhile, American riders are finally getting access to the Amflow PR Carbon series, which had previously launched in other markets.
Unlike Amflow’s earlier electric mountain bikes, the PR series features a removable battery, addressing one of the biggest practical complaints about high-performance eMTBs with integrated batteries.
The new 800 Wh battery weighs just 4 kg (8.8 lb) and can be removed for convenient indoor charging or swapped for a fresh battery to extend a ride. That’s especially useful for riders who don’t have a convenient charging outlet near their bike storage area.
Amflow claims up to 158 km (98 miles) of range under ideal conditions, though that’s based on relatively gentle riding on flat pavement in Eco mode. Riders tackling technical trails with high assistance levels should expect considerably less. But any way you slice it, 800 Wh is a huge battery for eMTBs and should deliver plenty of range under most conditions.
The standard PR Carbon uses the Avinox M2 motor with up to 125 Nm of torque, while the higher-end PR Carbon Pro upgrades to the more powerful Avinox M2S motor, producing up to 150 Nm of torque.
In the US, the PR Carbon starts at $4,999, while the PR Carbon Pro commands $6,799. European pricing starts at €4,499 and €5,899, respectively, based on German pricing.
All three bikes are available beginning today through ⁠Amflow’s official website and its network of authorized dealers. In the US, both models generally arrive as Class 1 e-bikes (no throttle) with a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h), though Amflow models can typically be unlocked to Class 3 performance with a top speed of 28 mph (45 km/h).
Electrek’s Take
Amflow has been one of the more interesting brands to watch in the premium e-bike space, largely because of how aggressively it has pushed the boundaries of motor performance and bike weight.
But these latest releases show that the company is thinking beyond simply building increasingly powerful electric mountain bikes.
The TL Carbon is particularly interesting to me because it brings that impressive Avinox performance to a more practical platform. As someone who spends a minority of my riding time in the dirt, Amflow suddenly looks a lot more interesting to me, personally. Not everyone needs a dedicated eMTB, but plenty of riders would appreciate a lightweight, powerful, well-equipped electric bike that can handle both weekday commuting and weekend adventures.
And the PR Carbon’s removable battery is a welcome development, especially as the industry continues to recognize that convenience and serviceability matter just as much as outright performance.
With the Avinox ecosystem continuing to expand across more bike brands and categories, Amflow is also facing increasing competition from other manufacturers using the same impressive motors. That makes it all the more important for the brand to differentiate itself through thoughtful bike design, not just headline-grabbing power figures.

title: BYD opens pre-orders for its first luxury electric SUV with over 1,000 km CLTC range
content:
Peter Johnson
| Oct 26 2026 - 7:36 am PT
opened pre-orders for the new Denza N8, a luxury five-seat electric SUV with a CLTC range of over 1,000 km (621 miles).
BYD Denza N8 orders open with 1,003 km of CLTC range
“The king of large 5-seater pure electric vehicles,” as BYD’s luxury sub-brand Denza calls it, is now available to pre-order in China.
BYD opened pre-orders for the new Denza N8 on Monday, and the results so far “have been excellent,” according to Li Hui, Denza’s general manager.
The new Denza N8 is “definitely the most anticipated luxury SUV of the year,” Li said. Denza confirmed in August that the new version will use its Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging Technology to deliver “a world-leading 1,003 km pure electric range.”
Although BYD has released several luxury EVs that offer more than 1,000 km of CLTC range, such as
the Denza Z9 GT
, this is its first electric SUV to break the 1,000 km mark under CLTC conditions.
BYD Denza N8 (Source: Denza)
For context, the plug-in hybrid version the new Denza N8 is replacing offered a combined CLTC range of 1,003 km (623 miles) on a full tank of gas and a full charge.
BYD didn’t reveal pre-order prices, but Li confirmed last week that the
Denza N8’s official launch
is scheduled for November.
It will go on sale after the new Denza N8L, a slightly longer six-seat version. The N8L is available in two versions: Premium and Flagship. The N8L EV Premium starts at 299,800 RMB, or about $45,000, while the Flagship model is priced from 329,800 RMB ($49,000).
Denza N8 EV interior (Source: Denza)
Those who place a reservation with a 2,000 RMB ($200) deposit will receive a 5,000 RMB credit as a limited-time special offer.
Measuring 5,150 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,820 mm high, with a 3,075 mm wheelbase, the Denza N8 EV is slightly longer than the Kia EV9 and Hyundai IONIQ 9.
Inside, the five-seat electric SUV features a massive 30″ infotainment screen that spans nearly the entire passenger-side dashboard, plus a new 43″ (1.1 meter) panoramic head-up display (PHUD) at the bottom of the windshield.
Other premium features include zero gravity seating in all rows, a three-spoke steering wheel, wireless phone chargers, and ambient lighting.
The luxury SUV is equipped with a roof-mounted LiDAR to support BYD’s God’s Eye 5.0 smart driving assistance system. It also features DiSus-A, BYD’s intelligent air suspension system, and rear-wheel drive.
The new Denza N8 EV will be available with a single rear-wheel-drive (RWD) or a tri-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The RWD version uses a single motor producing either 320 kW (429 hp) or 370 kW (496 hp).
BYD’s new Denza N8 and N8L CLTC driving range, battery specs, and more (Source: China MIIT)
The tri-motor Denza N8 uses BYD’s e3 platform. The setup includes a 270 kW (362 hp) front motor and two 310 kW (416 hp) rear motors, delivering a combined output of 890 kW (1,193 hp).
Regulatory filings earlier this year revealed it will be available with a 130.15 kWh or 105.79 kWh BYD Blade 2.0 battery, offering CLTC ranges of up to 1,003 km and 800 km, respectively.
BYD will announce prices next month, but given that the Denza N8L starts at 299,800 RMB ($45,000), the standard version will likely be priced below it.

title: Range Energy shows how its eTrailer saves almost as much as a Tesla Semi
content:
Range Energy, a company working to electrify trucking through the use of a trailer with its own battery and motors, has published an analysis showing how much fleets can save through electrification – and just at the right time, with diesel at record highs.
You may have heard a little something about diesel prices lately, which have just about doubled in less than a year due to Donald Trump’s war of choice in Iran.
Diesel is now at record highs, and it’s devastating fleets and truck drivers and anyone who uses any products that are delivered on trucks (so, everyone). It’s an urgent problem that needs an urgent solution, and solutions are not forthcoming from the responsible entities.
So, fleets have to seek another solution, and Range Energy would like to be the one that provides it.
Range is a startup based in California, founded and staffed by former Tesla employees and others from around the EV industry. It’s building an electrified trailer which we demoed at ACT Expo in 2024 (really, watch it, it’s a very cool demo) which promises to cut fleet fuel use significantly.
It does this by having its own battery and motors inside the trailer, meaning the tractor doesn’t have to work nearly as hard as the trailer can effectively pull its own weight. Even though the tractor still runs on diesel, it uses a whole lot less of it.
This differs from the other popular option for fleets: full electrification. There are a number of electric semi tractors available, and fleets have been moving to install them, getting their depots ready for charging. But Range lets you bring your own tractor, and electrifies the trailer instead.
Range previously published some early findings, showing a 36% reduction in fuel use in a testing scenario. It also did a pilot program with an egg farm in California, which improved the fuel efficiency of the farm’s diesel fleet by 50-70%.
Now Range has published its own white paper showing comparative savings that fleets can achieve with either its own solution, the eTrailer, or Tesla’s solution, the fully electric Tesla Semi. The paper does not cover the various other electric semi tractors available on the market today, just a face-off between Range and Tesla.
The analysis goes through several scenarios, mostly focusing on refrigerated trailer units (“reefers”), which is the first product Range is focusing on.
Trailer electrification is a great idea for reefers, because they usually fill up on volume rather than weight (called “cubing out”), meaning battery weight doesn’t eat into maximum trailer payload. Batteries also offer power to run refrigeration, meaning you don’t need to have a diesel generator on the trailer.
The upshot of the whole thing is that: fleets can save money with the Range eTrailer, and can theoretically save more money with the Tesla Semi, but the numbers are relatively close in the most common scenario, and the Tesla scenarios have a much wider spread depending on what implementation you consider.
For example, if you only use public chargers rather than your own depot, the Tesla Semi will be more costly because energy will be more expensive to your fleet than if you bought it at commercial utility rates. So, even though installing chargers in your depot sounds expensive, it will pencil out better in the end.
The best money savings came from having two Semis share the same charger, but that requires tight timings and overnight driving.
Another important feature Range points out is build time for a project. The nice thing about the eTrailer is it can slot into fleets immediately with little operational change required, whereas the larger charging needs of an electric tractor) tend to require bigger projects to get a depot ready with chargers (but despite the higher upfront costs, you get better long-term savings, since you avoid diesel entirely with an electric tractor).
In the end, Range found that its solution saves a little more money than the Tesla Semi does in most scenarios, but the difference is quite narrow, with each option having its strengths and weaknesses. Both solutions are better than diesel in most scenarios, but not all of them.
You don’t necessarily need to choose between the two, as an electrified trailer can still be used with an electric tractor. It works the same way in either case – using its own motors to take some of the effort off the tractor. This means extended range, for longer hauls with light loads that couldn’t quite make it on the Tesla Semi’s inherent range. And the benefit of being able to run the reefer while disconnected from the tractor or shore power remains as well.
The analysis has plenty of limitations. It has to estimate future diesel costs (it used a number below current prices, but still historically high), didn’t cover financing costs, it doesn’t have real-world data for the Tesla Semi, didn’t cover electrified tractor or trailer options from other companies, can’t analyze individual charging costs site-to-site since each is specific to a utility company, didn’t cover the myriad incentives available in various regions, and most of all it didn’t consider diesel emissions, which are a huge societal cost to everyone that electrification reduces (and full electrification reduces more).
So in the end, every fleet has a different use case, and should run the numbers themselves to see how either solution would fit in. But in the generalized case, it looks like there are plenty of savings available out there, whether through tractor or trailer electrification.
Top comment by OliveMagnet
I’m not sure I understand their claims when compared to the Semi. Doesn’t the Semi have its own electric takeoff system to power reefers? That means the reefer would be running on the same cost/kWh as the Semi but without the added capex for solar, batteries etc.
I guess if they are only modeling Semi + diesel reefer it makes sense but seems logical fleet operators would power the reefer with the Semi electric takeoff system. In fact, I imagine trailer manufacturers would begin migrating from hybrid reefers to fully electric reefers, removing the diesel components and lowering trailer costs further.
Either way, seems like a great solution when paired with diesel tractors!
Unfortunately, given diesel prices are at record highs right now, both of the options in the paper are a little suboptimal. Tesla Semis have been on order for almost ten years now, and Tesla only just claimed it has started production in earnest. And Range is still about a year out from volume production of its eTrailer, which it says will start in late 2027 – so, while an eTrailer will be able to slot into a fleet immediately when it’s available, it’s not available yet, which puts a damper on that potential benefit.
So neither can offer immediate relief, but both offer good options for fleets to plan for the next inevitable oil shock – which is why Range didn’t base its analysis solely on current prices (remember, we just had another shock in 2022, this nonsense happens all the time, maybe it’s time to stop using oil). But, the numbers in the paper for the Tesla Semi can be compared to numbers for other electric tractors already available today, which can in turn be compared to the costs of the eTrailer, for fleets so inclined to make that comparison.

title: Volkswagen gets L3 autonomous driving test permit in China, eyes 2027
content:
Volkswagen
Volkswagen Group
self-driving
Fred Lambert
| Oct 26 2026 - 6:59 am PT
VW Brand CEO Thomas Schäfer introduces the ID. EVERY1 concept car (Source: Volkswagen)
Volkswagen Group China now has a permit to test Level 3 autonomous driving on public roads in Hefei, and it says testing is already underway. The permit also covers large-scale driving data collection in the city.
It’s the latest step toward VW’s goal of L3 technology readiness in China by 2027. And the timing is good as the group holds its first China Technology Day in Hefei on Wednesday.
VW’s China autonomy stack
VW says the permit was issued under China’s strictest L3 framework and that its setup meets the country’s latest mandatory safety design standards. It didn’t say which authority issued it, how many vehicles are in the fleet, or which roads they can use.
Hefei makes sense as a base. It’s home to the Volkswagen China Technology Company (VCTC), the group’s largest R&D center outside Germany, and to its Volkswagen Anhui production site.
The software comes from CARIZON, VW’s intelligent driving unit in China, which started as a joint venture between CARIAD and Horizon Robotics. Its driver assistance system is called Hyper Sense 8 (HS8), which VW describes as its first “full-scenario” ADAS.
Behind it is GAIA 2.0, a world model VW built itself. VW says it runs simulation equal to 5 million km of safety testing per day, using about 30 million real-road scenario clips, and it wants to get that to 10 million km per day. VW is also developing its own system-on-chip, the C7H, which it says can support up to Level 4.
Ralf Brandstätter, chairman and CEO of Volkswagen Group China, kept the message on safety. He said the group “will never advance technology at the cost of safety” and called the permit an important step on the road to L3 readiness (our translation from Chinese).
A test permit, not a product launch
This is a road test permit. VW can’t sell L3 cars to customers with it.
China’s MIIT granted the country’s first L3 product approvals in December 2025 to two sedans: a Changan model capped at 50 km/h on designated Chongqing expressways, and a BAIC Arcfox model capped at 80 km/h on three Beijing routes. GAC’s Hyptec and XPeng already hold L3 road test permits too. So VW isn’t leading here. It’s catching up to Chinese brands on their home turf.
In July, VW, CARIZON, and Horizon Robotics said they would deepen their partnership, giving CARIZON “white-box” access to Horizon’s AI foundation model, and targeted the start of L3 deliveries in the second half of 2027. VW’s L2++ system is rolling out on seven new NEV models from its Chinese joint ventures this year.
VW also leans on XPeng in China. It bought a
roughly 5% stake in XPeng in 2023
and co-developed its China zonal electrical architecture, CEA, with the startup.
Outside China, the only Western automaker with a certified L3 system on sale is Mercedes-Benz, whose
Drive Pilot
works on approved highways in Germany and in California and Nevada. Mercedes also
got approval to test Level 4 driving in Beijing
back in 2024. Tesla’s FSD remains a Level 2 system everywhere it’s sold, China included.
Electrek’s Take
L3 is where liability moves. When the system is engaged, the automaker is responsible for the driving, not the person in the seat. That’s why so few companies have shipped it, and why the ones that have keep it on a short leash: specific roads, low speeds, mostly traffic jams.
China has been serious about building a framework for automakers to bring this techonology to market, and through it, we are seeing who is interested in this version of autonomy.
Not everyone is. Many automakers, including Tesla, have been talking about “skipping” level 3 and going straight to level 4.

title: A Magnetic Sensor Tile Is Perfect for Secret Gestures
content:
Like many a nerd, I have a certain fascination with locks. This originates in reading the memoir Surely You’re Joking, Mr. Feynman as a teenager, in which Richard Feynman recounts picking locks and cracking combinations while at his day job working on the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos. I currently have a couple of locksport pick sets and training locks that I purchased at hacker conferences over the years (although I’m still terrible at it), and I delight in the YouTube exploits of folks like the LockPickingLawyer.
All of which left me wondering if I could try building an interesting lock. One dodge that lockmakers have long used to challenge would-be plunderers is to conceal the existence of the lock itself. A modern variant of this is the magnetic lock, where a magnet is held or slid against an innocuous portion of a door or box, releasing a catch. The problem with this is that, once you guess the location of the lock, any strong magnet will open it.
So I started thinking about embedding an RFID reader under the surface and resigning myself to keeping track of yet another access card. But then I stumbled across something much more interesting: SparkFun’s US $100 magnetic imaging tile. I realized I could use this to build a magnetic lock that opens with a programmable secret gesture.
I used a few discrete components to drive the servo motor and put the lock into program mode [top], controlled by a Teensy 4.1 microcontroller [middle]. An array of Hall-effect sensors detect magnetic fields [bottom].James Provost
The magnetic imaging tile is a small-run SparkFun board based on the work of Peter Jansen. It features an 8-by-8 grid of Hall-effect sensors, and uses an SPI interface to talk to the microcontroller of your choice. These sensors can detect both the magnitude and polarity of a magnetic field, and the board can report its measurements hundreds to thousands of times per second, depending on how much processing power your microcontroller has available. This is easily fast enough to capture the motion of a magnet being moved by hand across the board’s sensor area—my secret gesture.
An interesting thing about using magnetic fields is that if I was in extreme paranoia mode, I could shield the entire lock behind copper sheeting, something I couldn’t do with an RFID reader. The copper sheet would act as a Faraday cage, blocking any RFID signal, along with any other electromagnetic fields an attacker with an EMF meter might use to locate the lock.
Choosing the Brains of the Box
I chose a Teensy 4.1 as my microcontroller. I like the Teensy because it offers loads of input/output, a 600-megahertz processor, a megabyte of RAM, and a built-in SD card, all in a slim package with an equally slim $32 price tag.
Wiring the Teensy to the magnetic-imaging tile was trivial, only complicated by the fact that one side of the board has a silk-screen error that misidentifies the SPI connections (SparkFun says this will be fixed in future runs of the board).
In extreme paranoia mode, I could shield the entire lock behind copper sheeting.
To create the gesture-recognition software, I once again turned to vibe coding. If you read my Hands On piece in the April 2026 issue of IEEE Spectrum on creating a teletext suite for ham radio, you’ll know I’ve been grappling with how vibe coding should be used in DIY projects, if at all. So this time, instead of letting Claude write all the software, I confined it to writing just two support libraries, which you can find in our online repository at https://github.com/IEEESpectrumHandsOn.
One library is in charge of recording a lock gesture and saving it to the Teensy’s nonvolatile storage. The other library monitors the tile and reports whether or not a newly detected gesture passes a selectable threshold to be considered a match.
I wrote the top-level code myself to keep it as DIY as possible. This code handles things like a button that puts the system in gesture-recording mode after a brief delay, the indicator LED for recording mode, and the code that operates the physical locking mechanism.
Hall-effect sensors rely on a current passing through a p-type slab of silicon. A magnetic field passing through the silicon deflects charge carriers toward the edges of the slab, creating a voltage proportional to the field [left]. By looking at the intensities of the voltages across an 8-by-8 grid of sensors, the microcontroller can reconstruct a gesture [right]. James Provost
Of course, I needed something to lock to demonstrate my proof of concept. I bought a wooden craft box and removed the existing lid latch. I glued a notched beam inside the lid and built a mechanism that uses a servo motor to rotate another beam in and out of this notch. I will be the first to admit this mechanism goes beyond “simple” and into “simplistic,” but it’s sufficiently robust for my demo. The box has ample room for the magnetic imaging tile to be mounted against one wall, along with the Teensy and other supporting electronics. These include a battery pack, the recording button, and a small additional board with two NPN transistors. These convert the Teensy’s 3.3-volt control signals to a 5-V signal needed to drive the servo.
Once it was all put together, I soon discovered that the small size of the magnetic tile’s sensing area—just 3 centimeters square—made it easy to fit the tile inside the box but hard to do the unlock gesture on the outside so that it is read correctly. Marking the outline of the sensor area on the outside defeated the point of having a hidden lock, so instead I once again turned to mining my Irish heritage. I created a Celtic knotwork pattern that runs in a band across the front of the lockbox (I used an online knotwork generator and then projected and traced the pattern onto the box). Using the pattern as a camouflaged reference grid I can make a repeatable gesture within the confines of the sensor area. (To make the gestures I’m using a magnetic stylus borrowed from a ferrite core-memory kit we featured in 2022.)
There’s obvious room for improvement in any more serious installation. The biggest drawback currently is that if the box is locked when the battery runs out, you can’t open it again without breaking something. This could be solved by adding a hidden inductive charging coil. Nonetheless, the demo lockbox works well—now I just have to think what I should store in it!

title: 1 秒下载两万部 4K 电影：3.2Pb/s，我国团队创下单纤双向实时光传输容量的世界纪录
content:
10 月 26 日消息，据科技日报从中国信科集团光通信技术和网络全国重点实验室获悉，该实验室日前联合鹏城实验室、烽火藤仓光纤科技有限公司，成功完成 3.2Pb/s（拍比特每秒）多芯光纤实时双向传输试验，
创下单纤双向实时光传输容量的世界纪录
“3.2Pb/s 的传输速率，
意味着可在一秒内下载两万余部 4K 电影
。”中国信科集团光通信技术和网络全国重点实验室光系统高级工程师杨超表示，该方案验证了多芯光纤超宽带扩容路线产业化潜力，为大型算力枢纽互联、骨干传输及 6G 承载提供下一代高速光通信核心技术支撑。
随着人工智能、大模型计算及数据中心规模化发展，网络流量呈爆发式增长，传统单模光纤传输系统逐步逼近容量极限。针对这一瓶颈，团队创新提出 24 芯多芯光纤双向传输架构，采用 10.3 公里 24 芯多芯光纤，融合 S+C+L 三波段复用与空分复用技术，
构建数千路并行传输通道，使总带宽规模大幅突破传统单模光纤容量上限
。系统搭载商用相干光模块，采用高阶概率整形调制，实现稳定实时双向信号传输；通过芯层排布优化有效抑制芯间串扰，简化信号均衡处理，兼顾传输性能与工程实用性。
“相比传统 C+L 波段商用单芯 G.652 光纤约 100Tb/s 的容量上限，
该系统将单纤总传输容量提升 32 倍
；完成 S 波段单波 400G、C+L 波段单波 1.2Tb/s（太比特每秒）自研光模块的实时传输验证，突破了仅依靠光谱扩容难以逾越的单芯光纤容量墙。”杨超介绍。
IT之家获悉，目前本次成果已作为邀稿投至国际光学权威期刊《Journal of Lightwave Technology》。

title: 亩产 1211.14 公斤：我国玉米种植迎全球新纪录，一个人一部手机管上万亩地
content:
IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，新疆伊犁州玉米完成了田间测产，311.56 万亩平均亩产达 1,211.14 公斤，创下全球同尺度大面积单产最高水平。
专家在玉米田里划定取样面积，收割、脱粒、清杂，称量籽粒鲜重，测定水分含量。今年，伊犁万亩示范区亩产提高到 1609.4 公斤。
新疆伊犁哈萨克自治州察布查尔锡伯自治县农户薛泉生：我今年种了 4 万亩地吧，产量要比去年的高了 100 公斤，每亩增收 200 元左右。今年增产主要原因就是我们的水肥一体化。
薛泉生所说的水肥一体化是大面积单产提升集成增产技术的重要一环。水肥一体化是借助压力灌溉系统把肥料溶进灌溉水里，通过铺在田里的滴灌带直接送到作物根部土壤的农艺技术。和大水漫灌、人工撒肥相比，它能把浇水量、施肥量都拿捏得刚刚好，既增产又节水节肥。
新疆伊犁哈萨克自治州党委农村工作领导小组办公室副主任农业农村局副局长杨虎：上了水肥一体机之后呢，氮肥的利用率从 30% 提高到了 50%，水分的利用率也提高了 30% 到 40%。
新疆伊犁哈萨克自治州察布查尔锡伯自治县农户薛泉生：一个人凭一部手机可以管个五千、一万亩地，很轻松的。我们就平时脚不沾地就把活干了。水、肥料、人工，基本上每亩地较三年前、四年前就要省到 50 块钱左右。
在玉米拔节、抽雄、灌浆等关键期，水肥一体化灵活调配水肥，避免“卡脖子旱”和脱肥，提高结实率和千粒重。同时，小流量滴灌还能缓解土壤板结，避免地表积水径流，减轻土传病害，提升抗倒伏能力。

title: 国内首款 4MW 级 DR40 燃气轮机成功完成 72 小时长期试车试验，主要面向应急电源车等场景
content:
IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，中国航发今日宣布，国内首款 4MW 级 DR40 燃气轮机已于 10 月 22 日成功完成 72 小时长期试车试验。

title: 小米用上苹果 iOS、一加刷华为鸿蒙，手机系统正式进入“互相偷家”时代
content:
AI 对世界的影响可能比你想象的还要大，一些商业公司花费数年建造的技术壁垒，都在最近短短几个月内被逐一攻破。
有 B 站网友昨日（10 月 25 日）发布视频，分享了自己的最新刷机成果 —— 为一台一加 Ace 5 手机成功刷入了鸿蒙 HarmonyOS 6 系统，并实现了 GPU 完美修复。
这台一加 Ace 5 手机在刷入 HarmonyOS 6 系统后，机型显示为华为 Mate 80 Pro，壁纸、系统动效、侧边快捷栏、应用小窗等功能均可以正常运行和使用。
值得一提的是，网友此次刷入的系统并非 OpenHarmony，而是预装于华为手机上的 HarmonyOS 6 系统。评论区中其他网友表示，自己原以为是开源鸿蒙，没想到是真 · 纯血鸿蒙。遗憾的是，目前还不支持 HMS 驱动，Wi-Fi 功能也未完成修复。
此外，关于华为旧机型刷入纯血鸿蒙 HarmonyOS 系统的可能性也成了讨论重点。网友表示，虽然移植难度较大，但项目理论上存在可行性。
一、手机系统“偷家”，小米手机用上苹果 iOS
随着 AI 技术突飞猛进，许多开发者在大模型加持下对各种老旧机型进行折腾，难度也大大降低，可以说手机系统正式进入“互相偷家”时代。
IT之家注意到，最近还有网友发布视频，展示其成功为一部小米 8 手机刷入 iOS 16.5 系统，可以看到该网友将设备机型伪装为 iPhone X，系统元素在小米 8 手机上呈现良好。
该网友在视频简介和评论区中表示，小米 8 和当年的 iPhone X 真的太像了，运行起来颇有当年的感觉，最初 GPU 存在卡顿情况，后续经过修复后流畅了不少。
目前，系统桌面显示和动画已经比较流畅，不过项目整体仍处于早期移植阶段，很多硬件驱动还需要继续适配，暂时不能作为日常系统使用。
公开信息显示，小米 8 于 2018 年 5 月 31 日推出，该机采用 6.21 英寸三星 AMOLED 异型全面屏（刘海屏），机身背部采用四曲面玻璃设计，配合 7 系铝金属中框，搭载了高通骁龙 845 移动平台，内置 3400mAh 电池。
不止小米 8，还有网友成功将一部小米 Redmi Note 12 4G 手机刷入 iOS 16 系统。
据称，这不是主题、启动器或模拟器，而是直接把苹果开源的 XNU 内核（苹果用于 Darwin 系统的混合内核）+ iPhone X 原版用户界面移植了过来。系统设置“关于本机”页面显示系统版本号为 iOS 16.7.16、机型为 iPhone X，触摸和音量键均能正常使用。
作为参考，Redmi Note 12 配备 6.67 英寸 FHD+ 分辨率显示屏，支持 120Hz 刷新，搭载骁龙 685 移动平台和 5000mAh 电池，后置 5000 万像素主摄。Redmi Note 12 5G 与前者配置基本保持一致，仅在处理器方面更换成了骁龙 4 Gen1 移动平台。
二、苹果 iOS 被“围攻”，还有更多惊喜
除了小米刷 iOS，有开发者把“上古刷机神器” HTC HD2 翻了出来，在 10 月 7 日公布了一项复古硬件移植项目，展示了在 HTC HD2 上成功运行 iOS 7 的成果，并公开了相关 XNU 内核及硬件支持代码。
公开信息显示，该项目目前已经能够让 iOS 用户态组件在 HTC HD2 上运行，触摸屏也已实现工作。
HTC HD2 是 HTC 在 2009 年发布的经典智能手机，因能刷入十几种不同操作系统而被称为“刷机之王”，如今又把 iOS 7 收入囊中。
还有更绝的，苹果刚推出折叠屏手机，就有开发者成功为 微软 Surface Duo 2 双屏手机刷入苹果 iOS / iPadOS 26 系统。
开发者表示，在其他人尝试移植 iOS 16/17 时，自己一直在推进 iPadOS 26 移植计划，目前已成功令微软 Surface Duo 2 运行 iOS / iPadOS 26，当下相应移植项目尽管仍处于早期开发阶段，不过已实现双屏运行，在硬件加速方面也取得一定进展。
在最新进展中，开发者透露 Surface Duo 2 的两块屏幕目前均可达到每秒 37 帧（37 FPS）的运行表现。相比之下，此前的运行帧率仅为每秒 3 至 10 帧，性能提升较为明显。
开发者还提到，目前使用的 Surface Duo 2 是一台“专门用于折腾的设备”，因此机身存在屏幕破损等情况。他也开玩笑地表示，后续还有望将微软 Surface Pen 模拟为 Apple Pencil，实现类 iPad 手写笔体验。
此外，开发者表示，如果没有其他人抢先完成相关工作，未来也计划将 iOS / iPadOS 移植到初代 Surface Duo 上，并将最新的 iOS / iPadOS 27 移植到 Surface Duo 2 上。
三、AI 大逆向时代，厂商封锁壁垒“四面漏风”
在软件开发领域，逆向工程（Reverse Engineering）是指通过技术手段对公开的功能进行分析，反推其设计原理。
这项操作在以前的“手工开发”时代就已经流行，但操作十分繁琐，而如今在 AI 加持下，逆向正变得越来越简单。
近期兴起的 AI 逆向还实现了很多有趣的项目，IT之家查询发现，除了安卓手机刷系统提速，还有网友实现了相机固件功能破解，为索尼 A7C II 相机制作定制固件，直接解锁了新款才有的 FL2、FL3 胶片模式。
据介绍，该固件还支持导入外部 LUT，支持富士 NC、理光 GR 直出色调，还能自定义电子快门声音、竖屏显示等，玩法大升级。
目前，这一 A7C II Tools 工具已推出 3.0 版本，是首个拥有正式图形界面的版本，驱动的设置、安装、冷加载和验证都通过一个窗口的按钮完成，甚至不需要命令行。
需要注意的是，该工具仅支持索尼 A7C II（ILCE-7CM2）固件 2.01。它不适用于其他型号，包括原版 A7C、A7 IV、A7CR、A7R V、A6700 和 A7 V。
IT之家提醒：修改相机可能导致无法开机、反复重启、功能异常或数据丢失，也可能影响官方更新、保修或维修。写入成功及读回一致不代表启动安全，恢复功能也不保证能救回相机。另外，有刷入该固件的用户反馈，会影响副厂电池识别。
除了系统 / 固件移植，AI 逆向也让游戏移植焕发生机。
比如有开发者将任天堂游戏机独占的《超级马力欧兄弟：惊奇》原生移植到 Windows 电脑平台。
在未使用模拟器的情况下，RTX 3050 笔记本运行《超级马力欧兄弟：惊奇》的帧率达到约 60 帧，几乎可以完美运行，只是偶尔存在轻微的图形故障和帧率下降。
该项目使用重新编译的 C++ 代码和 NVN 到 Vulkan 的转换层，并计划进一步优化、集成 GPU 测试，开发者还计划开源当前的私有代码库，包括重编译器、NVN → Vulkan 层以及 NVN 文档。
IT之家注意到，这位开发者还晒出了多条视频，展示《蝙蝠侠：阿卡姆疯人院》（Xbox 360 版）原生移植到 Windows 平台、《超级马力欧：奥德赛》移植 Windows 平台（图形 Bug、没有声音）等，还有主机游戏移植到安卓手机的项目。
随着 AI 的发展，反编译和重编译项目正在打破主机独占的壁垒，不过移植相关的版权问题更值得关注，毕竟“东半球最强法务部”任天堂可不是吃素的。这位游戏移植开发者也很有求生欲，表示自己不会提供任何游戏文件。
除此之外，还有安卓平板移植 Linux 系统、一句话让 AI 替换电视桌面等，种种案例似乎都在预示着 AI 大破解时代的到来。
手机厂商、相机厂商、游戏主机厂商们可能也要重新思考自己真正的护城河是什么，如果用户能够随意跳到竞争对手的生态圈，那么自己又该如何留下用户、甚至挖掘到对手的用户。

title: 我国风光累计装机容量突破 20 亿千瓦
content:
IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，国家能源局今日宣布，今年 1-9 月，风电和太阳能发电新增装机容量约 1.7 亿千瓦，截至 2026 年 9 月底，风电和太阳能发电累计装机容量达到 20.1 亿千瓦。
IT之家从国家能源局发布的数据获悉，太阳能发电装机容量 13.1 亿千瓦，同比增长 16.5%；风电装机容量 7.0 亿千瓦，同比增长 20.4%。国家能源局还提到，新能源快速发展，在能源领域发挥了不可取代的作用：
- 一是成为推进能源转型的主要力量。今年 1-9 月，风光发电量 19333 亿千瓦时，比去年同期增加 1937 亿千瓦时，风光发电增量占全社会新增用电量的 64%，新能源大规模替代传统化石能源的减碳效益持续释放。
- 二是成为保障能源安全的关键支撑。新能源跨越式发展有效提升了能源本质安全水平，助力我国从容应对全球能源危机，今年迎峰度夏最大负荷日，当日午间风光最大出力占到当时总负荷的比重超 40%，保障午间高峰供电基本可靠。
- 三是成为拉动能源投资的重要引擎。从大基地到分布式，从陆上到海上，新能源产业链条长、带动范围广、技术密集度高，始终是能源领域投资的关键发力点，今年 1-9 月，全国风电和太阳能发电完成投资额约占能源领域完成投资额的三分之一。

title: 星闪 3.0 无源 SLZ 亮相：无需电池与电容、传感覆盖 30 米，已落地电网等能源场景
content:
IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，据国际星闪联盟官方昨晚分享，其主办的 2026 国际星闪联盟产业峰会暨星闪生态创新展已于 24 日圆满落幕，有 30 余家产业生态伙伴联袂参展、数百件展品集中亮相。
活动上，星闪 3.0 无源 SLZ 登场亮相，展示了“无源”物联的极致性能。其采用纵激元通过标签纯无源设计、无需电池与电容，依靠微波供能与回波解析温度信息，系统响应时间小于 1 毫秒、实时采集时延仅 0.3～0.4 毫秒，较传统 RFID 约 100 毫秒的系统响应快约 100 倍。
值得一提的是，星闪 3.0 无源 SLZ 传感覆盖 30 米，多标签同步温度传感精度达 ±0.1℃，极速可达 3000PCS / 秒抗金属与工业干扰，已落地电网、发电机等能源场景。
据IT之家了解，无源 SLZ（无源射频）是星闪 3.0 将新增的第四种空口模式，有望对标整个 RFID 技术（RFID 全称是 Radio Frequency Identification，意为射频识别，是通过无线电波实现读写器与电子标签数据通信的非接触式自动识别技术，可精准识别目标，常应用于汽车防盗、门禁管理等领域）。
星闪目前的三种空口模式分别为：
同步宽带 SLB：主要用于承载以车载主动降噪、无线投屏、工业机械运动控制等为代表的业务场景，采用快速群组定位技术，测距精度 < 30cm；
同步窄带 SLE：主要用于承载包括耳机音频传输、无线电池管理系统、工业数据采集在内的具备低功耗要求的业务场景，已用于星闪数字车钥匙和手机端星闪查找等应用；
同步高精定位 SLP：采用 UWB 信号实现厘米级高精定位，测距精度为 +/-10cm，测角精度为 +/-5°，已用于星闪指向遥控器应用。

title: 美国 NHTSA 监管压力下，特斯拉仍推进 Cybercab 无人驾驶出租车交付
content:
IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，据汽车媒体 CarBuzz 今天报道，特斯拉正为 Cybercab 无人驾驶出租车大规模交付做准备，该公司已在得州奥斯汀启动了小规模部署。不过美国国家公路交通安全管理局（NHTSA）已经盯上了特斯拉，重点审查这辆没有方向盘和踏板的车辆是如何获得认证的。
IT之家从原报道获悉，特斯拉截至目前并未彻底解决这一法律问题。特斯拉车辆工程副总裁拉尔斯 · 莫拉维曾强调，特斯拉致力于尽快大规模推出无人驾驶出租车，努力在今年年底前将 Cybercab 交付给客户。从这名高管的言论看，特斯拉似乎有信心应对监管难题。
特斯拉 AI 负责人埃隆 · 阿肖克则认为，公司必须克服监管方面限制。只要立法机构认可相关安排，扩大产能就不会成为问题。
事实上，NHTSA 已提出修改相关法规的建议，为没有方向盘、加速刹车踏板的全自动驾驶汽车提供合法空间。不过在立法真空期内，Cybercab 究竟如何满足监管要求目前仍不明确。NHTSA 设定的 10 月 30 日期限即将到来，未来几天内我们将听到更多消息。

title: 转一圈只要 1.63 秒，已知自转最快的近地小行星被确认
content:
IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，中国科学院云南天文台团队联合国内外合作者，在超快自转近地小行星观测研究方面取得突破性进展，确认已知自转最快的近地小行星。相关研究结果已发表在国际天文期刊《天文学杂志》。
近地小行星指近日点距离小于 1.3 AU 的小行星，其中直径大于 140 米、与地球最小轨道交会距离小于 0.05 AU 的近地小行星被定义为潜在危险小行星。
近地小行星撞击造成的破坏力越来越引起人们的关注与重视，因此，对近地小行星的监测预警和防御关乎全人类的共同安全。
北京时间 2024 年 12 月 4 日凌晨，近地小行星 2024 XA1 从西伯利亚东部上空坠入地球大气层，从被发现到坠落全程仅约 10 小时，这是人类第 11 次成功预报近地小行星撞击地球。
为了高效获取 2024 XA1 的亮度信息，云南天文台团队利用丽江 2.4 米望远镜采用“守株待兔”观测方式，在 2024 XA1 进入大气层前最后 1 小时的宝贵窗口期成功监测到其坠落前图像。
研究结果表明，近地小行星 2024 XA1 的自转周期仅 1.63 秒，低于近地小行星 2024 BX1 的 2.58 秒，为目前已知自转速度最快的近地小行星。
如此极端高速自转条件下，天体表面离心加速度远大于自身引力，证明它不是依靠引力束缚的碎石堆结构，必须依靠岩石材料自身机械强度维系整体完整，属于强度主导的固态独体，可能来自大天体碰撞碎裂等原因而形成。
该研究工作不仅确认了已知自转最快的近地小行星 2024 XA1，也为研究米级、快速自转和快速移动近地小行星的内部物质结构提供了机会，同时提升了对短临预警小行星物理特性的获取能力。

Die internationale Vortragsreihe "Winter Talks" des Fachbereichs Architektur der Hochschule Bochum lädt in diesem Semester dazu ein, Ordnung und Mehrdeutigkeit in der Architektur neu zu betrachten.
Ordnung und Mehrdeutigkeit lassen sich als komplementäre Bedingungen begreifen, die es der Architektur ermöglichen, zugleich lesbar und offen zu bleiben. Im Zentrum der Vortragsreihe steht die Frage, wie architektonische Ordnung durch Struktur, Geometrie und Bewegung, Lesbarkeit und Stabilität erzeugen kann – und zugleich wie Mehrdeutigkeit durch komplexe Gestaltung Räume für verschiedene Nutzungen und Interpretationen öffnet. Die diesjährige Vortragsreihe versteht Architektur als einen Zustand, in dem eine geordnete Struktur Raum für Ungewissheit, Wandel und Pluralität bietet.
Die Veranstaltungen finden in englischer Sprache statt.

Blue Box Auditorium, Am Hochschulcampus 1, D-44801 Bochum
Kuratiert von @professurkinzelbach, ENBK Entwerfen und Baukonstruktion

05.11.2026: OFFICE Kersten Geers David Van Severen, Brüssel
David Van Severen: Massstab und Perspektive
OFFICE ist ein in Brüssel ansässiges Architekturbüro, das 2002 von Kersten Geers und David Van Severen gegründet wurde. Es dient als Plattform, um Architektur im Kontext der zeitgenössischen Kultur und des urbanen Umfelds zu erforschen und entwickeln. Die Projekte, unterschiedlich in Maßstab und Typologie, sind zugleich pragmatisch und innovativ; sie sind tief in verschiedenen architektonischen Traditionen verwurzelt und schaffen einen Rahmen, in dem sich das Leben in all seiner Komplexität entfalten kann. Die internationale Tätigkeit des Büros, die unter anderem mit dem Silbernen Löwen und dem Aga Khan Award for Architecture gewürdigt wurde, geht einher mit Forschungsarbeit, Publikationen und Lehrtätigkeiten.
19.11.2026: MADE arhitekti, Riga
Miķelis Putrāms: Struktur und Flexibilität
Das Schaffen von Architektur ist ein komplexer Prozess, der sowohl Struktur als auch Flexibilität erfordert. Das Büro MADE arhitekti unter der Leitung der Partner Linda Krūmiņa und Miķelis Putrāms hat Projekte für private Bauherren sowie öffentliche Aufträge mit Präzision und Engagement umgesetzt. Gebäude bringen einen gestalterischen Ansatz zum Ausdruck – doch noch wichtiger ist, dass sie unser Verhalten prägen. Flexibilität wird somit zu einem wirkungsvollen Instrument, um sowohl das Gebäude selbst als auch den Prozess seiner Entstehung zu steuern.
26.11.2026: ADEPT, Copenhagen
Simon Lyager Poulsen: Was wir nicht wissen, dass wir es nicht wissen
Indem sie soziale und urbane Synergien fördern, zeichnen sich die Entwürfe von ADEPT als „anti-ikonische“ Typologien aus – konzipiert als Rahmen für das Leben, fest verankert im jeweiligen Kontext, am menschlichen Maßstab orientiert und auf einen verantwortungsvollen Umgang mit Ressourcen ausgerichtet. Anstatt für eine festgelegte Zukunft zu planen, nähert sich das Büro seinen Entwürfen über Szenarien und offene Fragestellungen; dabei werden architektonische Ideen mit der Fähigkeit zur Anpassung, Aneignung und Veränderung in Einklang gebracht. Auf diese Weise schafft das Büro Gebäude und Orte, die nicht nur das aufnehmen können, was wir bereits kennen, sondern auch das, was wir heute noch nicht vorhersehen können.

title: Neues HPC-System für Klimaforschung am DKRZ wird von BULL geliefert
content:
Neues HPC-System für Klimaforschung am DKRZ wird von BULL geliefert

ICON-Simulation in 5 km Auflösung vom EU-Projekt EERIE. Die Farben zeigen die Meeresoberflächentemperatur, die Schattierung die Strömungsgeschwindigkeit. Der HLRE-5 wird solche Simulationen im Kilometer-Maßstab mit höherer Energieeffizienz ermöglichen.
| Quelle:
Visualisierung: M. Böttinger
| Copyright:
Michael Böttinger, DKRZ
Download
Das Deutsche Klimarechenzentrum (DKRZ) hat Bull, einem führenden Anbieter für Advanced Computing und KI, einen Auftrag im Wert von 40 Millionen Euro für seinen nächsten Supercomputer erteilt. Der Auftrag umfasst neben dem HPC- und Speichersystem auch Supportleistungen über fünf Jahre. Das auf der BullSequana XH3500-Plattform basierende System ist darauf ausgelegt, sowohl physikalische Simulationen als auch KI-gestützte Klimaforschung zu ermöglichen und dabei die Energieeffizienz gegenüber dem Vorgängersystem deutlich zu verbessern.
Das Hochleistungsrechnersystem für Erdsystemforschung (HLRE-5) soll voraussichtlich Anfang 2028 für die Nutzerinnen und Nutzer zur Verfügung stehen und wird in der Lage sein, zwei globale Klimasimulationen mit einer Auflösung von 5 km gleichzeitig auszuführen. Dabei soll der Energiebedarf pro simuliertem Jahr gegenüber dem derzeitigen System Levante um rund 75 Prozent sinken.
Dieses Engagement für Energieeffizienz ist nicht neu, sondern baut auf jahrelangen kontinuierlichen gemeinsamen Anstrengungen von DKRZ und Bull auf. Die aktuelle GPU-Erweiterung des Levante-Systems erreichte in den Ausgaben der Green500-Liste vom November 2025 und Juni 2026 den dritten Platz unter den energieeffizientesten Supercomputern der Welt. Die ersten beiden Plätze gingen ebenfalls an Systeme von Bull.
„Mit dem neuen System können wir den Energiebedarf für die Klimasimulationen unserer Nutzerinnen und Nutzer drastisch reduzieren. Für ein Rechenzentrum, dessen Aufgabe die Unterstützung bei der Erforschung des Klimas ist, ist das kein zusätzlicher Vorteil – es ist Teil unseres Auftrags“, sagte Dr. Hendryk Bockelmann, Abteilungsleiter Anwendungen am DKRZ.
„Wir sind stolz darauf, unsere langjährige Zusammenarbeit mit dem DKRZ, einem der führenden Klimarechenzentren Europas, fortzusetzen. HLRE-5 baut auf jahrelanger gemeinsamer Innovationsarbeit im Bereich des energieeffizienten Supercomputings auf und zeigt, wie moderne digitale Infrastruktur exzellente Klimaforschung unterstützen kann“, ergänzte Dr. Martin Matzke, Head of Northern and Central Europe bei Bull.
HLRE-5 besteht aus zwei Partitionen: einer GPU-Partition, die auf Superchips des Typs NVIDIA GB200 Grace Blackwell basiert und den Großteil der Simulations- und KI-Leistung des Systems bereitstellt, sowie einer CPU-Partition auf Basis von NVIDIA Vera-CPUs. Diese bringt erstmals die ARM-Architektur in das Kernsystem des DKRZ und verbessert die Energieeffizienz für Rechenaufgaben, die nicht auf GPUs ausgeführt werden, erheblich. Alle Rechnerknoten sind über NVIDIA Quantum-2-InfiniBand vernetzt. Diese Netzwerktechnologie ermöglicht die Kommunikation zwischen den Knoten mit geringer Latenz und hoher Datenrate (400 GBit/s), auf die globale Klimamodelle mit einer Auflösung im Kilometerbereich angewiesen sind.
„Wir sind NVIDIA für die langjährige Unterstützung bei der Optimierung von ICON für GPUs dankbar, die auch dazu beigetragen hat, dass wir 2025 den ACM Gordon Bell Prize for Climate Modelling gewonnen haben. Wir freuen uns darauf, diese Zusammenarbeit auf HLRE-5 fortzusetzen“, betonte Dr. Jan Frederik Engels, Mitglied des Gordon-Bell-Teams und Systemdesigner für den HPC-Teil des HLRE-5.
Beim Datenspeicher geht eine neue Strategie über die Kapazität als primären Maßstab für die Dimensionierung hinaus und konzentriert sich stattdessen auf die effiziente Nutzung von Ressourcen durch intelligente Datenplatzierung und die Verteilung auf unterschiedliche Speicherhierarchien. Im Mittelpunkt steht die neue IBM Storage-Scale-System-6000, das 60 Petabytes Festplattenspeicher mit einem Datendurchsatz von bis zu 340 Gigabytes/s mit einem dedizierten Flash-Speicher mit 500 Terabytes kombiniert. In enger Zusammenarbeit mit IBM können fortschrittliche Funktionen zur bedarfsgesteuerten Verteilung der Daten auf die Speicherhierarchien sowie die Nutzung der Speicherressourcen für unterschiedliche Forschungsaufgaben analysiert und weiter optimiert werden.
Der Flash-Speicher adressiert die rasant wachsenden Anforderungen der KI und ist dafür konzipiert, die für anspruchsvolle KI-Anwendungen erforderliche Leistung bereitzustellen. Zusammen mit der Größe und Effizienz der kapazitätsorientierten Speicherhierarchien bietet sie der Forschungsgemeinschaft eine leistungsstarke Grundlage sowohl für HPC als auch für die nächste Generation KI-gestützter Forschung.
Wie bei den Vorgängergenerationen setzt das DKRZ zur Kühlung des Systems auf die patentierte Direct-Liquid-Cooling-Technologien (DLC) von Bull. Dabei fließt warmes Wasser in einem geschlossenen Kreislauf durch die Rechnerknoten und führt die Wärme wesentlich effizienter ab als eine Luftkühlung.
Seit mehreren Jahren liefert das DKRZ einen Teil dieser Wärme an den benachbarten Fachbereich Chemie der Universität Hamburg. Mit der Installation von HLRE-5 wird die Kühlinfrastruktur modernisiert, sodass ein größerer Anteil der Abwärme zur weiteren Nutzung zur Verfügung steht. Die Universität Hamburg plant, diese Nutzung auf weitere Gebäude auf und rund um den KlimaCampus auszuweiten.
Die Gesamtinvestition in das System beträgt 40 Millionen Euro und umfasst einen fünfjährigen Supportvertrag. Die Finanzierung erfolgt hauptsächlich durch die Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft, die Max-Planck-Gesellschaft und die Stadt Hamburg im Rahmen der langfristigen Finanzierungsvereinbarung für die HPC-Systeme am DKRZ. Dank zusätzlicher Mittel der Max-Planck-Gesellschaft und des Bundesministeriums für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt im Rahmen der Hightech Agenda Deutschland (HTAD) konnte das System nochmals deutlich vergrößert werden.

title: Rennen mit der Roten Königin: Mit Spieltheorie zu mehr Softwaresicherheit im KI-Zeitalter
content:
Rennen mit der Roten Königin: Mit Spieltheorie zu mehr Softwaresicherheit im KI-Zeitalter
