title: 国产AI 3D大模型Hi3D来了！开源可商用，PK干掉GPT-6
content:
国产AI 3D大模型Hi3D来了！开源可商用，PK干掉GPT-6
还是专业的模型做专业的事情
听雨 发自 凹非寺量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI
3D生成，效果上看，确实还是专业的模型做专业的事情。
给模型一张漫威帅哥（别管是谁），这是原图：
这是GPT-6 Astra交的作业：
不是我说，这哪来的山顶洞人啊……
而这，是Hi3D V3.0生成的结果：
还有其他几组测试：
从左到右依次为：原图、GPT-6 Astra模型生成、Hi3D Agent模型生成。
Astra，怎么就你最丑啊！
可以看出，Astra搭出了可识别的基本形体，但Hi3D Agent及其V3.0模型生成的结果，在轮廓、体积关系和局部细节上都更接近参考图。
Hi3D Agent，是Hi3D面向3D创作者推出的AI助手；其背后的最新模型Hi3D V3.0，则是业界首个可商用2048³超高精度国产自研AI 3D模型。
这也体现了两类模型的分工：大语言模型负责理解创作意图、组织任务，专业3D模型负责生成三维结果。两者结合，才能让Agent把用户的要求落实到具体的3D作品上。
今天，Hi3D还正式开放V1.0模型代码。这是基于Sparc3D构建的高分辨率几何细化模型，也是Hi3D模型系列中较早完成、经过生产工作流验证的版本。
据团队介绍，V1.0基于约200万个经过筛选的3D资产进行训练，并在开放前接受了团队的生产工作流验证。
团队还希望把这一稳定、经过生产验证的版本，作为开发者和企业可以继续研究、部署和开发的基础。
- GitHub链接：https://github.com/hi3d-official/Hi3Dv1.0
- Hugging Face space链接：https://huggingface.co/spaces/ilcve21/Sparc3D（用户可免费体验Hi3D V1.0）
- Hugging Face代码权重链接：https://huggingface.co/hi3d-official/Hi3Dv1.0
- 官方开源项目页：https://www.hi3d.ai/hi3d-1-0-open-source（可下载代码，免费使用等）
生成、修改、应用，Hi3D接管创作流程
今天开源的Hi3D V1.0，技术源头可以追溯到2025年公开的Sparc3D
这项工作发表于NeurIPS 2025，提出了一套高分辨率三维建模框架，着重解决复杂几何结构的表示与重建问题，让细小部件和表面细节得到更充分的保留。
它的生成效果be like：
【此处无法插入视频，遗憾……可到量子位公众号查看～】
还是蛮惊艳的，可以明显看出Sparc3D对复杂几何细节的处理能力。
Hi3D V1.0沿用了这套核心架构，并将训练数据规模扩展至约200万个经过筛选的3D资产，进一步增强高分辨率几何生成能力。
我们来具体看看V1.0的创作效果：
V1.0技术报告中展示的装甲车，体现了模型对三维对象的完整生成能力
正面能看清车头倾斜的装甲面和轮胎花纹；转到背面和底部，车身结构依然连贯，车尾面板的分块、底盘与车轮的位置关系也能辨认。
对于参考图没有展示的区域，模型则进行了合理补全。
再来看看更复杂细小的结构。比如这个身穿铠甲、手拿大剑、背后展开双翼的雕塑：
经V1.0放大后，人物背后的羽翼是根根分明的，甚至还能看清羽毛相互叠压形成的层次。
从车身的整体结构，到羽片之间的细小间隔，这两组案例呈现了V1.0在不同尺度上的几何表现。
而模型生成之后，创作者也可以在Hi3D Agent中继续修改。
Hi3D Agent，是以Hi3D专业AI 3D模型为底座，将意图理解、任务规划、模型生成、持续修改、工程优化与应用交付连接起来的3D创作Agent。
比如，用户指出部件悬空和连接位置的问题，要求调整方向盘，并明确说明：接下来想把模型打印出来。
Agent按照这些要求列出了后续处理步骤，并围绕已有模型继续调整造型、局部结构、几何、纹理和网格，使结果更接近创作目标。
游戏与互动类内容中，Agent可以继续补充角色、道具和场景，将生成资产带入交互环境，推进到可玩的Demo。
【此处无法插入视频，遗憾……可到量子位公众号查看～】
针对动画与实时应用，Hi3D Agent则能对角色进行轻量化、骨骼绑定、动作和表情处理，使静态模型能够进入动画或实时内容流程。
【此处无法插入视频，遗憾……可到量子位公众号查看～】
实体创作中，Hi3D Agent衔接了Hi3D平台的拆件、连接结构、配色和打印准备能力，将数字模型继续转化为手办、潮玩等实体作品。
【此处无法插入视频，遗憾……可到量子位公众号查看～】
同时，生成结果也可以下载，并进入Blender、游戏引擎或其他专业软件继续加工。
从模型生成到修改完善，再到后续应用，Hi3D能够支持创作者完成不同阶段的工作，将想法逐步转化为可用的作品。
此次开源的V1.0，团队如何提升模型的结构完整性与细节表现，技术报告还给出了更具体的训练和评测信息。
扩充训练数据、细化几何，Hi3D V1.0的技术升级
Hi3D V1.0沿用Sparc3D架构，重点完善数据规模与高分辨率能力。
这一版本保留了原有的核心架构，主要工作集中在训练数据扩容高分辨率训练与输出，以及生产流程验证
首先是训练数据的扩容。相较于Sparc3D论文中50万个资产的训练设置，Hi3D V1.0将训练规模扩大到了约200万个经过筛选的3D资产，达到原来的4倍
这与单图生成3D的任务特点有关。单张参考图只能提供物体的部分信息，未展示的背面和遮挡区域，还需要模型根据学到的形状规律进行合理补全。
更丰富的训练资产，能够让模型接触更多类型的物体与结构，为这些推断提供更充分的学习样本。
那么，有了训练数据，模型又是如何逐步刻画细节的？
结合报告中的架构图，可以把这一过程理解为：先确定大体结构，再结合参考图逐级细化。
上游模型先根据图片生成一个粗网格，提供物体的整体轮廓和主要部件。随后，V1.0同时参考图片与粗网格，围绕物体表面进行稀疏几何细化。
每完成一个层级，系统都会提取出三维网格。这个结果既可以直接输出，也可以作为下一轮细化的基础，逐步进入1024³和1536³层级。
1536³，指的是几何提取网格的分辨率。可以把它理解为描述物体形状时所用的空间刻度：刻度越细，就越有条件表达细小的起伏和间隔。系统采用稀疏方式，主要处理表面附近的有效区域。
上文所展示的羽毛案例，之所以能做到根根分明，背后正是这种分辨率的体现。
目前，最新的Hi3D V3.0已将几何分辨率提升至
分辨率之外，还有几何细节与下游使用表现。
根据其技术报告，Hi3D V1.0的多视图保真度细节丰富度分别达到0.75和0.841，在报告所列对比方法中均排名第一
同时，其切片成功率达到90%，展现了进入后续3D打印准备流程的可用性。
△出自V1.0技术报告
切片是把三维模型转换为打印机逐层执行指令的准备环节。这项结果反映了生成网格进入打印准备流程的表现，实际能否顺利打印，还与壁厚、支撑和材料等条件有关。
据团队介绍，V1.0在开放前已经进入面向用户的真实生产工作流接受测试与使用。除了观察生成效果，团队也在实际创作任务中检验这些资产能否继续处理、进入后续应用。
开放模型与工具接口，让开发者和企业构建3D应用
本次开放的Hi3D V1.0，已在GitHub和Hugging Face正式上线。
官方已公开系统架构与效果对比，并开放源码；项目页面还有在线Demo可体验相关生成能力。
这套模型主要面向研究者、开发者和企业
研究者可以将其作为技术验证和模型研究的基础，探索复杂结构生成与细节保留；
开发者可以把几何细化能力接入专业工具，构建垂直应用和自己的工作流；
企业则可以结合正式发布的授权与部署条件，探索私有化部署、内部系统集成和业务适配。
开放模型之外，Hi3D还可通过MCP连接外部应用
开发者可以在支持MCP的Agent或工具中调用Hi3D，完成提交生成任务、查询进度和获取模型结果等操作，再将这些步骤接入自己的业务流程。
Hi3D Agent则直接服务创作者。用户可以通过自然语言描述需求，并围绕生成结果继续提出修改要求，让Agent协助推进创作。
三者各有分工：开放模型为自主开发提供基础，MCP让外部应用调用平台能力，Agent帮助用户直接完成创作。
这也对应着Hi3D作为AI 3D基础设施的定位：为模型开发、应用集成和实际创作提供支持。
这些工作也共同指向Hi3D提出的「Creator First」方向：
帮助新手更容易进入3D创作，减少专业创作者的重复操作，把更多时间留给设计与修改。
随着国产AI 3D技术不断成熟，想象与作品之间的距离，也在一点点缩短。普通人从一张图片、一个想法出发，也能做出属于自己的3D作品。

title: 小米披露灵巧手最新技术探索成果：基于1827个工厂SOP验证，升级21自由度仿生灵巧手
content:
< img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400">
10月27日，小米技术披露仿生灵巧手技术探索成果：以小米汽车工厂柔性制造场景为设计原点，带来高自由度仿生灵巧手的最新技术思考。
小米方面表示，小米机器人团队基于汽车工厂1827个标准作业程序（SOP）进行完整数据采集与分析验证，基于真实作业数据的仿真消融分析显示，在17~21自由度区间，仿生灵巧手平均稳定抓握成功率较6~15自由度提升15%~38%，其中 21 自由度在工厂操作覆盖度和抓握成功率上提升最大。在该场景下，继续提升自由度至 23 度及以上时，抓握能力提升明显放缓，堆自由度的边际收益下降。
基于上述结论，小米设计了全新21自由度仿生灵巧手，该灵巧手采用混合驱动与腱绳张力控制方案，实现精准抓握力控、提升可靠性与可维护性，同时对散热体系和全掌触觉进行了系统性优化。
中央财经大学数字经济经济融合创新发展中心主任、中国人工智能学会智能产品与产业工作委员会副主任陈端指出，小米此次以工厂真实作业场景为设计原点，“场景定义产品”的研发范式，是比硬件参数更稳固的护城河。“车间里采集的触觉、力位、装配时序数据属于稀缺的场景化资产，既用来训练灵巧手本体的操作策略，也能够持续反哺整个小米AI体系，提升跨场景迁移能力。”

title: 钛动科技发布行业首个Pro-Agent, Navos Pro定义结果导向的AI for Work | TGC 2026科技增长大会
content:
钛动科技发布行业首个Pro-Agent, Navos Pro定义结果导向的AI for Work | TGC 2026科技增长大会
10 月 23 日，以 “ AI is Profitable ” 为主题的 2026 TGC 科技增长大会于广州召开。
10 月 23 日，以 “ AI is Profitable ” 为主题的 2026 TGC 科技增长大会于广州召开。
面向AI for Work数万亿美元级蓝海市场，全球领先的AI营销科技公司钛动科技，在会上正式发布行业首个 Pro Agent ——Navos Pro。Navos Pro以 Professional、Proactive、Profitable 三大核心属性构建产品内核，让结果导向（Result-Driven）的 AI for Work成为现实，持续推动 AI 成为企业全球增长与生产力变革的核心引擎。
【Kevin Knight博士开场演讲】
本次大会由国际AI泰斗 Kevin Knight 博士领衔开场演讲，发言嘉宾汇聚 OpenAI、Google、阿里、字节、腾讯等全球 AI 科技公司，凝聚一个核心共识：“科技创造增长”产业新周期开启，AI 商业价值必须由真实业务指标验证。
Kevin Knight博士在《From Language to Action: The Next Leap in AI》开场演讲中，结合学术与产业双重视角给出判断：AI for Work 将成为 AI 应用最重要的方向之一。
【钛动科技创始人兼CEO李述昊主题演讲】
紧接着，钛动科技创始人兼 CEO 李述昊在其主题分享中，首先将 AI 商业机会落在企业长期、持续投入的营销和销售、编程和产品开发、管理三笔费用上，对应提出 AI for Growth、AI for Innovation与AI for Administration，三者预计构成AI for Work数万亿美元的广阔市场。在这一AI for Work三费框架中，Claude Code等AI产品主攻AI for Innovation，WorkBuddy等AI产品专注协同办公；而钛动科技的Navos Pro则将是AI for Growth的顶尖玩家。
李述昊进一步明确：“只做结果导向的 AI for Work ”。作为下一代 Agent，Navos Pro 具备Professional、Proactive、Profitable 三大能力体系，面向跨境电商、外贸、营销、商业分析等场景推进智能体落地：
1. Professional｜专业理解业务：输入品牌官网即可解析关键信息，搭建私有化品牌知识库；沉淀业务记忆，输出贴合品牌商业诉求的内容，解决通用 AI 不懂品牌生意的痛点。
2. Proactive｜主动发现机会：摆脱被动指令模式，7×24 小时监测多维度数据，主动挖掘增长机会、生成策略；AI 输出建议，人掌握决策权。
3. Profitable｜实现商业增长：以盈利为核心标尺，策略、创意、投放锚定 GMV、ROI 等指标，摒弃无效 AI 产出，保障效果可衡量、可盈利。
【Pro Agent Navos正式发布】
Professional、Proactive、Profitable 三大 Pro 体系背后，有着三层能力供给：
Professional 能力体系融合行业 Know-How 与专属数据，形成数据库、Agent、工作流、互动四大能力：以公域数据、领域Benchmark和垂直场景提供趋势、竞品、选品、素材与投放洞察；以 70+ MCP、100+ Skill 和用户反馈持续调优；以Skill、Template、数字员工，把选品、素材创作、广告诊断等流程标准化、自动化；以意图识别、结果反馈和过程可溯源保障互动。
Proactive 能力体系覆盖日均 10 亿+感知数据、2 亿+感知频次，支持千万+广告诊断、百万+行动建议和 10 万+建议采纳，围绕账户、商品、素材主动监测，输出预算、出价、卖点和素材迭代建议，并联动 Agent 或人工执行。
Profitable 能力体系以“批量创编、规模测试—规模生产、去伪存真—策略迭代、放大收益”推进，通过 Learning Loop 形成结果反馈、策略优化、持续进化闭环。技术底座上，Navos RSI以Agentic RL 驱动 Agent Harness 自迭代，覆盖轨迹采样、奖励设计、策略更新、版本写回与验证。
三层架构由 Agent Harness、32B/27B/5B 专业模型及营销知识库、Benchmark 指标库、方法论资产、多源异构数据和专业样本库构成，支撑多国家、多渠道、多行业、多场景复制。依托上述三大 Pro 体系，Navos 已完整覆盖出海营销链路，同时设置 Navos Lite 和 Navos Pro 双版本矩阵。
【Pro Agent Navos技术架构】
李述昊表示，Agent 演进的本质是工作发起权的转移：Chatbot 阶段，AI 被动应答；Copilot 阶段，AI 辅助执行；到了 Pro-Agent 阶段，AI 开始主动发现业务机会并交付真实增长，Navos Pro 将是这一阶段的代表。
他进一步复盘 Agent 演进故事线之上、更宏观的产业迭代逻辑：2012 年移动互联网时代开启 To C 流量为王的万亿级市场；2018 年 SaaS 时代开启以 To B 为主的万亿级市场；自 2024 年开启的 AI 时代，核心逻辑正从“能力供给”走向“价值验证”。
而钛动科技已通过服务数十万出海品牌的营销实践，率先完成这一“价值验证”，并开启生态布局：2026 年 7 月成为 ChatGPT Ads 全球首批技术合作伙伴，助力品牌 ROI 提升至 2.5 倍；8 月与腾讯 WorkBuddy 达成合作，将模型能力落地海外营销投放场景。
李述昊指出，AI for Growth，只是钛动科技验证 AI 重塑企业生产力的第一步，未来，钛动科技将继续把自身 AI 能力迁移至 AI for Innovation 与 AI for Administration，从而推动企业 AI 生产力的系统性重塑。
OpenAI 商业合作负责人 Lorry Destainville 分享 ChatGPT 商业化前瞻：ChatGPT 每周触达 12 亿用户，OpenAI 正在同步探索 Sponsored Agents和 Visual Ads，特别感谢钛动科技与其联手为品牌主提供可落地、可衡量的AI增长工具。
【大会主持人、钛动科技品牌公关 VP 张羽雪】
随后，由钛动科技品牌公关 VP 张羽雪主持，三场圆桌论坛重磅登场。美国泛大西洋资本周洁、Nextie 创始人李笛、深言序创始人叶军、阿里巴巴千问徐栋同台对话“新兴 AI 技术如何重塑商业未来”；谷歌刘步驰、中金公司赵丽萍、麦芽传媒翁成波、英雄电竞 Josh Ye 共议“ AI 时代的出海大趋势”；BytePlus Terry Wang、阿里巴巴千问邓兆俊、腾讯 WorkBuddy 杨彤对话“ AI 应用商业化的生态实践”。
【钛动科技创始合伙人聂艾玲介绍钛动科技投资版图】
大会最后，钛动科技创始合伙人、生态孵化和战略投资负责人聂艾玲，宣布启动 Pro-Agent Global Challenge 全球挑战赛，面向全球 AI 创业者征集 AI 前沿项目。大赛聚焦 Agent 架构演进、AI 营销、AI 内容入口与算力基础设施等赛道，并将开放资本、产业资源及全球增长通道为项目赋能。
至此，TGC 2026 拼齐了科技创造增长的全景图。AI is Profitable 正在加速兑现，AI for Work 万亿蓝海才刚刚起航。

title: First BC Wind monopiles arrive at Świnoujście
content:
The first monopiles for the 390 MW BC Wind offshore wind farm have officially
arrived at the port of Świnoujście, marking the start of logistical operations
ahead of the project's installation phase.
Once completed, the offshore wind farm will consist of 26 bottom fixed
wind turbines, each with a capacity of 14 MW, generating enough renewable
energy to power approximately 488,000 Polish homes and businesses.
According to the announcement, the milestone reinforces the potential of
Poland's port infrastructure, marking the first time foundations of this
scale have been accepted at a Polish installation port.
Pete Geddes, BC Wind project director, said: "The acceptance of the
first monopiles at a Polish port is an important milestone in the BC Wind
project and another step in the development of the domestic offshore wind
energy sector."
"We are pleased to be able to involve Polish companies in these activities,
creating an opportunity to gain practical experience and develop the skills
of local teams, while supporting the development of the domestic supply
Local companies will support the next stage of operations, including Dynap,
which will be responsible for a range of monopile and transition piece
related tasks. Team Project from Modrzewie will assist in the terminal's
adaptation, ensuring the ground is prepared for unloading foundation structures,
along with carrying out additional works as required.

GS Entec have completed monopile manufacturing facilities in South Korea
GS Entec has announced that its monopile manufacturing facilities at Yongjam
Works in Ulsan, South Korea, have been officially completed.
The facilities have been upgraded and automated, increasing the company's
annual production capacity from 40,000 tons to 150,000 tons.
According to the announcement, the upgrade will strengthen GS Entec's competitive
position within the offshore wind industry, not only through increased
production capacity but also through its ability to manufacture large-scale
monopiles for turbines of 15 MW and above.
GS Entec also reaffirmed its partnership with foundation design and manufacturing
company Sif, further strengthening its expertise and manufacturing capabilities.

title: RWE’s SeaMe project completes initial offshore testing
content:
RWE has announced that the SeaMe project (Sustainable Ecosystem Approach
in Monitoring the marine Environment) has officially completed its initial
offshore testing phase after two years.
The project tested a range of innovative technologies in real world conditions,
including drones, AI-assisted camera systems and autonomous underwater
vehicles.
Testing was carried out at RWE’s Kaskasi
offshore wind farm.
The aim of the project is to support environmental monitoring, construction
and operation of offshore wind farms, helping to make the process more
efficient and sustainable.
Tobias Keitel, CEO of RWE Offshore Wind, said: “As one of the world’s
leading companies in offshore wind, we aim to build and operate wind farms
in harmony with nature.”
Adding: “SeaMe demonstrates that innovative technologies can help us gain
an even better understanding of the interactions between offshore wind
energy and marine ecosystems.”
According to the announcement, the project will collect both biological
and physical environmental data. Combined with more frequent observations
and in-depth assessments of the marine environment, this information will
help track the development of marine ecosystems.
RWE said the data will be collected using minimally invasive, low-emission
methods, ensuring that monitoring activities remain both efficient and
environmentally friendly.

title: The UK and Taiwan launch new CCUS partnership
content:

(CCUS) partnership during the eighth UK Taiwan Energy Dialogue in Taipei.

5 GW of installed offshore wind capacity.

local supply chains, improved financing and preparations for floating wind
demonstration projects.

title: AM Green mega- project secures investment from Asian Development Bank
content:
AM Green mega- project secures investment from Asian Development Bank
ADB and Japanese government invest in 1.1 million tons of renewable ammonia production per year
India-based AM Green Ammonia has secured a loan of $100 million for converting the power source of an existing ammonia and urea plant from conventional gas to renewable energy. The decarbonised plant at Kakinada on India’s southeast coast is forecast to produce a capacity of 1.1 million tons of renewable ammonia per year, opening up a new export commodity opportunity for India as well as decreasing the carbon dioxide emissions of the fertiliser and chemical industries.
The loan is the first allocated under the Action for Creating Energy Security for Long-term Resilience (ACCEL) initiative administered by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and financed by the Japanese government and development collaborators.
Ammonia is used every day to produce the fertilizer that helps feed the world. This project changes how we make it. By using renewable energy instead of fossil fuels, India can produce it with far lower emissions and at a scale that can help reshape this industry. As the first investment under ACCEL, it also shows how ADB and Japan can turn energy security into practical investments in new markets and jobs.
Masato Kanda, President at ADB in his organisation’s press release, 15 Oct, 2026
Strengthening resilience of Asia’s energy supply chains is essential. Japan is advancing POWERR Asia, including through ACCEL, and I welcome the first joint project under ACCEL. Working closely with ADB, Japan will continue to support the diversification of energy sources, which will strengthen economic resilience across Asia.
Satsuki Katayama, Japan’s Finance Minister in ADB’s press release, 15 Oct, 2026
AM Green is developing a portfolio of renewable ammonia plants in India across Kakinada, Tuticorin and Kandla with a targeted total production capacity of 4 million tons per year of renewable ammonia. The first plant of this portfolio (AMGA-K1, 1 million tons per year capacity) is under construction in Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, and achieved the critical milestone of Final Investment Decision (FID) in 2024. This project was featured by the AEA in a webinar in March this year.
More recently, AM Green secured offtake for Phase 2 production from the Kakinada project by successfully bidding to supply the Asia lot of renewable ammonia in H2Global’s latest auction round. The cost of this long-term purchase agreement is a minimum €585 million over 10 years.
The ADB is a collaboration of members and partners (including Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) and Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC)) supporting sustainable, inclusive and resilient growth across Asia and the Pacific. Launched by the ABD in May 2026, ACEEL supports renewable projects to aid the transition towards diversified and sustainable energy systems in the long term.

title: Code of Practice for Ammonia Bunkering released for Singapore
content:
Code of Practice for Ammonia Bunkering released for Singapore
Maritime & Port Authority of Singapore prepares for bunkering operations
The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and Enterprise Singapore have launched a new “Singapore Standard” and two “Technical References” (TRs) today covering ammonia bunkering, bunker fuel sampling, and testing for polymers in residual based marine fuels. The trio of documents were released at the recent Singapore International Bunkering Conference and Exhibition 2026.
TR 148:2026 “Code of Practice for Ammonia Bunkering” (TR 148) sets out the requirements for the safe and efficient conduct of ammonia bunkering operations within the Port of Singapore. The Technical Reference includes details about custody transfer, bunkering procedures, safety & personnel competency, and “provides a common framework for bunker suppliers, bunker craft operators, shipowners and other industry stakeholders to plan and conduct ammonia bunkering operations”. To validate TR 148, MPA Singapore and Pilbara Ports Authority will work to share operational experiences (including an upcoming bunker trial at the Port of Port Hedland in northwest Australia), accumulate practical experience, and support the deployment of ammonia bunkering globally.
As shipping transitions towards a wider range of marine fuels, our bunkering standards and capabilities must evolve with it. These new standards will support the industry’s transition and strengthen Singapore’s ability to serve the bunkering needs of global shipping as new fuel pathways develop.
Ang Wee Keong, Chief Executive MPA, in his organisation’s official press release, 14 Oct 2026
Standards are an important enabler of maritime decarbonisation, providing a common foundation for new fuels and practices to be adopted safely and consistently. As the marine fuel landscape evolves, TR 148, SS 730 and TR 155 extend this assurance across bunkering operations, fuel sampling and quality testing, including for emerging fuels such as ammonia. Together, they support Singapore’s transition to a multi-fuel future and reinforce our position as a trusted global bunkering hub.
Choy Sauw Kook, Director-General (Quality & Excellence), Enterprise Singapore, in MPA’s official press release, 14 Oct 2026
The documents can be purchased from the Singapore Standards eShop.

title: Eastern Pacific Shipping receives its first ammonia dual-fuel vessel
content:
Eastern Pacific Shipping receives its first ammonia dual-fuel vessel
Very Large Ammonia Carrier Terra Clove delivered in South Korea
Singapore-based Eastern Pacific Shipping (EPS) has received delivery of the world’s first ammonia dual-fuel Very Large Ammonia Carrier (VLAC). Named Terra Clove, the VLAC was built by South Korea-based Hyundai Heavy Industries (HHI) and is powered by Everllence’s B&W 6G60ME-C10.5-LGIA two-stroke engine. The vessel can carry 93,000m³ of ammonia as cargo and can be propelled by ammonia or conventional marine fuel. The realisation of the Terra Clove was via collaboration between EPS, HHI, Everllence, Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS).
Upcoming practical trials involve ammonia fuel operations in the Terra Clove engine. Renewable ammonia fuel will be supplied by South Korea-based LOTTE Fine Chemicals (LOTTE), and produced by China-based Envision Energy.
EPS is committed to knowledge sharing in the maritime decarbonisation space. At the vessel launch, it announced a formal strategic partnership with Denmark-based Mærsk Mc-Kinney Møller Center for Zero Carbon Shipping. This is in addition to collaborating a white paper about the design, operational safety and training considerations for ammonia-fuelled VLACs, due to be published later this year. Additionally, EPS is a founding partner of the Global Centre for Maritime Decarbonisation (GCMD).
Three years ago, EPS and our partners set out to move ammonia propulsion from concept towards commercial reality. The delivery of Terra Clove is an important milestone in that journey and demonstrates what can be achieved through long-term collaboration across the maritime industry. At the heart of the vessel is the world’s first Everllence B&W G60ME-C10.5-LGIA engine, representing the first seagoing application of Everllence’s two-stroke ammonia engine technology. This is an important technological achievement, but preparing for ammonia-fuelled shipping requires more than the engine alone. It requires the right vessel design, safety systems, operating procedures, infrastructure and, most importantly, trained and capable seafarers. We thank HHI, Everllence, MPA, ABS and everyone involved in bringing Terra Clove to life. Together, we are building the experience and capabilities needed to support the safe and practical use of green ammonia as a marine fuel.
Cyril Ducau, CEO of EPS, in his organisation’s press release, 22 Oct 2026
The Everllence engine passed Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) in April this year, and was then installed aboard the Terra Clove. Also installed was a High Pressure Selective Catalytic Reduction (HP-SCR) exhaust aftertreatment system, designed to remove up to 95% of NOX formed during combustion.
The testing and installation of the engine signals that the wait-and-see period is coming to an end. For many shipowners, the successful installation and test of ammonia engines removes the psychological barrier. This shifts the market conversation on ammonia as a fuel from ‘Can we do it?’ to ‘When should we order?’
Donghwan Kim, Sales Promotion Manager at Everllence, quoted in The milestone that bridges innovation and reality

title: Energy China begins Phase II construction at Songyuan
content:
Energy China begins Phase II construction at Songyuan
600,000 tons of renewable ammonia per year total capacity in northeast China
Construction of Phase II of China Energy Engineering Group’s HyFlow Songyuan Hydrogen Energy Industrial Park commenced on October 20. Located in Jilin Province, northeast China, Phase II is predicted to cost RMB 10.83 billion (approximately $1.6 billion). The investment increases the renewable ammonia production from 200,000 to 600,000 tons per year. This increase is aided by the addition of 1,600 MW of renewable energy generating capacity.
A 10% improvement in production cost of renewable ammonia compared with Phase I is forecast, calculated from optimisations in equipment, system integration and platform management allowing improved matching of intermittent renewable energy supply to maintain stability in the ammonia production process.
Long-term offtake agreements have already been signed by Energy China and international customers. Maritime ammonia first-mover CMB.TECH signed an off-take agreement for renewable ammonia produced at the Songyuan project in December 2025, and this month renewable ammonia fuel from Songyuan was used to bunker the bulk carrier Mineral Europa, which is on its way to Australia to commence commercial operations. CMB.TECH will also acquire a minority stake in Jiangsu Andefu (ADF) one of China’s largest ammonia supply chain companies and China’s first exporter of liquid ammonia in 2011.
If Phase I demonstrated technical feasibility, taking the project from zero to one, Phase II will address the challenge of commercial scaling, taking it from one to N.
Li Jingguang, Chairman of China Energy Engineering Group Hydrogen Energy Co. in his organisation’s press release, 20 Oct 2026
This is a landmark achievement in developing new quality productive forces and building a modern energy system.
Ni Zhen, Chairman of China Energy Engineering Co. in his organisation’s press release, 20 Oct 2026
The Songyuan Hydrogen Park, including details about Phase II, was covered in an AEA Project Features webinar in October 2025.

title: Færder Tankers: the “Green Ammonia Fueled Fleet”
content:
Færder Tankers: the “Green Ammonia Fueled Fleet”
European Commission investments include three ammonia-centric projects
As part of the recent round of net-zero technology projects to receive funding (via “reinvestment” of revenues collected from from the EU Emissions Trading System), the European Commission has granted around €26 million each to three medium-scale ammonia projects. As well as Færder Tankers’ project, the Commission will support:
- Maersk Tankers’ Project RIPPLE, exploring the retrofit of the company’s new Very Large Ammonia Carrier vessels with dual-fuel engines in Denmark.
- And H2SITE’s Phantom project – a demonstration-scale ammonia-to-hydrogen cracking facility at the Port of Rotterdam able to produce 20 tons per day of high-purity hydrogen.
Mobile bunkering units: bringing the fuel to you
Færder Tankers’ Green Ammonia Fueled Fleet (GAFF) project plans to deploy the first European fleet of medium gas carriers equipped with a “tri-fueled” propulsion system, able to run on ammonia, LPG and heavy fuel oil. Currently being developed by Færder in Norway, the vessels will overcome bottlenecks by transporting ammonia fuel and providing ship-to-ship bunkering capabilities on key routes “between India, the US Gulf Coast and northwest Europe”. Færder aims for the fleet to transport up to one million tons of ammonia fuel per year, particularly renewable ammonia sourced from countries like India.
The 50,000 m3 “WorkHorse” midsized gas carrier is being developed by Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners and Færder in Norway, and will be able to utilize cargo as fuel. The design features a retractable bow thruster and aft thruster for increased manoeuvrability, maintaining the same physical dimensions as current midsize gas carriers. The first vessel is expected to be delivered in the second half of 2028, joining CIP’s future fleet of ammonia carriers.

content:
Maersk Tankers: EU funding for ammonia engine retrofit project
European Commission investments include three ammonia-centric projects
As part of the recent round of net-zero technology projects to receive funding (via “reinvestment” of revenues collected from from the EU Emissions Trading System), the European Commission has granted around €26 million each to three medium-scale ammonia projects. Project RIPPLE: converting newly-delivered VLACs to run on ammonia fuel
With a view to powering its new fleet of Very Large Ammonia Carriers (VLACs) with ammonia fuel, Maersk Tankers will embark on a project to retrofit this series of vessels with dual-fuel engines, subject to securing commercial commitments from customers. Via a new incorporated entity Ammonia Carriers A/S, the RIPPLE project will explore the retrofit of four of these VLACs in Denmark.
Our ambition to power our new fleet of Very Large Ammonia Carriers (VLACs) with ammonia has taken an important step forward. Our retrofit project, RIPPLE, has been selected for EU Innovation Fund funding, pending finalisation of the grant agreement. The project would equip vessels with dual-fuel engines, enabling them to use ammonia as marine fuel and reduce emissions from their operations. Moving ahead with the retrofits will depend on securing commercial commitments from customers. With ten VLACs joining our fleet, we see significant potential to support the adoption of ammonia as a marine fuel.

title: Ecobat break-up complete as Clarios acquires North American recycling business – Batteries International
content: Clarios is set to acquire Ecobat’s remaining lead recycling operations in the US, just weeks after Ecobat exited its lithium recycling business to “fully focus” on North American recycling activities. Clarios announced proposals on October 27 to acquire Ecobat’s three US critical mineral recovery and processing facilities, hinting at new investment in these sites and further potential expansion in the US. The looming sell-off of Ecobat’s North American business was exclusively revealed by Batteries International in October 2025. Now the sale to Clarios, financial details of which have not been disclosed, marks the final step in a portfolio transformation Ecobat started last year — under which the company has completed 10 divestitures spanning 17 sites across six countries in around 16 months, including the sale of its European operations. Ecobat president and CEO Tom Slabe said the deal “completes the strategic initiative we announced with the earlier sale of our European operations and delivers a strong outcome for Ecobat’s stakeholders”. The proposed acquisition will preserve and strengthen domestic critical mineral processing and recovery capacity at a time of growing demand for critical minerals and increasing focus on supply chain resilience, Clarios said. By integrating these facilities into its industry-leading circular supply network, Clarios said it will enhance its ability to recover, process and return valuable materials into the US manufacturing base. The proposed acquisition, conditionally expected to close by early calendar year 2027, includes Ecobat’s facilities in California, Indiana and Middletown, New York, as well as the Dallas office. Together, these facilities currently process more than 40 million batteries annually, recovering lead, tin, antimony and other materials. Clarios and Ecobat said they intend to work closely with employees, union representatives and regulators to focus on continuity of operations, environmental compliance, workforce stability and long-term investment in US critical mineral processing and recovery capacity. Clarios CEO Mark Wallace said: “As a world leader in critical minerals processing and recovery, Clarios is uniquely positioned to strengthen this highly capable US recycling operation supported by an experienced workforce. “We see a significant opportunity to build on Ecobat’s foundation by evaluating opportunities for future investment in these operations and supporting the continued success of the business.” The post Ecobat break-up complete as Clarios acquires North American recycling business appeared first on Batteries International .

title: The Tech Issue Making This Midterm Election Different
content:
Stationary Batteries
Along with the usual debates over funding for programs, transportation, and regulatory changes, this year's election cycle features a heated new flashpoint: whether AI data centers should be built — and where.
October 27, 2026
4 Min Read
Data centers have become a hotly-contested election issue in 2026, with citizens in many communities opposing their presence.
Nic Antaya / Stringer/ Getty Images News
With U.S. elections now less than a week away, candidates are making a final push for support in their costly campaigns. While local and state issues vary widely, one topic is drawing attention nationwide: whether, where, and how data centers should be built, and who will fund and power them.
The booming demand for AI infrastructure — driven in part by President Trump's
push to help the U.S. compete with China in artificial intelligence
— has created pent-up demand for new AI data centers across many states. But concerns over electricity usage, water consumption, and waste removal have led communities nationwide to push back against these projects. According to polls, attempts by data center operators to ease these concerns have largely been met with skepticism.
Gubernatorial races highlight the divide
Nowhere is the divide over data centers more apparent than in this year's gubernatorial races across several dozen states. A
MultiState
, a lobbying and government affairs organization, surveyed candidates in 36 gubernatorial races and found positions ranging from full support to conditional approval to temporary moratoriums.
Democratic candidates have generally favored moratoriums, while many Republican candidates have called for stricter regulation rather than outright bans. However, given politicians' often-shifting positions, some proposed measures have already drawn intense scrutiny from local advocacy groups.
New York: candidates take opposing stances
New York Governor Kathy Hochul, running for re-election against Republican Bruce Blakeman, was among the first to take a firm stance against data centers. In July, Hochul s
igned a one-year ban on large-scale AI data centers
. Business groups criticized the move as unilateral, arguing it could drive economic development away from the state — particularly in upstate regions already struggling with companies relocating elsewhere.
Blakeman has sharply criticized Hochul's approach, arguing
she should have worked with data center developers to address concerns
rather than impose an outright ban. Instead, he has called for operators to build their own electricity and water-recycling facilities to reduce strain on regional resources.
Blakeman's position echoes comments made earlier this year by President Trump, who s
uggested data center operators construct their own power-generation facilities
. One complication: power grid access is often regulated by state-run utilities, meaning operators would likely still need to negotiate arrangements with them.
Although Hochul's stance has been labeled draconian by critics, she appears to have public support. A
Siena Research Institute poll from Septembe
r found that 63% of New Yorkers surveyed would oppose data centers even after the one-year moratorium expires.
Texas: a Governor's changing position
Texas, a state with both a strong data center presence and ongoing power grid challenges, is also hosting a pivotal gubernatorial race. Governor Greg Abbott
has largely supported data center development
but recently called for state regulators to audit proposed projects before allowing them to connect to Texas's power grid. His position has since hardened further —
he's now calling for a halt on all new data center permits
until existing projects undergo a complete audit.
Abbott's opponent, State Representative Gina Hinojosa,
has called for a full moratorium on data centers
, according to an MSNBC report, and has advocated for new laws clarifying the scope of AI development. The same report cited a
Texas Politics Project poll
showing that 58% of Texas voters oppose data centers being built in their communities.
Ohio: over 200 data centers and a divided race
Ohio, reportedly home to more than 200 data centers, is also holding a closely watched gubernatorial election between candidates with starkly different views.
report on Cleveland.Com
says that Democratic candidate Dr. Amy Acton supports a conditional moratorium, stating she would back new data centers only if they meet requirements involving costs, labor, environmental safeguards, location and transparency.
The same report
noted that Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy favored projects only if they meet electricity-benefit, property-tax, and environmental conditions. Meanwhile, Libertarian candidate Don Kissick supports a temporary moratorium while the state assesses long-term effects and lawmakers establish standards.
Innovation Ohio, a progressive policy advocacy organization,
commented on the data center positions of Acton and Ramaswamy in a report
, stating that while Acton's proposal appears workable, Ramaswamy's plan offers little more than vague assurances.

title: Why Ford’s Included Inverter Matters for Bidirectional EV Power
content:
Charging
EV Batteries
Automotive & Mobility
Ford's 2027 Fathom pairs a built-in inverter with bidirectional home power, signaling a more accessible path for EV energy integration.
October 28, 2026
3 Min Read
Ford Home Power Station and Ford Home Backup Power Panel.
Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) and vehicle-to-home (V2H) technology has attracted growing attention as electric vehicles (EVs) become more closely connected to the grid. EVs are increasingly being viewed as mobile batteries that can store electricity and return it when needed. Automakers begin to present them as practical consumer features rather than long-term possibilities.
Ford’s news about the
2027 Fathom electric truck
fits into that trend. The company says the truck will start at $28,350 MSRP and offer available bidirectional AC power. The most notable element of the announcement is that the Fathom does not require a separate wall-mounted inverter to supply a projected 10 kW of AC power to a home. Instead, the vehicle includes the inverter.
The E-box is one of Fathom’s five main modules. It serves multiple functions including sending AC power to a home. Credit: Ford.
Why the integrated inverter matters
Including the inverter in the vehicle is a first. Extra hardware can make home energy integration more expensive, more difficult to install, and harder for buyers to understand. By integrating the inverter into the truck, Ford appears to be reducing one of the technical barriers that has limited wider appeal.
Related:
Five Takeaways on CATL's Heavy-Duty Truck Electrification Strategy
But Ford says customers who want to use these functions will still need the Ford Home Power Station, and those who want backup capability during outages will also need the Ford Home Backup Power Panel. Ford outlines two ways the system could work for customers:
The Home Power Management, which would allow owners to charge the truck when electricity prices are lower and use the vehicle’s stored energy to power the home when prices are higher. In locations with time-of-use electricity pricing, that model could help some households reduce monthly energy costs.
The Home Backup Power, which would allow the truck to send electricity to a home during an outage. That positions the vehicle as an alternative to traditional backup generators, with the added benefit of operating without natural gas or diesel.
For Fathom customers, that two-way flow of electricity can work in two ways. Credit: Ford.
Why this is relevant beyond one vehicle launch
This announcement reflects a broader shift in how EVs are being presented to consumers. EVs are no longer defined only by range, charging speed, or performance. Increasingly, they are also being marketed as part of a household energy strategy.
Bidirectional energy features have often been associated with higher-priced EVs, which can limit their relevance to mainstream buyers. A lower entry price, if maintained, suggests that these capabilities may begin to move into a broader section of the market. That could increase public awareness of bidirectional charging and raise expectations for future EV models.
Related:
Home EV Chargers Need NEC and UL-Listed 50-Amp EV-Certified Receptacles
At the same time, there are still open questions. The final installed cost will depend on the required hardware, home configuration, and installation work. The practical value of 10 kW of AC power will vary depending on household loads, and real-world backup duration will depend on how much battery capacity is available when an outage occurs.

title: Oracle Cloud to Offer Google TPUs and New AI Chips
content:
Oracle is broadening the range of AI chips available through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, saying it plans to deploy Google’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) as well as inference chips from OpenAI, Cerebras, SambaNova, and Positron AI. The move gives OCI customers more options for running AI workloads beyond Nvidia GPUs.
Oracle said Tuesday, Oct. 27, that it will become the first hyperscaler to offer TPUs outside Google Cloud.
The announcement, made at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas, came alongside an expansion of Oracle’s partnership with Nvidia. Oracle said Nvidia’s
Vera Rubin NVL72
systems and Vera CPUs are now generally available on OCI. The company also said it plans to expand OCI Superclusters to multi-gigawatt scale using Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 systems.
Industry analysts said Oracle’s adoption of the additional AI accelerators gives customers more flexibility to match infrastructure to specific workload requirements. While Oracle Cloud has relied primarily on Nvidia GPUs, it also has some AMD GPU deployments, according to analysts.
Related:
How Chiplets Could Transform Server Design – And Data Centers
“Oracle has been a leader in AI factory development using Nvidia systems, and their move today suggests that they’re aligning with the industry direction towards heterogeneous computing,” said Brendan Burke, research director at Futurum Group. “Oracle is working closely with partners like OpenAI to select the best-fit compute, including Cerebras for fast inference.”
“The usage of alternative accelerators suggests that there are unique advantages to each, and that it’s worthwhile to offer choice to customers overall,” Burke added.
Matt Kimball, vice president and principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, said the announcement is an aggressive expansion by Oracle Cloud to support multiple AI chip architectures.
“This is Oracle trying to be the open silicon cloud – something for everybody,” Kimball said.
Burke noted that the challenge for Oracle will be proving that the new AI accelerators are competitive with Nvidia-based offerings and showing long-term commitment to them rather than treating them as limited experiments.
OCI Expands Beyond Nvidia with New AI Accelerators
Oracle said Google TPUs for training and inference will be available on OCI in 2027, with adoption ramping over a multi-year period. Oracle also said it will deploy the
Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine
for high-speed AI inference in 2027, while Positron AI’s
Positron Atlas
inference chip is now generally available on OCI.
Oracle also said Tuesday that it will deploy OpenAI’s
Jalapeño
inference accelerators, developed in partnership with Broadcom. OpenAI and Broadcom previously said they expect
initial deployment
of Jalapeño by the end of 2026, but Oracle did not specify when the chip will be available on OCI.
Related:
Microsoft Pushes Custom AI Chips with Azure Maia 300
SambaNova also announced Tuesday that it is collaborating with Oracle to deploy its SN50 inference chips in OCI, though no availability date was given in the press release. The SN50 is SambaNova’s fifth-generation Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit chip, designed for agentic AI workloads.
SambaNova asserts that the chip delivers up to five times the speed of competing chips at a total cost of ownership that is three times lower. The company also said the SN50 draws an average of 20 kW per rack, which is low enough to scale in existing air-cooled data centers.
Why Google Is Bringing TPUs to Oracle Cloud
Burke said Google
are highly competitive processors that have shown significant generational improvements.
With its eighth-generation TPU family, Google introduced two versions of the processor: TPU 8t for training and TPU 8i for inference. In a company
blog post
, Google said both versions deliver up to twice the performance per watt. Google also said TPU 8t provides up to 2.7x better performance per dollar, while TPU 8i provides up to 80% better performance per dollar than the previous generation.
Related:
AMD to Acquire World Labs for $8.2B to Advance AI Models and Robotics
Hyperscalers such as Google and AWS have found strategic value in building custom AI chips for their own infrastructure and cloud services. Now they also appear to see an opportunity to commercialize those chips more broadly.
reportedly
considered selling its
Trainium
AI chip for use in third-party data centers. Oracle’s announcement suggests Google also sees a market for TPUs beyond its own cloud platform.
After weighing whether to reserve its compute capacity for internal teams or make it more broadly available, Google appears to have shifted toward external deployment, Burke said. He attributed that move in part to continued tightness in the AI compute market.
“There's higher value in making it available than using it all internally,” he said.
Kimball said Google’s decision to make TPUs available on OCI allows customers to use them without migrating their data to Google Cloud.
“This is about Google understanding the value that it’s delivering in its TPU and trying to bring that value to customers, regardless of where their data lives,” Kimball said. “Oracle Cloud has a lot of customer data and a lot of AI use cases being deployed in it, so it only makes sense that you would want to bring TPUs to where the data is.”

title: Rethinking the Blind-Mate Connection
content:
Much of the conversation around liquid cooling focuses on the system itself. However, higher cooling demands are also changing expectations for the individual components within it.
One such component is the connection point between IT equipment and the
cooling infrastructure
. For server and rack designers, that connection now must do more than simply link two sides of a liquid loop. It must support greater coolant flow, fit within increasingly constrained server-tray space, and accommodate alignment variations that come with real-world installation and removal.
Those requirements have helped drive the development of a newer approach to the traditional blind-mate connection: the pivoting blind-mate coupling (PBMC).
PBMC technology was developed through collaboration within the Open Compute Project ecosystem and reflects a broader industry effort to address the changing needs of high-performance
liquid-cooled systems
. Parker Hannifin’s BQC Series is one example of this newer coupling architecture.
Related:
Why AI Data Center Cooling Needs to Get Smarter
Why the Connection Needed to Change
The development of the PBMC started with a practical set of system-level requirements.
Newer rack and
server architectures
called for greater flow through the connection while reducing the space the coupling occupied in the server tray. The connection also needed more self-alignment capability between the two sides as equipment was inserted and removed.
Solving one of those problems can make another more difficult.
Increasing flow can push designers toward larger flow paths. Server designers, meanwhile, are trying to preserve as much usable tray space as possible. And because a blind-mate connection is made during installation rather than being manually aligned by a technician, the coupling must also account for the possibility that the plug and socket may not align perfectly every time.
PBMC technology was developed to address those requirements as part of the same connection design.
Accounting for Real-World Misalignment
Blind-mate couplings already solve an important problem in liquid-cooled server systems: they allow a connection to be made as equipment is installed from the front (cold-aisle) side of the system.
That matters for more than convenience. The rear (hot-aisle) side of a server rack can contain manifolds, connections, and other equipment operating in a high-temperature environment. Installation and removal from the cold aisle can reduce the need for personnel to reach into the hot aisle to handle connections at the rear of the rack.
Related:
The Hidden Failure Domain in N+1 Data Center Cooling
The tradeoff is that a blind-mate connection does not have a technician guiding the two coupling halves together. Server trays, racks, and manifolds are also not always positioned with perfect precision. Small differences in component location can add up by the time the two sides of the connection meet.
A pivoting blind-mate design provides more self-alignment capability as the two sides of the connection come together. Rather than depending as heavily on near-perfect alignment between the two halves, the connection can accommodate a greater degree of positional variation during mating. For system designers, that can reduce the sensitivity of the connection to the normal dimensional variation present throughout the surrounding equipment.
That does not mean PBMCs replace every traditional blind-mate connection. They are particularly relevant in server-tray and blade-system applications where self-alignment capability, higher flow, and limited available space all have to be considered together.
More Flow Without Giving Up Server-Tray Space
Flow performance was another major factor behind the PBMC’s development.
As cooling requirements increase, the connection cannot become an unnecessary restriction within the loop. It needs to support the required coolant flow while keeping pressure losses through the connection under control.
Related:
Beyond WUE: Assessing Data Center Water Resilience
Simply making every component larger, however, is not an ideal answer.
Space inside the server tray is limited, and cooling hardware competes for room with the computing equipment it is meant to support. The length and overall footprint of the coupling therefore become part of the system-design conversation.
PBMC designs address that challenge by combining a larger flow path with a compact overall package. The objective is straightforward: support higher flow without requiring designers to give more of the tray to the connection itself.
Designing for High-Flow Conditions
Higher flow also creates challenges less visible than the connection size.
One is seal retention.
O-rings and other seals must remain securely positioned as fluid travels through the connection. Under demanding flow and pressure conditions, a poorly retained seal can be pulled from its groove and carried downstream with the system fluid.
This condition, often referred to as seal washout, can compromise the connection and create problems elsewhere in the cooling loop.
For that reason, seal retention becomes an important design consideration as coupling flow requirements increase. Retention features can help keep seals properly positioned under demanding operating conditions rather than treating them as an afterthought to flow performance.
Part of a Broader Shift in Liquid-Cooling Design
The value of PBMC technology is not tied to any one feature. Its development reflects how closely connected the requirements within modern liquid-cooling systems have become. Flow affects component size. Component size affects available tray space. Blind mating affects alignment requirements. Higher flow introduces its own mechanical considerations.
That means choosing a connection is no longer only a matter of moving coolant from one side to the other. Designers increasingly have to ask whether the connection can support the required flow without consuming too much tray space, tolerate normal alignment variation, support cold-aisle installation and service, and maintain reliable sealing under demanding operating conditions.
Those were the types of requirements that drove the PBMC approach through the Open Compute Project community. Parker Hannifin was among the companies involved in that work and has applied the PBMC architecture in its BQC Series, offering one example of how coupling manufacturers are responding to a broader shift in high-performance liquid cooling.

title: Where Solid-State Micro-Cooling Fits in Data Centers
content:
Managing heat in AI infrastructure is getting more complicated as rising power density turns thermal design into a performance constraint.
Liquid cooling
is increasingly focused on high-power CPUs and GPUs, but not every heat-producing component in a server sits under a cold plate. SSDs, memory, retimers, and optical subsystems can still develop localized hotspots that affect throughput and reliability.
That is the gap xMEMS says its solid-state micro-cooling technology is designed to address. The company has begun mass production of its XMC-2400 and XMC-4800 chips, which use a silicon-based design to move air without rotating blades or bearings. xMEMS says the products mark the first large-scale commercialization of solid-state active cooling for
edge AI systems
“As AI infrastructure evolves, component-level cooling will become an increasingly important complement to traditional system-level thermal management,” Mike Housholder, vice president and general manager of the Thermal Management Business Unit at xMEMS, told
Data Center Knowledge
Related:
Rethinking the Blind-Mate Connection
Why Liquid Cooling Leaves Some Hotspots Untouched
Cold plates
remove heat from the surface they touch directly. In liquid-cooled servers, that can leave some subsystems with uneven thermal coverage.
xMEMS sees enterprise SSDs as the clearest near-term example. Housholder said a cold plate attached to one side of an SSD can cool the controller and some NAND packages, while NAND on the opposite side may run hotter. That temperature gradient, he said, can contribute to thermal throttling and limit I/O performance during sustained workloads.
“We see enterprise SSDs as the strongest near-term use case,” Housholder said. “As AI workloads drive faster storage and more sustained data transfers, thermal throttling can limit SSD performance.”
The company argues that localized airflow inside the drive can reduce that imbalance. “Placing uCooling inside the SSD to cool the opposite-side NAND can reduce or remove this temperature gradient to maximize performance,” Housholder said. He added that similar thermal challenges are beginning to emerge in other dense AI infrastructure components.
How Solid-State Micro-Cooling Works
Unlike a conventional fan, solid-state active cooling uses a silicon chip to generate directed airflow. xMEMS builds its uCooling chips on a piezoMEMS semiconductor platform and says the all-silicon design can deliver high-pressure airflow through narrow micro-channels without the mechanical wear associated with small rotating fans.
Related:
Can Evaporative Cooling in Data Centers Still Make Sense?
According to xMEMS, the XMC-2400 delivers up to 28 cubic centimeters of airflow per second at up to 1,300 Pa of back pressure and consumes about 150 milliwatts (mW). The XMC-4800, which the company is targeting for enterprise SSDs, delivers up to 48 cubic centimeters per second at up to 1,100 Pa and consumes about 240 mW.
“At approximately the size of a thumbnail, the XMC-2400 can be embedded into highly constrained environments to deliver highly targeted airflow to heat-generating components where conventional approaches are difficult to implement or scale,” Housholder said.
(Image: xMEMS)
Why Micro-Cooling Is a Complement to Existing Cooling Systems
The company is not positioning the technology as an alternative to rack- or server-level cooling. Housholder said its airflow is only a fraction of what a conventional system fan can provide, making it better suited to localized hotspots inside tightly packaged subsystems than to whole-system thermal management.
“Solid-state active cooling is best viewed as a complementary technology that helps address localized hotspots within a broader cooling architecture, rather than a replacement for conventional cooling methods,” Housholder said. “Comparatively, uCooling’s airflow is a small fraction of that from a conventional system fan, but its ability to be embedded inside hard-to-reach subsystems brings value to the overall system thermal architecture.”
Related:
Why AI Data Center Cooling Needs to Get Smarter
In practice, that means the technology is more likely to arrive as part of another component than as a field-installed data center retrofit. xMEMS says uCooling can be mounted on flex or rigid PCBs and pre-assembled inside subsystems such as SSDs and laser modules, where airflow is difficult to deliver with chassis fans or cold plates alone.
Where Solid-State Micro-Cooling Could Expand Next
Longer term, xMEMS sees a path toward co-packaging thermal solutions that bring cooling closer to the processor package itself. For mainstream data center processors, however, Housholder said air-based micro-cooling may give way to liquid micro-channel designs because of the power density involved. He said air-based uCooling is likely to be more viable in edge AI systems, where thermal envelopes are lower and space constraints are tighter.
“Given the power density of data center processors, liquid (not air) micro-channels in the co-packaging architecture may be the next step,” Housholder said. “There are likely applications in co-packaging at the edge that are more viable for our air-based uCooling.”
The future of cooling is likely to incorporate a combination of technologies.
“Longer term, we expect future thermal architectures to combine liquid cooling, passive thermal solutions and localized active cooling technologies working together to optimize overall system performance,” Housholder said.

title: Ingrid Capacity, Alpiq explore up to 500 MW of Nordic BESS projects - Energy Storage
content: Swedish battery energy storage system (BESS) developer Ingrid Capacity and Swiss energy company Alpiq have signed an agreement to explore long-term offtake contracts for projects totaling up to 500 MW across northern Europe. The agreement builds on an existing project in Finland: the 45 MW/90 MWh battery storage system in Pedersöre, jointly owned by Ingrid Capacity and French asset manager Mirova. The partnership combines Ingrid Capacity’s battery storage portfolio and operational expertise with Alpiq’s financial strength and ability to offer long-term offtake agreements that could facilitate project financing. The companies said the arrangements are intended to enable more efficient financing structures and give investors flexible, long-term exposure to energy markets through this asset class. Amanda Niklaus, chief revenue officer at Ingrid Capacity, said financing and commercial agreements are becoming just as important as technology and operational performance as the Nordic battery market evolves. The company has a battery storage portfolio of 950 MWh, including projects in development, under construction and operational. The partnership aims to secure part of future revenues through long-term offtake agreements. Under such contracts, a buyer commits to purchasing electricity, storage capacity or services under agreed terms. These commitments can give lenders greater certainty and help projects secure financing. Batteries can earn revenue across several markets, including electricity trading, grid balancing and ancillary services. However, these revenue streams fluctuate with electricity prices and power system requirements. Aivaras Simkunas, Alpiq’s head of energy solutions for the Nordic countries, said the company’s financial backing and long-term offtake contracts could help secure project financing while preserving flexibility in Nordic electricity markets. title: LG Energy Solution, Energix sign MoU to explore up to 4.5 GWh of BESS deployments - Energy Storage
content: LG Energy Solution has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Israeli-headquartered renewable energy developer Energix-Renewable Energies Ltd to expand their collaboration on battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in Europe and North America. Under the non-binding agreement, the companies will explore the supply of around 2 GWh of BESS solutions over the next 24 months. LG Energy Solution stated it would be approximately 1.5 GWh supplied to Europe, with another 0.5 GWh in North America. The companies will also discuss increasing the overall deployment volume to around 4.5 GWh, with 3 GWh allocated to Europe and 1.5 GWh for North America, through LG Energy Solution’s operations in both regions. According to Energix, the MoU was signed during a leadership summit in Seoul, South Korea. The company also said the partnership could include the deployment of U.S.-manufactured, FEOC-compliant battery systems for its U.S. projects. This latest MoU builds on an existing relationship between the companies in Europe. LG Energy Solution previously supplied battery solutions for the 24 MW / 56 MWh Nowe Czarnowo BESS in Poland where Energix was the developer. A potential collaboration between the companies is also being discussed for Energix’s Jonava project in Lithuania. It is a hybrid renewable energy project, combining 330 MWp of solar PV, 140 MW of onshore wind, and a 320 MWh BESS, with commercial operations targeted for 2027. “Through our collaboration with Energix, we will expand ESS business opportunities in Europe and North America and further strengthen our global customer base,” said Changbeom Kang, ESS battery division leader of LG Energy Solution. “Leveraging our differentiated technology and local manufacturing capabilities, we will accelerate the growth of our global ESS business.” Energix is currently targeting a long-term global portfolio pipeline of more than 8 GW. Asa Levinger, CEO of Energix Group, said the MoU is an important step towards that goal. “This agreement marks an important step in strengthening our long-term relationship with LG Energy Solution. We look forward to exploring opportunities to deploy high-quality energy storage solutions across our project pipeline and accelerate the expansion of renewable energy in our core markets,” said Levinger. title: Bosch’s popular e-bike motor just got upgraded with more power and less weight
content:
Micah Toll
| Oct 28 2026 - 12:32 am PT
Bosch has unveiled the latest generation of its popular Active Line Plus electric bicycle motor, bringing more power, less weight, and a significantly smaller footprint to one of the company’s most widely used drive systems.
The new motor is designed primarily for everyday riders, including commuters, recreational cyclists, and those who want a comfortable e-bike that can handle everything from city streets to weekend trail rides.
And while it isn’t
most powerful motor, the upgrades are fairly substantial.
The new Active Line Plus now produces up to 600 watts of peak power and 60 Nm of torque, along with a maximum pedal assistance level of 340%. That’s enough to give riders a healthy boost when accelerating away from traffic lights or climbing hills, without necessarily turning their everyday commuter into an overpowered mountain bike.
Like its predecessor, the motor is designed for Class 1 electric bicycles in the US, providing pedal assistance up to 20 mph (32 km/h) without a throttle.
Remember, the Active Line motor is the drive system model that
many e-bike companies use for their modestly performing e-bikes
. It gives good power and control, combined with all the tech we’ve come to expect from Bosch, but it isn’t the motor e-bike makers use when they need an electric mountain bike to scale a steep mountainous trail.
Smaller, lighter, and quieter
Perhaps even more interesting than the increased power is what Bosch has done to the motor’s physical design.
The company developed a new two-stage gearbox that helps reduce the motor’s overall volume by 17% while shaving approximately 1.1 lb (0.5 kg) off its weight.
The new drive unit now tips the scales at around 6 lb (2.7 kg), making it easier for bicycle manufacturers to integrate into slimmer, more traditional-looking frames.
Bosch also says the new gearbox uses specially machined gears to make the motor virtually silent, while updated sensors and software provide smoother, more natural-feeling pedal assistance.
That’s particularly important for a motor like the Active Line Plus, where riders are often looking for an experience that feels like riding a regular bicycle, just with a bit of extra help.
The motor also supports Bosch’s eShift electronic shifting system, which can automatically manage gear changes for riders who prefer to focus on pedaling instead of shifting.
Bosch has additionally improved the motor’s sealing and bearings for better all-weather durability. The housing uses approximately 40% recycled aluminum, helping reduce the carbon footprint of its production.
Coming soon to new electric bikes
Trek will be the first North American bicycle brand to introduce the new Active Line Plus motor, installing it on the company’s Marlin+ electric bike.
Bosch also announced several other additions to its e-bike ecosystem, including a new compact LED Controller that’s 65% smaller than its predecessor, an updated ConnectModule with Bluetooth-based theft tracking, and a new 720 Wh PowerTube battery weighing just 8.6 lb (3.9 kg).
There’s also a new Intuvia 200 display, offering a 2.4-inch grayscale screen for riders who prefer a traditional handlebar-mounted display.
While high-performance e-bike motors tend to grab the headlines with increasingly outrageous torque figures, there’s something to be said for improvements to the more practical end of the market – something for the riders looking for convenient and effective transportation instead of peak performance figures.
For the average commuter or recreational rider, a quieter, lighter motor with plenty of usable power is likely to make a bigger difference than squeezing another few dozen Newton-meters out of an already powerful drive system.
And with Bosch’s extensive network of bicycle manufacturing partners, we can expect to see this updated motor making its way into plenty of new electric bikes.

title: CATL pushes ahead with 20 Ah solid-state EV batteries, with 500 Wh/kg in sight
content:
Solid-state batteries
Peter Johnson
| Oct 28 2026 - 8:12 am PT
CATL hit another milestone in its
solid-state battery
development, advancing to 20 Ah cells. The world’s leading battery maker aims to begin small-scale production in 2027.
CATL continues advancing solid-state EV batteries
CATL remains the leading global EV battery manufacturer by a wide margin. According to
SNE Research
, CATL held a commanding 39.9% share of the global EV battery market through the first half of 2026.
To stay ahead, the company is advancing several new battery chemistries, including solid-state and sodium-ion, promising to be safer, more efficient, and lower cost than traditional lithium-ion batteries.
When investors asked about the progress of its solid-state battery program on Tuesday, CATL said it continues to invest heavily in all-solid-state batteries and expects to begin small-scale production in 2027.
As it has stated before, output is expected to be limited at first as it scales up to mass production around 2030.
Speaking at the Summer Davos Forum in June, CATL chairman and CEO Robin Zeng said that, on a scale of one to nine, all-solid-state batteries
have only reached
level four.
All-solid-state batteries differ from semi-solid-state batteries in that they require a solid electrolyte to conduct lithium ions, rather than a liquid.
Dr Wu Kai, CATL’s chief scientist (Source: CATL)
The company uses a sulfide-based solid electrolyte system, which offers high ionic conductivity and deformability, but maintaining stable contact between solid components remains a hurdle.
CATL said its sulfide-based batteries have now entered 20 Ah trial production as it aims to achieve an energy density of 500 Wh/kg.
Trial production in 2027, reaching mass market in 2030
CATL’s 2027 timeline to begin small-scale production aligns with other automakers and battery manufacturers racing to introduce all-solid-state EV batteries.
Toyota, which has been promising solid-state batteries for nearly a decade now, aims to launch the
first all-solid-state battery-powered EV
in 2027 or 2028.
Toyota EV battery roadmap (Source: Toyota)
Using Sumitomo Metal Mining’s proprietary powder synthesis technology, Toyota claimed to have developed a “highly durable cathode material” for all-solid-state batteries last October. Toyota revealed
a prototype
last year, claiming it can deliver 745 miles (1,200 km) of range and charge in under 10 minutes.
However, like CATL, Toyota expects production to be limited and will not reach the mass market until closer to the end of the decade.
(Source: Toyota)
Samsung SDI, on the other hand, aims to begin mass production of its SolidStack all-solid-state batteries in the second half of 2027.
BYD, which ranks second in global EV battery sales behind CATL, also plans to launch its first solid-state battery-powered vehicle in 2027.
In an exclusive interview with
last month, executive vice president Stella Li said BYD is in “the leading position” on solid-state batteries and will “prove that” next year.
BYD’s battery division, FinDreams, aims to begin producing
sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries
in limited batches in 2027, ramping up to mass production by 2030.
Electrek’s Take
While solid-state batteries are often hailed the “holy grail” of battery tech, they are only one part of the equation.
CATL, BYD, and others continue advancing lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and sodium-ion batteries, which will ultimately create more efficient, lower-cost options that offer various performance needs.
BYD’s second-generation Blade LFP batteries already deliver
over 1,000 km
(621 miles) of CLTC range. What’s next?
One thing is certain: New battery chemistries and evolving tech will only continue making EVs more efficient, unlocking longer driving ranges, faster charging speeds, and better performance.

title: Ford casts 5,000 'unicastings' for Fathom EV truck in Tesla-style shift
content:
Ford Fathom
Fred Lambert
| Oct 28 2026 - 6:56 am PT
A Ford team member inspects a Fathom unicasting (Image: Ford)
Ford has now produced more than 5,000 large aluminum “unicastings” for the Fathom, its upcoming $28,350 midsize electric pickup, as it fine-tunes the process ahead of a 2027 launch.
Each truck gets two of them, front and rear, replacing 146 individual parts. It’s the clearest sign yet that Ford is all-in on the manufacturing approach Tesla popularized with its Giga Press six years ago.
Inside Ford’s unicasting process
The update comes from Vladimir Bogachuk, Ford’s chief engineer of advanced vehicle structure architecture, in a
post on Ford’s From the Road blog
. The castings are made at Ford’s Shelbyville Technical Center and shipped to Louisville Assembly Plant for process testing and prototype builds. Louisville is the Kentucky factory Ford is retooling for the Fathom and other vehicles on its
Universal EV Platform
A Fathom unicasting at Ford’s Shelbyville Technical Center (Image: Ford)
Ford melts aluminum ingots at about 1,300°F (700°C) and injects the metal into either a front or rear structure mold. Once a robot pulls the part out, it goes into a quench tank, gets trimmed and machined, and then runs a gauntlet of checks: industrial X-ray scans for pores and voids, dimensional measurements in a climate-controlled room, optical surface scans, and lab tensile and chemistry tests on samples.
Machining a Fathom unicasting after it comes out of the casting machine (Image: Ford)
Nothing ships to Louisville until a batch clears every inspection. Ford says it’s also working on cutting cycle time and on designing the castings for “modular repairability.”
Every batch is held until it clears inspections, including industrial X-ray scans (Image: Ford)
That last part has been the main reason why automakers have been reticent about larger cast parts. Repair cost is the biggest knock on giant castings, since a damaged one-piece structure can turn a moderate crash into a write-off. Lucid executive Cory Steuben has said insurance concerns drove the company’s decision to skip gigacasting altogether.
Tesla started it with 70 parts
Tesla kicked this off in 2020 with the first IDRA Giga Press at Fremont, a machine with roughly 6,000 tons of clamping force. It
cast the Model Y’s rear underbody in a single piece
, replacing 70 parts, and Elon Musk said the change removed the need for about 300 robots.
Tesla wanted to go much further. It added a front casting, tied the two together with a structural battery pack, and moved to even bigger presses for the Cybertruck. But in 2024, Reuters reported that Tesla had backed away from its plan to cast nearly the entire underbody in one piece, and the automaker has reportedly since dropped the front casting on some Model Y production.
So Ford’s 146-to-2 figure looks great on paper. But it’s a front-and-rear layout, basically the same architecture Tesla launched with on the Model Y. Ford isn’t leapfrogging Tesla here. It’s catching up, just with a vehicle that will cost less than any Tesla on sale.
Ford has now produced more than 5,000 Fathom unicastings (Image: Ford)
The industry went bigger, but not everyone
Since that first Giga Press, a growing list of automakers have bought huge presses or committed to them:
Volvo started EX60 production at Torslanda this year with a single rear megacasting, and it
ordered two 9,000-ton-class IDRA presses
for its new plant in Slovakia.
Xiaomi runs 9,100-ton presses, combining 72 components into one underbody casting.
Xpeng casts the G6’s front and rear underbody, merging more than 300 parts across the two.
Honda is installing six 6,100-ton presses at its Anna Engine Plant in Ohio for EV components.
Toyota has shown its own gigacasting process, and group supplier Aisin plans to spend $3.4 billion over three years.
Others aren’t buying it. Stellantis has said it won’t invest in gigacasting, while BMW and Mercedes-Benz have stuck with smaller presses for body parts. Hyundai pushed its “Hypercasting” plan back two years.
Electrek’s Take
We’ve been tracking this casting race since Tesla’s first Giga Press showed up in Fremont, and the lesson so far is simple. Fewer parts is great, but the press alone doesn’t make a car cheap. The whole factory does.
That’s why Ford’s approach is worth watching. The unicastings are one piece of a bigger overhaul at Louisville, where Ford is splitting the line into three branches (front, rear, and the battery pack with the interior floor) that meet at the end. Ford says that can be up to 40% faster than its current assembly, or about 15% net once it reinvests some of the savings into automation and insourcing. It’s very close to the logic behind Tesla’s “unboxed” process, and they are betting it’s what actually gets you to a $28,350 truck.

title: New retro electric motorcycle to debut at EICMA with a novel feature: a second gear
content:
Electric Motorcycles
Micah Toll
| Oct 28 2026 - 6:48 am PT
Most electric motorcycles have something in common: a single-speed transmission. But a British company is preparing to shake things up at this year’s EICMA motorcycle show in Milan, where it will unveil a new electric motorcycle demonstrator featuring an unusual two-speed transmission designed to shift gears without interrupting power delivery.
The company behind the technology,
E-Motiv Shift Systems
, has developed what it calls a seamless powershift transmission, promising improved acceleration, better efficiency, and a more engaging riding experience.
Unlike conventional motorcycle transmissions, which generally require a brief interruption in power during gear changes, E-Motiv’s system is designed to maintain torque throughout the shift.
That could offer some interesting advantages for electric motorcycles, where a lower first gear could provide stronger acceleration while a taller second gear could help optimize motor efficiency at higher speeds.
Of course, most electric motorcycles don’t actually need multiple gears, and
very few have ever offered multi-speed transmissions
. Electric motors produce strong torque across a wide operating range, which is why manufacturers generally prefer the simplicity, lower weight, and reduced maintenance of single-speed drivetrains.
But that doesn’t mean a second gear couldn’t offer some benefits.
E-Motiv’s technology actually traces its roots back nearly 25 years to the Zeroshift transmission system, which eventually found its way into Aprilia’s MotoGP racing motorcycles in 2015.
The latest electric version was developed through a £1 million UK government-funded project involving motorcycle manufacturer BSA, the University of Bath, and the Institute of Advanced Automotive Propulsion Systems (IAAPS).
The demonstrator motorcycle, known as Demo 1, was conceived by British design consultancy Envisage and is being built by IAAPS. Real-world testing is scheduled to begin in early 2027.
E-Motiv will showcase the technology at EICMA from November 3-8, though the demonstrator remains a development project rather than a production-ready motorcycle.
Whether two-speed transmissions eventually become common on electric motorcycles remains to be seen. But if E-Motiv can deliver meaningful efficiency and performance improvements without adding too much weight, cost, or complexity, it could give future electric motorcycles another interesting trick up their sleeves.

title: Tesla Semi catches fire on I-880 with no crash, closes freeway for 10 hours
content:
Tesla Semi
Electric Semi Truck
Fred Lambert
| Oct 28 2026 - 5:34 am PT
Photo: CHP Hayward
A Tesla Semi caught fire on Interstate 880 in Hayward, California, on Tuesday evening, and there was no crash. The electric truck’s lithium-ion battery burned long enough to keep the southbound freeway closed for about 10 hours.
The driver got out unhurt. But a Class 8 electric truck catching fire on its own, in traffic, is something Tesla and its growing list of Semi customers need to explain.
What happened on I-880
The fire broke out at around 5:35 p.m. PT in the southbound lanes near Route 92. CHP Hayward then closed I-880 in both directions, citing “the potential risk of hazardous chemical smoke,” and posted these photos from the scene:
🚨 TRAFFIC ALERT – I-880 FULL CLOSURE 🚨
A Tesla semi-truck has caught fire on I-880, resulting in a complete shutdown of both northbound and southbound lanes due to the potential risk of hazardous chemical smoke.
The driver told officers the truck caught fire and that they didn’t know why. No other vehicles were involved.
Northbound reopened Tuesday night. Southbound took much longer. CHP initially warned that the battery could burn for 15 to 18 hours, but crews beat that estimate, and
CHP Hayward posted
that all lanes were open at around 3:30 a.m. Wednesday.
The CHP photos show firefighters laying foam around the burned-out tractor, with the front of a Premier Trailer Leasing trailer charred behind it. The truck’s operator hasn’t been identified, and Tesla, which doesn’t have a press office, hasn’t commented. The cause is under investigation.
The second Semi fire to close a California interstate
We’ve been here before. In August 2024, a Tesla-operated Semi
caught fire on I-80 near Emigrant Gap
while driving from Livermore to Tesla’s facility in Sparks, Nevada. At the time, no crash was reported. The
NTSB later found
the truck had left the road on a curve, hit a delineator post and a tree, and its battery ignited after the impact. Firefighters used about 50,000 gallons of water, and the lanes stayed closed for up to 15 hours.
Hayward is different. Without a crash, the focus shifts to the truck itself: the battery pack, the high-voltage system, the drive units, or something as ordinary as a tire or brake fire that spread.
And the timing isn’t great for Tesla. The company only
started volume production of the Semi in Nevada
this year, after nearly a decade of delays. WattEV ordered 370 Semis in May, mostly for drayage at the Port of Oakland, just a few miles up I-880 from where Tuesday’s truck burned. In September, Tesla was also named lead supplier on a 2,500-truck ZET SCALE order.
Electrek’s Take
First, some perspective, because this fire is going to get used as an anti-EV talking point. Truck fires are common. According to
NFPA data
, US fire departments responded to an average of 15,462 large-truck fires per year between 2018 and 2022. That’s about 42 a day, in a fleet that’s overwhelmingly diesel. Mechanical failure was a factor in 44% of them, and only about 2% were tied to a collision.
The same goes for cars. NFPA and DOT data put the US average at one vehicle fire for every 17 million miles traveled, and combustion vehicles make up the vast majority of that fleet. Tesla
one fire per 140 million miles for its own vehicles. That’s Tesla’s number, but independent data, like
government figures we’ve covered before
, points the same way: gas vehicles catch fire more often than EVs.
But that doesn’t get the Semi off the hook. Diesel fires happen across millions of trucks. Tesla doesn’t disclose Semi deliveries, but PepsiCo, its launch customer, was up to about 86 trucks in 2024, and volume production only started a few months ago. With a fleet that small, one fire with no crash is a big data point. It’s also the second Semi fire to shut down a California interstate in about two years.
So we need the cause. If a tire, a brake, or the trailer caught fire and it spread to the tractor, that’s a regular trucking problem. If the pack went into thermal runaway on its own, Tesla needs to find out why before tens of thousands of these trucks hit the road, and fire departments need a better plan than letting a loaded truck burn on a freeway for half the night.
The NTSB investigated the last one. It should look at this one too, and Tesla should publish what it finds. Will it?
