title: AI-Powered Coffee Runs And Service Visits Are Coming To Rivians In 2027
content:
AI-Powered Coffee Runs And Service Visits Are Coming To Rivians In 2027
Rivian Chief Software Officer Wassym Bensaid says new AI integrations will order your coffee and automate vehicle service starting next year.
Rivian's AI assistant will soon order coffee on your route so it’s fresh when you arrive at a coffee shop.
Future updates will automatically diagnose vehicle issues and book service appointments behind the scenes.
Rivian aims to eventually let owners control virtually every vehicle function through voice and AI.
When Rivian launched its in-house AI assistant in May, the company promised that the tech would soon do far more than answer ChatGPT-style questions, switch on the A/C, or text your friends. It pitched a chatbot that could be deeply integrated into your R1S or R2—but also deeply integrated into your life.
The Assistant hit the scene with Google Calendar capability, allowing drivers to move meetings on the fly, and Gmail came in October. In an interview on the Plugged-In Podcast this week, Rivian Chief Software Officer Wassym Bensaid said flashier integrations are coming soon, including one that will overhaul the service experience for Rivian owners.
"What I'm really excited about is the possibility in the future where you can bring your own personal digital ecosystem to the car through these AI integrations, and then also the possibility that you can start integrating with multiple other agentic experiences," he said.
One example: ordering coffee on your way to work. Bensaid said the Assistant will be able to help you order coffee from the right place at the right time, so that it's at the right temperature when you swing by.
The Rivian Assistant can answer general knowledge questions, control the vehicle, and integrate with a driver's Google Calendar and Gmail.
Thanks to AI, the experience of getting a Rivian serviced will become a lot smoother and more automated, he said. Rivian's AI tech will soon proactively diagnose issues, set up service appointments for owners, and make sure the service center has the right parts before an owner arrives, he said.
"That's a complete paradigm shift in that entire experience, and not only enables us to have a much more delightful experience for customers, but then it's a big efficiency lever for us and it helps us be much more competitive from a cost standpoint for something like service," he said.
We asked when exactly Rivian owners can expect these features to hit their vehicles. Bensaid said a lot of them are already in the works but need to get more reliable before a wider release.
"We're very close," he said. "We're talking about things that we will launch in 2027."
To check out our full Wassym Bensaid interview, head to Spotify, Apple, or scroll down to the video player below.
Rivian has an ambitious tech vision for its AI. And the Rivian Assistant is already impressive in some ways. But owners have also complained about shortcomings. I asked Bensaid about those growing pains.
"Similar to other features, other technologies, there's still tuning, and there's still some refinements that we need to continue doing," he said. "A lot of them is on us, which is great. Some of them are work with our partners in terms of how we ground some of the requests and how we really optimize them."
But getting today's features right is only part of the challenge. Rivian ultimately wants the Assistant to handle virtually anything drivers can do through the touchscreen.
"Our philosophy is eventually, through that deep OS integration, the end state is really having that ability to, through voice and through AI, you will be able to do everything that you're doing with your fingers on the screen."

title: Rivian's Charging Network Grew 39% In A Year
content:
Rivian's Charging Network Grew 39% In A Year
The startup is actively investing in its own EV fast charging network, even though its models can use Tesla Superchargers.
- Rivian hasn’t forgotten about its DC fast charging network.
- The Rivian Adventure Network grew 39% in the last 12 months, surpassing 1,000 individual chargers.
- Meanwhile, the company’s slower Waypoint chargers aren’t getting much love.
Rivian’s Adventure Network of DC fast chargers has expanded nearly 40% in the last 12 months, surpassing 1,100 individual chargers and 150 locations across the United States.
The company said in its third-quarter earnings report that its EV fast charging network now has 1,185 ports capable of delivering up to 300 kilowatts of power, up 39% compared to last year’s third quarter. Meanwhile, the number of stations has gone up to 165, or 26% more than at the end of Q3 2025.
Rivian DC fast charger
The startup claims its fast chargers are powered by 100% renewable energy, though that doesn’t always mean that he electricity coming out of a charger is sourced from a photovoltaic array or a wind farm. Instead, every kilowatt-hour delivered through a RAN charger is matched with renewable sources that may operate in another town or another state.
Rivian has continued to invest in its own charging infrastructure, which uses purpose-built stalls, even though its passenger models have access to tens of thousands of public DC chargers across the U.S., including countless NACS-equipped Tesla Superchargers.
However, while the DC charging infrastructure was mentioned in the startup’s latest presentation, the Waypoints network of Level 2 chargers has gotten a lot less attention. The slower chargers didn’t get a single mention in any of the company’s most recent documents, but they haven’t been completely forgotten.
That said, the growth rate seems to have been significantly slower compared to the RAN network. According to data from the Department of Energy’s Alternative Fuels Data Center (AFDC), the company installed just ten 11-kilowatt chargers this year, with the latest pair going online in October. In total, Rivian operates 540 Waypoint Level 2 chargers at 208 locations in the U.S.
Despite the quick growth in its DC charging network, the California startup is still a tiny player in a rapidly evolving industry. By comparison, Tesla, the biggest name in the game, has over 40,000 fast charging ports at nearly 3,300 locations in the U.S., with an additional 14,000 Level 2 Destination Chargers at almost 4,000 sites.

title: Waymo's Public Fast-Charging Problem Is Infuriating EV Drivers
content:
Waymo's Public Fast-Charging Problem Is Infuriating EV Drivers
Robotaxi companies need to figure out how their driverless cars can be less annoying for everyday drivers.
- Some Waymo robotaxis in San Diego, California, are crowding public fast charging stations.
- Regular electric vehicle drivers are frustrated as they have to wait for spots to open up.
- Waymo said it prioritizes charging at its own depots.
Imagine pulling up to a public fast-charging station for a quick top-up, only to find several Waymo robotaxis occupying the stalls. That's reportedly happening in San Diego, California, where some EV drivers say they've had to wait up to an hour or find another charging location.
The Alphabet-owned company is rapidly expanding across the U.S. and now serves riders in 15 cities. But its growing fleet is creating an unexpected headache for some EV drivers. While Waymo operates dedicated depots for vehicle maintenance and charging, some of its robotaxis are also using public fast-charging stations, the Los Angeles Times reported Friday.
“They come in droves,” one driver told the outlet.
Waymo told the newspaper that it has people at some public charging locations to assist robotaxis as they arrive, and that it tries to avoid having vehicles crowd one station. Its Jaguar I-Paces and Zeekr vans that are sometimes driven by humans may also use public chargers during breaks, the spokesperson said. The company prioritizes its own charging hubs, Waymo said. But setting up dedicated facilities can take time when entering new markets.
The friction between Waymos and EV drivers highlights how the arrival of autonomous vehicles is creating some unexpected headaches.
EV drivers in Nashville and St. Louis have also accused Waymos of hogging public chargers, according to social media posts. Santa Monica residents also complained last year about noise from Waymos returning from overnight shifts which had beeping parking sensors and flashing lights. In San Francisco, residents have reported Waymos honking at each other in the middle of the night at a depot.
EVgo told the LA Times that its San Diego chargers are available to both private EV drivers and robotaxis. In other words, Waymo isn't breaking any rules by plugging in. But that doesn't make the situation any less frustrating for drivers who depend on those stations.
It’s certainly an awkward situation. Building more public fast chargers will help—and we know that’s happening nationwide at a steady speed. And Waymo says it prioritizes its own private depots. But as it stands, robotaxis and human drivers are competing for limited real estate.

title: AI 基建掀起军备竞赛：微软、谷歌、甲骨文等巨头承诺投入超 3 万亿美元
content:
IT之家 10 月 31 日消息，据彭博社今天（31 日）凌晨报道，AI 基础设施建设仍将吸引巨额资金。Alphabet、Meta、微软、亚马逊和甲骨文五大科技巨头承诺，未来数年将在数据中心等领域投入超过 3 万亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 20.01 万亿元人民币）。
随着数据中心建设竞赛愈演愈烈，五家公司披露的租赁、建筑、能源及设备采购承诺大幅增长。这些资金有的将在短期内支出，有的则涉及未来数十年的长期合同。
谷歌的支出承诺规模最大。根据 Alphabet 提交的监管文件，包括技术设备、能源和租赁在内的合同承诺总额超过 1 万亿美元（现汇率约合 6.67 万亿元人民币），接近一年前的八倍。
Meta 的支出承诺同样大幅攀升，未来支出总额超过 8,000 亿美元（现汇率约合 5.34 万亿元人民币）。其中将近一半用于尚未生效的数据中心租约，最长分 30 年支付。Meta CFO 苏珊 · 李在上周的分析师电话会议上说：“我们预计将继续大举投资，支持核心业务和新兴 AI 项目。”
今年商界的一大争论，是科技企业斥资数千亿美元建设 AI 数据中心，究竟能否收回投资。Alphabet 和 Meta 都是全球最赚钱的企业之一，却因投资有望改变行业格局的新业务，出现自由现金流由正转负的情况。
不过，五家公司的支出并非全部用于数据中心，披露口径也不完全一致，因此很难直接比较。
例如，Meta 的部分预算用于 Reality Labs 部门的消费级硬件产品，Alphabet 和亚马逊的计划支出则包括内容授权费用。本次统计也没有计入现有租约和债务等其他大额支出。
五家公司未来的租赁付款承诺合计 1.3 万亿美元（现汇率约合 8.67 万亿元人民币），其他采购承诺合计 1.9 万亿美元（现汇率约合 12.67 万亿元人民币）。除微软外，数据均取自各家公司最新财报。微软的采购和建设订单数据来自截至 6 月底的年度报告，该公司此后尚未更新这两项数据。
甲骨文是首家因投资 AI 数据中心而陷入自由现金流为负的大型科技公司。在本周早些时候举行的投资者说明会上，甲骨文预计到 2028 年恢复正自由现金流，并计划通过供应商融资和客户预付款等方式，减少项目初期需要自行承担的资金支出。

title: 全球首例，美国一公司完成在人体内直接编辑 DNA 试验
content:
感谢IT之家网友
软媒用户1238620
10 月 31 日消息，美国生物技术公司先导医药（Prime Medicine）10 月初宣布，已利用先导编辑技术，
全球首次在人体内直接编辑 DNA
，治疗一名威尔逊病患者。首批临床试验结果预计 2027 年公布。
IT之家注：威尔逊病是一种常染色体隐性遗传的铜代谢障碍病，核心问题是身体排不出多余的铜，导致铜沉积在肝脏、大脑、角膜等部位。目前的药物治疗具有非治愈性，需要终身治疗。肝移植是目前唯一的治愈选择，但受限于器官供应，且存在较高的手术风险。
在一项针对威尔逊病的全球临床试验中，该团队为参与者
直接重写肝细胞中的 DNA
。首位患者本月初接受了试验，但安全性和效果的检测结果预计要到明年才会出炉。
Prime Medicine 首席医疗官 Mohammed Asmal 在新闻稿中表示，该疗法“有潜力为患者提供一次性治愈性治疗，理想情况下是在肝脏和神经系统不可逆损伤发生之前。”
IT之家查询了解到，Prime Medicine 是一家美国的生物技术公司，致力于为患者创造和提供下一代基因编辑疗法。该公司正在部署其专有的
Prime Editing 平台
—— 一种多功能基因编辑技术。
Prime Editor 的设计目的是在基因的正确位置进行正确的编辑，同时最大限度地减少不必要的 DNA 修改，宣称有潜力修复几乎所有类型的基因突变，并适用于多种不同的组织、器官和细胞类型。

title: 印度自己的空间站 BAS 规划公布：模块化设计，2028 年开造
content:
IT之家 10 月 31 日消息，据印度政府科技与技术部生物技术司披露的信息，在 10 月 27 日开幕的印度“新兴科学技术与创新大会”上，印度空间研究组织 Bharatiya Antariksh Station 项目（BAS 项目）主管 K. Kalpana 女士公布了印度自己的空间站 BAS 的相关规划。
BAS 规划设计为一座重 54 吨、由 5 个模块组成的空间站，轨道高度 450 公里，拥有 100 立方米适居容积，60 千瓦发电，具备通用对接能力，将容纳 3 至 4 名长期宇航员及 3 名短期宇航员访客。
每个模块各司其职，形成一个统一的、电学集成的轨道复合体，设计注重高容错性和资源共享。IT之家附具体各模块用途如下：
- BAS-01（基础模块）将提供船员栖息地、维护和技术试验。它将集成科学机架和非再生式 ECLSS 生命支持系统。
- BAS-02（核心模块）将作为中央节点，配备国际对接系统标准（IDSS）对接适配器。它将集成科学机架、再生式和非再生式 ECLSS，以及锻炼和体能维持设备。
- BAS-03（科学模块）将专用于科学研究和支持舱外活动（EVA）。它将配备有效载荷机架和再生式 ECLSS 系统。
- BAS-04（实验室模块）将容纳地球观测穹顶和研究设施。它还将包括额外的宇航员舱室和卫生设备 PHMS。
- BAS-05（停靠模块）将集成通用对接机制，以方便未来空间站的扩展。它将特别支持新模块和货运飞行器的接收。
此外，BAS 空间站将依靠内部和外部的机械臂进行维护和组装操作，还计划使用自由飞行动态机器人和人形机器人进行检查和轨道操作。
BAS 空间站将进行分阶段组装，计划 2028 年 6 月发射第一个模块 BAS-01，随后通过 Gaganyaan V5 任务进行货物对接演示，以及后续的宇航员和模块发射，为 2035 年完成空间站组装铺平道路。
BAS-01 的研发和发射获批预算约为 1.85 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 12.34 亿元人民币）。

title: 国内首个：新疆发现特大型锆（铪）砂矿，大幅提高我国锆矿自给能力
content:
感谢IT之家网友
10 月 31 日消息，据央视财经今日报道，新疆阿克苏地区拜城县发现
国内首个古河湖相锆砂矿
，这将大幅提高我国锆矿自给能力。
2006 年至 2019 年，通过地质资料二次开发，圈定多处锆（铪）矿矿化异常和找矿靶区。
2024 年以来，聚焦锆矿成矿有利区，通过 3 年攻坚实现了锆砂矿重大找矿突破。为表彰彭宇和王海涛两名地质队员在发现该矿中作出的贡献，将其命名为“宇海锆矿”。
2026 年 9 月，经评审认定，宇海锆矿资源储量规模相当于 40 多个大型锆矿，伴生的铪矿也达到超大型规模。
新疆维吾尔自治区自然资源厅相关负责人表示，将尽快组织宇海锆矿矿业权公开出让，督促矿业权人加快增储上产，力争将宇海锆矿打造成为全国重要的资源勘查开发基地。
锆 Zirconium（gào）与铪 Hafnium（hā）同属于元素周期表第四副族，物理化学性质相差无几，在自然界中它们总是相伴相生，所以很难找到只含锆不含铪的矿物。它们就像同一家族的“孪生兄弟”，几乎形影不离，
如何高效地把这对“孪生兄弟”分开至今仍是科学界攻关的难点
锆：几乎“不吃”中子，加上出色的耐腐蚀性和耐高温性，
是核反应堆中核燃料包壳材料的理想选择
，既能抗高温耐腐蚀，又不吸收裂变产生的中子，保证链式反应持续稳定运行。
铪：“爱吃”中子，这一特性使它可以成为
核反应堆控制棒的核心材料
，通过放入、取出控制棒，可精准调控反应堆的裂变速率。
锆还凭借优异的耐腐蚀性能广泛应用于化工设备、海洋工程和人体植入材料等领域，而高密度高熔点的铪，则常被用于火箭发动机的喷嘴、航天器的热防护系统等场景。
锆用处很大，但分布不均，全球锆储量高度集中于澳大利亚，约占七成，而中国占比不足 1%。新疆拜城大型锆（铪）砂矿的发现
填补了国内区域超大型锆（铪）矿床找矿空白
，将有力提升我国锆（铪）矿资源保障能力。

title: 小鹏集团总裁王凤英：2027 年起，部分城市将设立 MONA 独立门店
content:
IT之家 10 月 31 日消息，据界面新闻 10 月 30 日报道，小鹏集团总裁王凤英在 2026 巴黎车展期间表示，从 2027 年开始，部分城市将设立 MONA 的独立门店。她还提到，未来“不排除 MONA 品牌独立的可能性”。
报道提到，一线渠道端已经出现动作。北京一家小鹏汽车门店销售人员对界面新闻表示，“小鹏和 MONA 应该会分开销售，MONA 会有独立门店。新出行 CEO 贺磊称，广州市海珠区一家商场已出现待入驻的“小鹏 MONA 销售中心”。
此外，小鹏内部的产品策略也在调整。小鹏近期将 F、D、I、G 四条产品线合并为 G、D 两条产品线，I、F 并入 G 产品线，MONA 继续独享 D 产品线。这项调整进一步区隔了 MONA 与小鹏主品牌的产品规划。
IT之家注意到，小鹏 MONA L05 于 10 月 29 日晚上市，官方指导价 14.48 万元起，首销限时价 13.98 万元起。MONA L05 是 MONA 系列第三款车型，也是该系列首款大五座 SUV，面向全球 65 个国家和地区适配开发。车身长宽高为 4870/1930/1636mm，轴距 2940mm。
此外，小鹏汽车于 10 月 27 日宣布 MONA L05 新产线首批 5,000 台下线，号称是“独立产线，全力保供”。

title: 市场监管总局批准发布 2 项生物芯片国家标准，时隔 15 年更新、行业术语有了“普通话”
content:
IT之家 10 月 31 日消息，据国家市场监管总局 10 月 30 日公告，市场监管总局（国家标准委）批准发布《生物芯片基本术语》《人体疾病易感 DNA 多态性检测微阵列芯片》2 项新版推荐性国家标准，将自 2027 年 2 月 1 日起实施。
《生物芯片基本术语》（GB/T 27990—2026）作为生物芯片领域的基础性标准，代替了实施十余年的 2011 年版，系统重构了行业概念体系。标准紧扣技术演进与产业需求，新增核酸检测芯片、免疫检测芯片、器官芯片等核心术语，并进一步完善了生物芯片、微阵列芯片、微流控芯片等基础定义的表述。内容覆盖基础术语、芯片探针、微阵列芯片分类、微流控芯片分类四大板块，全面囊括当前市场主流产品类型，将有效消除技术交流中的概念歧义，助力学术研究、产业协同与国际对接。
《人体疾病易感 DNA 多态性检测微阵列芯片》（GB/T 29889—2026）聚焦疾病易感 DNA 多态性检测场景，明确微阵列芯片可一次并行检测数十至数万个位点，并围绕全流程管控提出五大核心要求。该标准主要规定四方面内容：
- 一是规范血液、唾液、口腔黏膜、组织等样品采集、储运与预处理要求；
- 二是要求检测位点需经过不少于 500 人份中国人群研究验证；
- 三是规定位点检出率不低于 99%、准确率和重复率不低于 99.9%，并设置阴阳对照；
- 四是要求建立位点关联数据库、配备风险评估软件并出具标准化检测报告。
与旧版相比，新版不仅提高了位点验证样本量门槛，更将规范范围从单一产品技术要求延伸至检测样品、位点验证、产品应用与服务认可的全链条。
IT之家从公告了解到，该 2 项标准紧密配套、互为支撑，将有力规范人体疾病易感基因检测全过程，为生物芯片产品研发、质量评价、健康管理服务提供统一技术依据，进一步助推我国精准医学与健康管理产业规范、高质量发展。

title: 我国首次载人登月任务乘组计划由三人组成，两人着陆月球表面
content:
感谢IT之家网友
pzvincent
xxy171070
软媒新友2547452
10 月 31 日消息，第七届载人航天学术大会于今日（10 月 31 日）在北京航空航天大学举行，据《环球时报》报道，我国计划在 2030 年前实现中国人登陆月球，
将采用“两次发射，一次登月”的方式实现载人登月
中国载人航天工程副总设计师兼月球探测工程总设计师王翔在大会上介绍称，我国首次载人月球探测计划采用环月轨道对接飞行模式，采用两枚长征十号运载火箭，先将着陆器送往月球轨道，然后再发射载人飞船与着陆器实现交会对接，航天员进入着陆器并与载人飞船分离着陆月面，开展有关科学探测活动。
完成任务后，航天员乘坐着陆器从月面上升，在月球轨道上与载人飞船实现二次交会对接，航天员乘坐载人飞船返回地球。
王翔介绍称，我国首次载人月球探测任务乘组
，其中两人着陆月球表面。
综合IT之家此前报道，
中国登月服外观于 2024 年 9 月首次公布
，主要用于航天员执行月面出舱活动任务时的生命保障和作业支持，能够对月球表面的真空、高低温、月尘、辐射环境等复杂环境进行综合防护，着服航天员可以完成行走、攀爬、驾车、科考等月面出舱活动作业。
根据规划，2028 年至 2030 年间，我国将在文昌航天发射场密集执行 3 次无人绕月验证任务及 1 次载人登月任务，标志着中国载人航天工程正式从近地轨道迈向地月空间。
2026 年 10 月 31 日，第七届载人航天学术大会在北京开幕。来自载人航天相关领域的 800 余位专家学者齐聚一堂，以“智汇星河，数智赋能载人航天高质量发展”为主题，
聚焦载人航天领域前沿技术、工程实践与发展需求，交流前沿成果、深化学术研讨，为数智技术与载人航天工程深度融合、推动工程高质量发展汇聚智慧和力量
本届大会由中国载人航天工程办公室主办，中国载人航天工程运行与管理支持中心、北京航空航天大学共同承办，中国科学院空间应用工程与技术中心、北京航天飞行控制中心、中国航天员科研训练中心等单位协办。载人航天工程总体及各系统“两总”代表，工程有关参研参试单位、国内有关高校和科研机构的领导、专家、学者及大会论文作者等参加会议。
大会会期 2 天，设置开幕式、主旨报告和学术分会等环节。大会邀请 11 位院士、国内相关领域知名专家和航天员代表，
围绕空间站运行与应用、月球科学与探测、航天领域数字化等内容作主旨报告，分享最新研究成果与工程实践经验
学术分会设置载人航天共性技术、近地载人空间站、月球探测工程 3 个专题，共 15 个分论坛，着力打造航天领域前沿技术、科技成果、战略发展、应用转化等系列交流合作平台。大会共征集主题论文 364 篇，将为 15 名优秀论文作者颁发荣誉证书。

title: 把空气“冷冻”起来存电能：我国液态空气储能重大突破，全球最大规模、百分百国产
content:
10 月 31 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，
全球最大规模 60 兆瓦液态空气储能国家示范项目
成功并网发电，实现液态空气储能技术工程化、商业化落地的重大突破。
该液态空气储能项目位于青海省格尔木市，总规模 6 万千瓦，每天可助力 60 万度清洁能源消纳，
全年输电量约达 1.8 亿度，满足 3 万户家庭一年的用电需求
项目采用-194℃ 超低温深冷液化核心工艺，以空气作为工质，
在常压超低温条件下实现电能与冷能的存储与释放
，兼具大规模、长时效、长寿命等优势。
中国绿发储能公司总工程师季伟：
项目设备国产化率达到了百分之百
，储能功率和容量均居世界首位，多项核心指标达到世界领先水平。
项目在建设过程中，攻关研制出全球最大水平剖分式离心压缩机、单台流量最大液体膨胀机等一批首台套核心装备，打通从核心部件、系统集成到工程落地的全链条，实现“压缩 — 液化 — 存储 — 发电”全流程精准控制和“冷 — 热 — 电 — 气”多能流实时协调调度。
液态空气储能是一种长时储能新技术，不靠特殊矿洞、不靠化学电池，
依靠空气的液化与汽化完成能量转移
，适配我国广阔的新能源基地。
IT之家从报道了解到，项目采用零下 194 摄氏度超低温深冷液化工艺。工作原理通俗来说，就是在风电、光伏出力富余、电网负荷低谷时段，
用富余电力将空气冷却至零下 194℃ 液化
，以常压液态形式储存；到用电高峰，再把液态空气气化膨胀，驱动膨胀机组发电，实现“低谷存、高峰用”，完成电能跨时段转移。
液态空气储能以空气为循环工质，运行过程无污染物排放，不依赖特殊地形条件，选址灵活、循环寿命长、安全性高，适合新能源消纳、火电深度调峰、液化天然气冷能综合利用等场景，丰富了我国长时储能技术路线。

title: 梦舟载人飞船和揽月着陆器将首次飞行，我国载人登月任务最新进展公布

title: 科学家发现治疗 2 型糖尿病新靶点，找到胰岛素抵抗关键影响因素
content:
IT之家 10 月 31 日消息，据 scitechdaily 今日报道，一项临床试验发现，一种在 2 型糖尿病患者肌肉中异常高含量的蛋白质，可能干扰了身体对胰岛素的反应能力。
研究人员发现，在去除被称为 Miro1（Mitochondrial Rho GTPase1）的蛋白质后，在临床前模型中恢复了胰岛素反应性，这为治疗胰岛素抵抗提供了可能的新方法。
这项发表在 《自然 · 通讯》 上的研究还发现，有氧运动可以降低 2 型糖尿病患者的 Miro1 水平。
Miro1 位于线粒体的外膜上，这些结构负责产生细胞大部分可用能量。骨骼肌在调节血糖方面起着重要作用，因为它会根据胰岛素吸收血液中的葡萄糖。当肌肉对胰岛素产生抵抗时，血液中的葡萄糖被有效去除，这导致了与 2 型糖尿病相关的血糖升高。
为了调查 Miro1 的参与情况，科学家们考察了其在细胞、临床前模型以及 2 型糖尿病患者中的影响。实验显示，过量的 Miro1 会损害肌肉中的胰岛素反应，而去除该蛋白后，在临床前模型中这些效应得以逆转。
肌肉中的胰岛素抵抗是 2 型糖尿病的核心，其分子原因至今仍不明朗。这项经过多年努力的研究，科学家们终于将 Miro1 确定为关键答案的一部分。通过追踪 Miro1 从细胞到临床前模型再到患者的过程，科学家发现 Miro1 的积累会损害肌肉对胰岛素的反应。对于该领域来说，这是一个新的治疗靶点。
研究人员还进行了一项随机对照试验，参与者涉及肥胖和 2 型糖尿病患者。一组进行了有氧运动，另一组则接受了标准医疗护理。被分配进行锻炼的参与者肌肉中 Miro1 水平较低，同时胰岛素敏感性和线粒体能量产生有所改善。
IT之家提醒，尽管去除 Miro1 在实验模型中改善了胰岛素反应，但研究人员尚未确定针对该蛋白进行人类治疗的安全性或有效性。科学家们还需要探明 Miro1 如何促进胰岛素抵抗、调整其活性是否能改善血糖调节等诸多问题。
Kirwan 在美国路易斯安那州立大学彭宁顿生物医学研究中心工作期间领导了这项研究。此后，他被任命为俄克拉荷马大学健康哈罗德 · 哈姆糖尿病中心执行主任，将继续研究糖尿病的生物机制及潜在治疗方法。
该研究的第一作者 Elizabeth Heintz 曾在彭宁顿生物医学综合生理与分子医学实验室攻读博士生。

title: 马斯克公布 Neuralink 脑机新产品进展：第二款产品“盲视”只待监管批准
content:
IT之家 10 月 31 日消息，马斯克透露，Neuralink 第二款脑机接口设备 Blindsight（盲视）已完成工程研发，接下来只待监管部门放行。这款设备旨在帮助失明者以及从出生起就没有视觉的人获得视觉能力。不过，迄今尚无公开披露并得到确认的人体植入试验结果。
马斯克 30 日在 X 上发文称：“从工程研发的角度来说，设备已经准备就绪，只等监管部门批准。”
与 Neuralink 此前推出的首款植入设备不同，“盲视”并不是读取大脑活动并将信号传输出去，而是反过来向大脑输入信息。设备将摄像头获取的画面转换为信号，传递到大脑视觉皮层，试图绕过已经受损的眼睛和视神经，让使用者获得视觉信息。
2024 年 9 月，FDA 授予“盲视”突破性医疗器械认定，以加快审批审查。但这项认定既不代表 FDA 已经确认设备安全有效，也不意味着产品获得上市销售许可。“盲视”目前仍处于临床试验阶段。
马斯克今年 8 月曾透露，若获得监管批准，Neuralink 计划在未来 6 至 12 个月内开展人体植入。截至目前，公司没有公布“盲视”的人体试验结果。
动物试验方面，Neuralink 已开展长期测试，截至 2025 年年中，有一只猴子连续植入该设备已有三年。
除了 Blindsight，马斯克还介绍了 Neuralink 的首款产品 Telepathy（心灵感应）。这款设备可以让瘫痪患者通过脑信号操控电脑。“只需通过思考，就能与电脑或其他人进行高速交流。”
马斯克预计，未来几年，“心灵感应”的信息输出能力将远超人类最快的说话和打字速度。他还希望 Neuralink 未来能够将运动和感觉信号传递至四肢，让失去行动能力的患者重新使用双手，甚至恢复行走。

| Blindsight | 向大脑视觉皮层输入视觉信息 | 2024 年 9 月获得突破性医疗器械认定，尚未获准上市 | 尚无公开确认的人体试验结果 |

title: 鸿海董事长刘扬伟：预计未来数年攻下全球 AI 服务器半壁江山
content:
感谢IT之家网友
10 月 31 日消息，当地时间 30 日。据美国 CNBC 报道，鸿海计划进一步扩大 AI 服务器业务，并加大在美国的生产布局。董事长刘扬伟表示，AI 基础设施市场需求依然强劲，集团希望借此进一步提高市场份额。
刘扬伟在接受采访时透露，公司目前占据全球约 40% 的 AI 服务器市场份额，预计明年有望提高至约 45%，未来数年则
有机会达到 50%
长期以来，鸿海以代工组装苹果
闻名。近年来，AI 基础设施业务逐渐成为集团的重要增长引擎。
刘扬伟预计，未来三至五年，AI 基础设施业务将
贡献富士康 60% 至 65% 的营收
，不包括直接在本地硬件上运行人工智能和机器学习算法的端侧 AI 设备。
AI 基础设施订单持续增长，至少未来一年半的产能都已排满。目前订单主要来自 AI 模型开发商和云服务提供商，政府及企业客户尚未全面采用 AI 技术，但整体市场需求依然强劲。
在美国市场，鸿海也准备进一步扩大生产规模。刘扬伟表示，集团计划向供应链上游延伸，以便更好地满足美国市场的需求。
考虑到美国的制造成本较高，鸿海初期将
优先生产 AI 服务器机柜、数据中心设备等利润率较高的产品
。刘扬伟认为，随着美国本土生产规模扩大，制造成本最终也有望随之下降。通过此次扩张，公司希望进一步巩固在 AI 基础设施供应链中的地位，业务布局将从服务器、机柜
延伸至整座数据中心和算力服务
不过，刘扬伟也提醒，AI 市场增长并不意味着企业可以不计成本地扩大投资。他强调必须严格控制投资规模，直言“过度投资会毁掉公司”。
随着 AI 业务发展，公司每年在 AI 领域的投入预计会
超过原定的 30 亿至 50 亿美元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 200.09 亿至 333.48 亿元人民币）
，具体取决于垂直整合的推进程度。
对于大客户削减 AI 支出可能带来的影响，刘扬伟认为，单一客户需求下降，可以通过其他业务领域的增长予以弥补。但如果整个行业的需求都出现下滑，鸿海乃至整个 AI 供应链都将面临更大的挑战。

Supply Chain Digital explores the top five stories from the past week, including people moves, robotics deployment and sustainability initiatives
GXO to Deploy Digit 5 Robots in E-Commerce Fulfilment Sites
GXO Logistics is expanding its partnership with Agility Robotics to deploy Digit humanoid robots at two additional US e-commerce fulfilment sites. The deployments are expected to begin in early 2027 at facilities in Statesville, North Carolina, and Lebanon, Tennessee. GXO will initially use Digit 4 units before transitioning to Digit 5 robots when the newer series becomes commercially available.
GXO Logistics has been an early adopter of robotics technology in its logistics operations. The agreement expands on the companies’ multi-year agreement in 2024 to deploy Agility Robotics’ Digit humanoid robots in a live GXO warehouse environment in Flowery Branch, Georgia. Digit units have moved more than 100,000 totes at the Flowery Branch facility, demonstrating the technology’s ability to perform repetitive material-handling tasks reliably in an active logistics environment.
Fabian Köhler, will become Group CEO at Culina Group Limited. Credit: LinkedIn
Culina Announces New CEO After Brand Unification
Culina Group has announced that current Chief Executive Officer Liam McElroy will be succeeded by Fabian Koehler, the Deputy CEO, with effect from 1 February 2027.
The announcement of the executive appointment follows shortly after Culina group announced that it was unifying its subsidiaries under a single brand: Culina.
The announcement in mid October affected established logistics brand names including Culina Logistics, IPS, Stobart, Great Bear, Fowler Welch, Warrens, CML, Stobart Europe, IRF and iForce.
Culina will operate through five specialist divisions: Chilled & Fresh Logistics, Contract Logistics, Transport Logistics, Integrated Packing Services and International Logistics.
WCS & Hershey: Establishing Sustainable Cocoa Supply Chains
The Hershey Company has committed US$2.5m to the Wildlife Conservation Society as part of a four-year project in Cross River State, Nigeria. The partnership aims to
strengthen supply chain resilience
in a region where more than 100,000 households depend on cocoa farming for their livelihoods.
According to the Wildlife Conservation Society, the area contributes almost one third of Nigeria's cocoa exports.
The Cross River State contains Nigeria's largest remaining rainforest and serves as the country's most important cocoa-producing region. This concentration of production makes the region strategically important for maintaining stable cocoa supply chains.
Leidos will deploy AI-driven automation, cloud technology and modern software practices across the Pentagon’s ELMS under a potential US$95m, five-year contract from the DLA. Credit: Getty
Leidos Brings AI to Pentagon Asset Management
Leidos will deploy AI-driven automation, cloud technology and modern software practices across the Pentagon’s Enterprise Logistics Management System (ELMS) under a potential US$95m, five-year contract from the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA).
ELMS is used by more than 50 government agencies to manage over 80 million items of government property valued at more than US$140bn. The system supports asset accountability throughout the property lifecycle and underpins the logistics network that helps keep US warfighters equipped and ready.
The contract extends Leidos’ support for ELMS and its predecessor, the Defense Property Accountability System, to more than 21 years. The agreement includes one base year and four option years, running through August 2031.
ImportGenius offers a source of customs and bill-of-lading information covering more than 25 countries, with data sourced from government customs agencies and other public trade records. Credit: ImportGenius
ImportGenius: AI, Trade Intelligence and Supply Chain Risk
The pressures for supply chain leaders to identify potential supply chain risks, whether those are from
geopolitical
disruption or shifts in the competitiveness of individual suppliers, have never been greater than at present.
Data has become an increasingly important element of competitive advantage. But supply chain leaders understand that the strength of the data they are relying on to identify
disruption
, assess competitors and explain strategic decisions is a key variable.
ImportGenius is a supplier of international trade and supply chain intelligence. Through advanced data management technologies, the firm is able to help its clients make sense of hundreds of millions of shipping manifests and customs records from government agencies and private companies around the world.
Artificial intelligence
can be used to improve trade data quality, support supplier discovery, improve shipment analytics and sharpen supply chain mapping. However, the successful application of AI relies on its use as a support for human decision-making, rather than when it operates without controls.

title: GAC launches battery production in Thailand - electrive.com
content:
Inpow Battery Technology, the battery division of Chinese automaker GAC, has started production at a new plant in Thailand. This expands the group's local manufacturing footprint in Southeast Asia.
Image: Inpow
Inpow Battery Technology officially began production at its new battery plant in Thailand on 29 October. The facility is located east of Bangkok, specifically in Si Racha, Chonburi Province. Inpow is responsible for battery production within the GAC Group. The start of production marks another step in the Chinese conglomerate’s expansion of local supply chains in Southeast Asia.
The plant’s opening coincides with another milestone for Inpow: as the company recently announced, its cumulative global production has now reached 300,000 battery packs. These batteries are already used in a range of electric models from the GAC Aion brand, including the i60, N60 and UT.
With the new site in Thailand, GAC can localise battery production closer to its vehicle manufacturing operations. The new battery plant is likely to play a significant role in the further development of the Southeast Asian market. Local production can shorten transport routes and reduce dependence on supplies from China.
GAC Aion already produces locally
This step builds on GAC’s existing expansion in Thailand. As early as July 2024, GAC Aion
opened its own vehicle plant in the Southeast Asian country
. The location is part of the group’s strategy to use Thailand as a production and distribution base for further markets in the region.
With the additional battery plant, an important part of the value chain is now also being localised. The combination of vehicle and battery production could help GAC strengthen its competitive position against other Chinese manufacturers that are also increasingly investing in Southeast Asia.
Thailand is considered one of the most important automotive hubs in Southeast Asia and has been working for several years to align its industry more closely with electric vehicles. The government is promoting the establishment of corresponding production capacities and aims to position the country as a regional hub for electromobility.

title: 10 massive Battery storage projects around the world
content: Storing electricity at the scale of several gigawatt-hours is becoming a reality for power grids around the world.From a solar-powered development in Abu Dhabi to battery installations across Saudi Arabia, these projects are designed to store electricity and supply it when it is needed.The following list includes individual facilities, multi-site programs, and phased developments, with capacities reflecting their published scope.Some are already operating, others remain under development, and Moss Landing illustrates why historical capacity must be distinguished from what a facility can deliver today.1. Masdar–EWEC round-the-clock project, UAE -19 GWhMasdarAbu Dhabi’s Masdar–EWEC development combines a 5.2-gigawatt solar plant with 19 gigawatt-hours of battery storage. The project is designed to deliver 1 gigawatt of renewable electricity around the clock, extending solar power delivery beyond daylight hours.Masdar laid the foundation for the project in October 2025, with operations targeted for 2027. Its design includes grid-forming technology, black-start capability, and forecasting and dispatch systems to coordinate electricity generation, storage, and delivery.2. SEC–BYD battery storage program, Saudi Arabia – 12.5 GWhBYD announced a 12.5-gigawatt-hour energy storage contract with Saudi Electricity Company in February 2025.The agreement covers multiple grid-scale projects and brings BYD’s combined Saudi cooperation with the utility to 15.1 gigawatt-hours, including an earlier 2.6-gigawatt-hour delivery.MEED identifies the program as five facilities with a combined power rating of 2.5 gigawatts, built with Alfanar as the engineering, procurement, and construction contractor.Equipment supplier NR Electric reported that SEC’s five-region, 2.5-gigawatt storage project completed its grid-connected charging and discharging tests on May 27, 2026, marking commissioning.3. Oasis de Atacama, Chile – 14.1 GWh (overall platform)Grenergy’s Oasis de Atacama is a phased solar and battery storage development in Chile. Although earlier plans set its storage capacity at about 11 gigawatt-hours, the company’s September 2026 announcement raised the overall platform a capacity to 14.1 gigawatt-hours.That figure reflects the wider development, with individual phases coming online separately.Grenergy confirmed in September 2026 that Gabriela, the fourth phase, was operational with 272 megawatts of solar generation and 1,100 megawatt-hours of battery storage.4. Najran, Khamis Mushait, and Madaya storage program, Saudi Arabia – 7.8 GWhSaudi Arabia’s 7.8-gigawatt-hour storage deployment spans three sites at Najran, Khamis Mushait, and Madaya. Sungrow supplied more than 1,500 PowerTitan 2.0 systems and announced grid connection completion in December 2025.The equipment integrates batteries, power conversion systems, medium-voltage transformers, and switching equipment into preassembled units. Sungrow says factory testing and preassembly reduced on-site installation work, while a local service team supported installation, commissioning, and grid connection.5. Envision Jingyi Chagan Hada, China – 4 GWhThe Envision Jingyi Chagan Hada Energy Storage Power Station in Inner Mongolia has a reported capacity of 4 gigawatt-hours. It connected to the grid in late December 2025, forming part of Envision’s wider 12.8-gigawatt-hour regional storage cluster.According to the Sustainable Markets Initiative’s project showcase, the station passed the grid’s three-charge, three-discharge verification in a single attempt.Its control system combines forecasting, dispatch, and electricity-market trading, coordinating how stored energy is managed and sold.6. Edwards & Sanborn, USA – 3.287 GWhCalifornia’s Edwards & Sanborn project combines solar generation with 3.287 gigawatt-hours of battery storage. Developer Terra-Gen and contractor Mortenson announced substantial completion of the Kern County development in January 2024.The installation spans more than 4,600 acres, with part of the project on Edwards Air Force Base.Mortenson identifies LG Chem, Samsung, and BYD as battery suppliers, while the project serves customers including California utilities, the city of San Jose, and Starbucks.7. Moss Landing, USA – 3 GWh (historical installed capacity)Wikimedia CommonsVistra’s Moss Landing Energy Storage Facility reached 750 megawatts and 3,000 megawatt-hours of installed capacity after its third expansion entered commercial operation in June 2023.That expansion added 350 megawatts and 1,400 megawatt-hours, establishing the California site as a major early example of multi-gigawatt-hour battery storage.Its historical capacity requires qualification following the January 2025 fire at the 300-megawatt facility.EPA confirms that the affected building has had no active battery storage operations since that incident, while Vistra subsequently decided not to return the separate 100-megawatt facility to service.8. Collie Battery, Australia – 2.24 GWhCollie BatteryNeoen’s Collie Battery in Western Australia has a combined capacity of 560 megawatts and 2,240 megawatt-hours. The development comprises a 219-megawatt first stage and a 341-megawatt second stage; the company’s October 2025 update said both are operational.The service addresses electricity reliability risks associated with coal-plant retirements, growing rooftop solar generation, and demand on Western Australia’s South-West Interconnected System.9. Bisha BESS, Saudi Arabia – 2 GWhThe Bisha battery storage facility in Saudi Arabia’s Aseer province is rated at 500 megawatts and 2,000 megawatt-hours.Contractor Alfanar describes the delivered installation as a four-hour system that stores electricity during low-demand periods for redistribution when demand rises.Bisha has also demonstrated a capability needed after a major grid outage: black start, or restoring power without relying on an already energized network.NR Electric reported a successful black-start test in February 2026 using its integrated power conversion, power management, and energy management systems.10. Huadian Xinjiang Kashgar, China – 2 GWh (first phase)The first phase of Huadian’s Kashgar energy storage project in Xinjiang has a capacity of 500 megawatts and 2,000 megawatt-hours.A Huadian Xinjiang account published by the China Energy Storage Alliance confirms that the first storage block entered grid-connected operation in July 2025.The installation uses 100 lithium iron phosphate storage units and combines grid-forming and conventional storage configurations, each accounting for half its capacity.State Grid Kashgar said the project supports renewable electricity use and grid stability in a region where photovoltaic generation represents a substantial share of installed power capacity.ConclusionThese projects show how battery storage is expanding from individual installations to multi-site programs measured in gigawatt-hours.Their engineering challenges extend beyond capacity to grid integration, reliable operation, and safety. As more facilities enter service, how consistently they store and deliver electricity will matter as much as their size.

title: 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles approved as US boosts Ukraine defense
content: Lockheed Martin, a major defense supplier, is likely to supply Ukraine with 500 Patriot air defense interceptor missiles after the US State Department approved the potential sale Friday, October 30.​According to the press statement, the approval came following a request from the government of Ukraine to purchase Patriot Advanced Capability-3 (PAC-3) Missile Segment Enhancement (MSE) missiles to improve its integrated air and missile defense capabilities.​Patriot’s PAC-3 MSE variant, manufactured by Lockheed Martin, is one of the most advanced, high-velocity surface-to-air missile interceptors capable of shooting down incoming ballistic missiles. Ukraine, allies backs purchase​The estimated cost of purchase for these 500 missiles is estimated at $2.1 billion. Ukrainian national funds financed by the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan and donations from allies including Canada, Germany and Norway through the US JUMPSTART program will be used to make the purchase, the State Department said. No U.S. funds will be used to make the purchase, the statement added.​Under the agreement, the company will supply PAC-3 MSE classified and unclassified spare parts and other related logistics and program support elements.​ However, the U.S. government did not comment on when the Ukrainian military will receive these crucial defensive weapons.​Lockheed Martin, the principal contractor for the newly approved missile sale, is already in talks with allied nations to establish PAC-3 production outside the US, as the demand for the interceptor surges globally.​By 2030, the company plans to expand its annual production capacity, up from 600 missiles to 2000, while investing in 20 facilities on the American soil.​PAC3 Edge to combat hypersonic weaponsIn addition to greenlighting the sale of 500 Patriot air missiles to Ukraine, the U.S. Army also awarded a nearly $1.1 billion contract to Lockheed Martin to develop PAC-3 Edge, an advanced interceptor technology. The new combat technology is expected to expand air- and missile-defense coverage against advanced threats, including hypersonic weapons. These missiles, with greater engagement range and altitude, are designed to replace PAC-3 MSE and THAAD.​Built on combat-proven PAC-3 MSE, PAC-3 Edge will have a new seeker, improved propulsion, and upgraded controls. These engineering changes are intended to improve precision, maneuverability, and performance at greater ranges and altitudes, a company official said.​The seeker of the advanced missile system is tasked with tracking targets during the engagement, while the propulsion determines the energy available along the flight path, and control systems enable the missile to adjust its trajectory. The combined effectiveness of these systems will determine if PAC-3 Edge can meet its proposed engagement envelope against maneuvering targets, noted the company officials.​However, no official announcements provided a number for PAC-3 Edge’s interception ranges, altitude limits, seeker operating characteristics, or demonstrated performance against representative hypersonic targets.​The latest development award marks progress toward expanding the defensive capability. However, whether PAC-3 Edge delivers the proposed improvement against advanced missile and hypersonic threats will depend on the results of its development, testing, and integration program.​

title: Aging warships to get Western eyes to improve naval gun targeting with modern tech
content: The UK’s Chess Dynamics has landed a £3 million ($4 million) contract to supply its SeaEagle fire control system to the Indonesian Navy. Delivered in cooperation with Indonesia’s state-owned PT Len Industri, SeaEagle will be installed on two Bung Tomo -class light corvettes for the Indonesian Navy (TNI AL). These systems will offer the ships greatly improved capability to identify, track, and engage targets (including aerial targets) using their naval guns. To this end, it is not a new offensive capability, but rather an upgrade to existing optics. The SeaEagle Fire Control Electro-Optical (FCEO) is a highly sophisticated, stabilized camera and targeting system. This kind of electro-optical system uses sensors like visible-light cameras and thermal imagers. Depending on the design, such systems can also come with laser rangefinders. Such systems are able to identify and acquire targets like vessels and other objects even in low-light conditions. Giving old seadogs new eyes These maritime surveillance systems are able to track moving objects by keeping their sensors trained on a target despite the ship rolling, pitching, and  changing directions. The system is also able to calculate targeting information like bearing, elevation, and range that can be fed to the ship’s 76 mm OTO Melara guns. Importantly, SeaEagle will interface with the ships’ existing Thales TACTICOS Combat Management System. What’s more, SeaEagle’s cameras can operate passively, meaning they don’t need to transmit detectable signals like radar. This makes the system particularly useful for discreet target tracking, although its laser rangefinder does emit detectable pulses when used. This is very interesting, as using radar can announce its presence. Electro-optical tracking can be considerably more discreet, although lasers are detectable and the system remains limited by visibility and atmospheric conditions. The main advantage of this for the Indonesian Navy is that their ships will effectively be able to upgrade gun capability without replacing the guns wholesale. It will also enable the Indonesian Navy to beef up parts of its roster without commissioning new vessels. The three Bung Tomo -class warships are British-built vessels that Indonesia acquired after their original customer, Brunei, declined to take delivery. Being corvettes, they are relatively small warships, but still capable of carrying out significant naval operations. So, rather than buying entirely new vessels, Indonesia is modernising its electronics, sensors and command systems. According to reports, one, the KRI Usman Harun (359), already has SeaEagle installed. Part of a wider upgrade package The KRI Bung Tomo ( 357) and KRI John Lie (358) will now be upgraded under this new contract. According to reports, this forms part of a larger modernization program for the Indonesian Navy . Other upgrades will include SMART-S Mk2 radar system, STIR EO Mk2 fire controls, and Vigile Mk2 R-ESM designed to detect and analyze electromagnetic signals emitted by other platforms. There is overlap in the capabilities of some of these, but this is by design. They not only complement each other, but also provide a level of redundancy, which is critically important for modern warships . It is worth noting that the modernisation of KRI Usman Harun was originally expected to be completed by the end of 2023. However, the work has taken considerably longer than anticipated, highlighting the potential complexity of integrating modern systems into ageing warships

title: Chery Tiggo 2 gets 0 Stars in Latin NCAP Crash Test
content: Chinese automaker Chery is facing renewed questions about vehicle safety after its Tiggo 2 compact SUV received a zero-star rating in the latest Latin NCAP crash tests. The assessment found an unstable body structure and footwell during frontal impact, poor protection for the driver’s chest and a fire risk that contributed to the vehicle scoring zero for adult occupant protection.The results also gave the Tiggo 2 zero points for child occupant protection. The SUV, sold in different markets as the Tiggo 2 Pro, Tiggo 2 Pro Max and Chirey Tiggo 2, comes with four airbags and electronic stability control as standard. It nevertheless achieved just 48.89 percent for pedestrian protection and 45.45 percent for safety assistance systems. The result adds to scrutiny of Chery’s quality controls as the company expands its presence in overseas markets, including Latin America and Southeast Asia.Unstable structure, fire risk Latin NCAP evaluated the Tiggo 2 through frontal and side-impact tests, whiplash assessments, pedestrian protection tests and evaluations of its electronic stability control and emergency maneuvering performance.During the frontal impact, the vehicle’s body structure and footwell area were both rated as unstable. The driver’s chest showed poor protection, with high compression recorded during the collision. Latin NCAP also identified a fire risk during the test, which contributed to the zero-point result for adult occupant protection.The absence of standard side head-protection airbags meant the vehicle was not subjected to the side pole impact test, resulting in an additional penalty. The assessment also found that the rear seats lacked seatbelt pretensioners and load limiters, while the vehicle could not demonstrate adequate protection for a smaller adult passenger in the second row.Child occupant protection was equally concerning, with Latin NCAP awarding the Tiggo 2 zero points after identifying problems in both dynamic crash testing and child restraint system installation. The assessment recorded high forces on the head and neck of the 10-year-old test dummy during frontal and side impacts, while the 3-year-old dummy faced head exposure and a risk of ejection in the side-impact test.Previous quality lapsesAccording to Alejandro Furas, Latin NCAP’s secretary general, the result puts Chery in the spotlight for offering low safety performance in a popular vehicle segment. The organization also argued that mandatory safety labelling based on independent crash-test results could help consumers make better-informed purchasing decisions.The crash-test result comes weeks after Chery encountered another quality issue in Malaysia, where an Omoda 5 experienced a rear axle assembly separation earlier in October. The incident prompted Malaysia’s Road Transport Department to temporarily suspend the model’s Vehicle Type Approval, halting new registrations while the issue was addressed.Chery subsequently initiated a recall covering 8,878 Omoda 5 C and H variants. Chairman and president Yin Tongyue also apologized for the quality concerns during the World Intelligent Connected Vehicles Conference on October 21, saying the company needed to establish itself in overseas markets rather than pursue short-term gains.The incidents involve different vehicle models and separate technical problems, but they come at a time when Chinese automakers are expanding rapidly beyond their domestic market. Chery has exported vehicles to more than 80 countries and regions, and the Tiggo 2 is among its entry-level models aimed at markets across Southeast Asia, Latin America and the Middle East.

title: China's Humvee-like launcher could pack 12 ready-to-fire missiles
content: China’s short-range air defense system could be getting a significant upgrade, with reports suggesting its 4×4 launcher vehicle may soon carry three times as many ready-to-fire missiles.The speculation follows a social media post featuring images and video of what appears to be an updated version of China’s Yitian-L short-range air defense system on the move.Missile launch capacity tripledThe redesigned launcher was seen carrying two six-round missile packs instead of the four individual missile canisters used on earlier versions. As before, the launcher is mounted on the Dongfeng Mengshi 4×4, China’s equivalent of the Humvee, but now features two six-tube launch packs on the vehicle’s roof.The vehicle was photographed while being transported, although it remains unclear where and when the images were taken.It is also unknown whether the vehicle belongs to the Chinese military or represents an export variant. NORINCO, the state-owned defense manufacturer that builds the Yitian family of air defense systems, has not commented on the reported upgrade.“China knows its priority is building the Yitian-L air defense system for its people, not war,” the social media user wrote alongside the video of the Chinese Humvee.The Yitian system is designed to protect troops and fixed sites against low-flying helicopters, drones, and cruise missiles. In its current configuration, the lightweight Yitian-L carries four TY-90 infrared-guided missiles and a foldable 3D X-band radar mounted on the roof. NORINCO claims the radar can detect targets up to 11 miles (18 km) away. The TY-90 missiles have an engagement range of 500 m to 3.7 miles (6 km) and can intercept targets at altitudes of up to 2.48 miles (4 km). The system is operated by a two-person crew using a joystick-controlled digital console from inside the vehicle.Could tackle drone swarmsIt is also unclear whether the additional missiles are standard TY-90s or a smaller derivative. The TY-90 was originally developed as a short-range air-to-air missile for Chinese helicopters before being adapted for ground launch with a passive infrared guidance system that tracks targets using their heat signatures. Because the missiles are fire-and-forget weapons, the launcher does not need to continuously illuminate the target, helping reduce the chances of revealing the vehicle’s position during combat. The available images also do not show whether the upgraded Yitian-L retains the same radar and fire-control system or whether the increased missile load affects its range or performance.A launcher carrying 12 missiles could help address a challenge highlighted in recent conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East, where swarms of small drones can rapidly exhaust four-missile launchers. The original Yitian and the newer Yitian II, both mounted on armored personnel carriers, carry eight TY-90 missiles each. If confirmed, a 12-round Yitian-L would exceed the missile capacity of either heavier variant.So far, the Yitian-L has primarily been marketed as an export product.

title: Farthest human-made object in space loses contact, goes nearly one light-day away from Earth
content: NASA briefly lost contact with Voyager 1 in mid-October after the nearly 50-year-old spacecraft stopped transmitting a detectable radio signal during two scheduled communications attempts. The signal returned on October 20, but engineers are still investigating what caused the interruption. The incident comes just weeks before Voyager 1 is expected to become the first human-made object to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, a point at which radio messages will take a full 24 hours to travel in either direction. NASA’s Deep Space Network, a global system of large radio antennas used to communicate with distant spacecraft, failed to detect Voyager 1’s signal on October 18 and 19. The probe is now approximately 16 billion miles (24 billion kilometers) from Earth. Communication resumed on October 20, about 48 hours after the interruption began. NASA says the team has maintained contact with the spacecraft since then. An automatic safety response may hold the clue Engineers are still trying to determine what triggered the communications loss. However, NASA has established that one group of Voyager 1’s thrusters went offline during the incident, prompting its backup thrusters to switch on automatically. The spacecraft is programmed to respond this way when its onboard computers detect a potential problem with the active thrusters. This automated protection system can place the probe in a stable, safe configuration and pause normal operations while engineers investigate. The spacecraft’s signal returned before the team sent commands to troubleshoot the issue from Earth. “This is the first time we’ve seen the spacecraft do something like this, but we are also at a point in the mission where we have to expect the unexpected,” said Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory. “We’re relieved to be back in contact with Voyager 1 and are eager to understand what happened.” The incident is another reminder of the challenges of operating spacecraft launched nearly half a century ago, especially as their onboard power supplies continue to weaken. NASA is trying to squeeze more life out of Voyager 1 Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, rely on radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs), which convert heat from decaying plutonium into electricity. As the radioactive material decays, the spacecraft lose about four watts of electrical power each year. To keep the probes operating, engineers have gradually switched off instruments and other systems that are no longer essential to their missions. In September, the Voyager team completed a major power-saving effort on Voyager 1, nicknamed the “Big Bang.” Engineers simultaneously switched off three devices and activated lower-power alternatives, helping reduce energy consumption while maintaining the spacecraft’s thermal balance. The procedure was designed to extend the operating life of Voyager 1’s remaining science instruments. Without the changes, NASA estimated that it would have needed to shut down another instrument as early as summer 2027. Both spacecraft are now traveling through interstellar space, beyond the heliosphere, which is the enormous bubble of particles and magnetic fields generated by the Sun. They remain the only spacecraft to have directly studied this region. A 24-hour wait for a message from Earth Voyager 1 is approaching another remarkable milestone . On November 18, 2026, NASA expects the spacecraft to reach a distance of 16.094 billion miles (25.902 billion kilometers) from Earth, equivalent to one light-day. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours. Since radio signals travel at the speed of light, reaching Voyager 1 will then take an entire day. A response from the spacecraft will require another day to return. That means a simple exchange with the probe will take roughly 48 hours, even if everything works as expected. Voyager 1 is currently traveling at approximately 38,000 mph (61,155 kph). Launched in September 1977, it has become the most distant human-made object from Earth, having traveled far beyond the planets it was originally sent to explore. The one-light-day milestone will not change the spacecraft’s surroundings or operations. But it will offer a striking measure of how far humanity’s most distant explorer has traveled and how long its signals must journey to reach home.

title: Fish switch leaders 2.8 times a second to stay in sync, reveals a virtual reality study
content: Schooling fish switched the neighbor guiding their movements about 2.8 times a second in a virtual reality experiment, offering new insight into how they stay in sync. To investigate coordinated movements in fish, researchers chose the rummy-nose tetras ( Hemigrammus rhodostomus ) for the study, a species known for its schooling behavior. Using a closed-loop virtual reality system, real tetras interacted with digital fish that the researchers could control. The projector cast these images of virtual fish on the walls of a 52.2-centimeter bowl containing 15 liters of water. A depth camera tracked the real fish’s movement in three dimensions. “Collective motion in animal groups emerges from local interactions, yet how individuals select and integrate social information remains poorly understood,” the researchers said. Investigating schooling behavior Researchers programmed virtual fish to respond to their one, two, or four most influential neighbors. They conducted eight one-hour experiments for each setup. The team compared swimming speeds , distances between individuals, alignment, spatial organization, and turning behavior. They found that coordination increased when the virtual fish responded to more neighbors, the researchers stated in the study. “Groups became more cohesive, fish trajectories became smoother, and departures of the real fish from the virtual subgroup became less frequent.” Although the virtual schools became more cohesive when the programmed fish responded to more neighbors, however analyses showed the real fish behaved as if it primarily tracked a single influential neighbor. “The turning statistics provide a clear behavioral indicator that the dynamics of the real fish are best explained when it responds to a single most influential neighbor.” And this neighbor wasn’t always the closest fish either. Influential neighbors switch as they swim The most influential neighbor changed as the fish moved in sync. Researchers recorded an average switching frequency of about 2.8 times per second. Roughly 40 changes occurred between two consecutive spontaneous U-turns. “…Influential-neighbor switching reflects the continuous spatial reorganization of the group rather than periods of sustained leadership by particular individuals.” Fish coordinate their movements through changing interactions rather than relying on one leader. “Social influence is continuously redistributed as individuals move relative to one another, generating a rapidly evolving interaction network that nevertheless supports robust collective coordination,” the researchers said . Unlike the previous perspective, coordination doesn’t necessarily require integrating information from many neighbors simultaneously. Limitations of virtual reality The researchers acknowledged limitations in their experimental approach. Although the virtual fish responded visually to the movements of the real fish, they did not generate water movements or pressure disturbances. Researchers explained that fish are known to rely on multiple sensory pathways, such as vision, hydrodynamic cues, and pressure sensing through the lateral line system when coordinating their movements within schools. However, in the virtual-reality set up, the digital fish could only be perceived visually because they don’t generate water movements and pressure disturbances, which would need to be addressed in later experiments. In the future, the team would like to conduct their experiment on larger groups with the missing conditions built into the model. The results suggest the fish coordinated through continuously changing interactions rather than following a fixed leader. The research findings were published in PRX Life .

title: Keeping homes powered in a blackout: 2 battery options compared
content: A blackout forces households to decide what needs electricity first: the refrigerator, a few lights, or the heating system. A home battery and a portable power station can both supply stored energy, but they differ in how they deliver it and how much installation they require.For households choosing backup power, the decision comes down to which appliances must run, how long outages typically last, and whether the system needs to work automatically. A portable station can suit selected devices, while an installed home battery can support circuits throughout the house, depending on its configuration.How the two systems deliver backup powerA home battery connects to the household electrical system through an inverter and associated control equipment. In a backup-capable installation, that equipment disconnects the home from the grid during an outage and supplies designated circuits from the battery. Depending on system design, coverage can include selected essential loads or the entire home. A portable power station packages battery storage, an inverter, and outlets into a unit that supplies appliances plugged directly into it. This makes it useful for powering individual devices without installing a permanent battery system.The distinction is becoming less rigid, however. Some larger portable stations support expansion batteries and can connect to household circuits through compatible transfer equipment. Buyers therefore need to compare the actual configuration. A portable unit connected to a home panel involves different equipment and installation requirements from one used simply to charge phones.Capacity determines runtime, while output limits appliancesTwo specifications matter: energy capacity and power output. Capacity, measured in watt-hours or kilowatt-hours, indicates how much energy the battery can store. Output, measured in watts or kilowatts, determines how much load equipment can operate simultaneously.California’s Air Resources Board emphasizes that backup batteries must be sized for both demand and runtime.Consider a simplified example: a battery delivering 1 kilowatt-hour (1,000 watt-hours) to appliances could support a constant 100-watt load for 10 hours. Actual runtime depends on conversion losses, the available charge, and how appliances cycle.Starting demand also matters. A refrigerator or pump may briefly require more power when their motor starts. Check the backup system’s continuous and surge ratings against the appliances it must operate.A larger battery does not automatically mean every appliance can run together. Tesla advises Powerwall owners to manage high-consumption equipment during outages because combined demand can exceed the system’s power rating. Reducing those loads also extends runtime.Which option makes more sense?For a renter or a household covering occasional short outages, a portable station is a practical starting point when the priority is a few essential plug-in appliances. Compare its purchase price, usable capacity, output, weight, and charging options.An installed home battery deserves closer consideration when automatic backup and hardwired appliances are priorities. Compare complete installed quotes, including electrical work and backup controls, rather than battery prices alone.For extended blackouts, recharging becomes decisive. Both options eventually exhaust their stored energy unless another source replenishes it. Compatible solar panels can help, but production depends on sunlight and system capabilities.Existing rooftop solar does not automatically provide power during blackouts. The US Department of Energy explains that conventional grid-connected solar generally shuts down during outages; continued operation requires an appropriately configured inverter and storage system.Start with an appliance list and a realistic outage duration. If a few outlets cover those needs, portability may be sufficient. If the requirement extends to automatic circuit-level backup, an installed system may justify the additional work.

title: Kongsberg lands contract boost to expand underwater drone capabilities
content: Kongsberg Gruppen ASA will supply autonomous underwater vehicles and associated components under a $54 million contract modification from the Department of War Innovation Unit (DIU), extending its collaboration with the agency and the US Navy. The contract modifies an existing Prototype Other Transaction Agreement, with deliveries of a broad range of autonomous underwater vehicles accounting for most of its value. The company did not identify the vehicle models, quantities, delivery schedule or specific missions covered by the modification. The agreement adds to a year in which Kongsberg has signed AUV contracts worth NOK 1.7 billion ($184.6 million USD) across defense and commercial markets. The company said the latest contract supports its ambition to expand in undersea warfare. Expanded underwater deliveries The modification covers both autonomous vehicles and associated underwater capability components. Kongsberg did not provide a breakdown of the contract’s value between those categories or detail how the components would support the vehicles. The announcement identifies the delivery of underwater capabilities as the main driver of the modification. Its reference to a broad range of AUVs leaves the precise mix of platforms undisclosed. “This contract continues our collaboration with DIU and the US Navy and reflects confidence in KONGSBERG’s autonomous underwater technology. We remain focused on delivering reliable systems for demanding operational environments,” said CEO Eirik Lie. “It also demonstrates the value of our dual-use portfolio in delivering defense capabilities and further strengthens our position as a technology and defense company,” he added. Lie’s comments place the contract within the company’s existing relationship with its defense customers. He also highlighted the role of a portfolio serving both military and commercial requirements in supporting defense capability deliveries. Defense and commercial demand Kongsberg has more than 30 years of experience in autonomous underwater vehicles . It develops and delivers large AUV systems for defense and commercial customers worldwide, alongside its work on systems adapted for defense missions. Camilla Kiss, executive vice president of Kongsberg and president of its Discovery division, said the latest contract reflected continuing demand across both markets. “Autonomous underwater systems are a core part of KONGSBERG’s technology portfolio. So far in 2026, we have signed AUV contracts worth a total of NOK 1.7 billion across all markets. This progress supports our strategic ambition to grow in undersea warfare and strengthens the foundation for continued development,” she said . The NOK 1.7 billion figure covers contracts across all markets. It represents the broader AUV business described by Kiss, rather than the value of the DIU modification alone. AI and onboard processing Kiss also pointed to artificial intelligence, edge processing and autonomy as technologies changing what underwater platforms can undertake. Her comments described the direction of development across the company’s underwater portfolio; the announcement did not specify which technologies or configurations would be included in the latest deliveries. “Advances in artificial intelligence, edge processing and autonomy are enabling platforms to undertake increasingly complex missions with greater persistence and operational effectiveness. We are at the forefront of this development,” Kiss said. Kongsberg linked these advances to its continued development of autonomous underwater capabilities for defense and commercial customers.

title: NASA’s Swift telescope to fall back to Earth after 21 years in orbit
content: After more than 21 years watching some of the universe’s most violent events, NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory has reached the end of its mission. The spacecraft is expected to re-enter Earth’s atmosphere in the coming weeks, but its scientific legacy is far from over. Researchers will continue mining its enormous archive of observations for years, potentially uncovering discoveries long after the telescope itself is gone.NASA announced on October 23 that Swift had ended science operations after its orbit dropped too low for the spacecraft to reliably point its telescopes at astronomical targets. Its final observation took place on October 20, when it was orbiting approximately 171 miles (275 kilometers) above Earth.The observatory was originally designed for a two-year mission. Instead, it operated for more than a decade beyond that planned lifetime, observing everything from distant stellar explosions to black holes and objects in our own solar system.A telescope built to chase cosmic explosionsLaunched on November 20, 2004, Swift was designed primarily to detect gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), brief but extraordinarily energetic flashes associated with some of the most powerful events in the universe.These bursts can last from fractions of a second to several minutes. Their fleeting nature makes them hard to study. Astronomers must locate them quickly and turn other telescopes toward the source before the light fades.Swift was built to do exactly that. Its Burst Alert Telescope detects gamma-ray bursts and determines their positions, allowing the spacecraft to rapidly turn its X-ray and ultraviolet/optical telescopes toward the event. NASA says the observatory could typically redirect its instruments within about a minute.That rapid-response capability helped transform the study of gamma-ray bursts and made Swift a valuable tool for time-domain astronomy, which examines how astronomical objects change over time.Over its lifetime, the spacecraft observed more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts and studied over 1,400 supernova explosions. It also monitored active galaxies powered by supermassive black holes, observed stars being torn apart by black holes, and studied comets and asteroids.One notable observation came in 2022, when Swift helped investigate GRB 221009A, nicknamed the BOAT (Brightest Of All Time). The extraordinary burst of radiation became one of the brightest gamma-ray events ever detected.An attempted rescue couldn’t save the observatorySwift’s descent accelerated due to increased solar activity. When the Sun becomes more active, it heats Earth’s upper atmosphere, causing it to expand. That increases atmospheric drag on satellites in low Earth orbit, gradually slowing them down and reducing their altitude.NASA attempted to extend Swift’s life through an unusual servicing mission. The agency contracted Arizona-based Katalyst Space Technologies to develop a robotic spacecraft called LINK, designed to rendezvous with Swift, capture it, and raise its orbit.LINK launched on July 3, 2026, aboard Northrop Grumman’s Pegasus XL rocket. However, an attitude-control problem prevented the spacecraft from capturing or boosting Swift. NASA announced in August that the orbit-raising attempt would not proceed, although LINK would continue demonstrating rendezvous and proximity-operation capabilities.With Swift continuing to lose altitude, its science operations eventually became unsustainable. NASA ended the mission after the spacecraft entered safe mode on October 20.A 12-terabyte scientific legacyAlthough Swift is about to disappear from orbit, its observations will remain accessible to researchers. NASA says the mission has produced approximately 12 terabytes of data, including nearly 22 years of brightness measurements, multiwavelength spectra, and more than 1.5 million images from its Ultraviolet/Optical Telescope.The archive has already contributed to approximately 7,000 scientific papers. Its value could continue growing as astronomers revisit older observations, combine them with newer measurements, and apply improved analytical techniques.NASA’s Swift archive makes the mission’s observations publicly accessible, allowing researchers around the world to explore its data.Swift’s departure will nevertheless leave a gap. NASA is exploring ways to maintain rapid-response observations of cosmic events using existing space telescopes and potentially new commercial capabilities.For a spacecraft that spent more than two decades chasing some of the universe’s briefest and most energetic flashes, its final chapter is fittingly unusual. Swift may soon burn up in Earth’s atmosphere, but the cosmic events it captured will remain available for astronomers to study long after its last signal is gone.

title: Northrop Grumman secures $56 million for Triton drone upgrade
content: Northrop Grumman will upgrade a single U.S. Navy MQ-4C Triton maritime surveillance drone under a nearly $56 million contract modification awarded on October 28. The work covers installation of a B7 retrofit material kit and is scheduled for completion in May 2030.Naval Air Systems Command awarded the firm-fixed-price modification without competition, committing the full $55,986,538 from fiscal 2027 aircraft procurement funds. The announcement does not identify the aircraft receiving the kit or explain what equipment, software, or capabilities the installation will change.Upgrade details remain undisclosedNorthrop Grumman will perform 64 percent of the work in Palmdale, California, where Triton aircraft are built. Another 34 percent will take place in San Diego, with the remaining 2 percent distributed across other U.S. locations.The B7 designation follows the numbering used for individual Triton airframes in earlier contracts. However, the Navy has not confirmed whether this installation will bring the aircraft to the Integrated Functional Capability 4 standard, commonly called IFC-4.Previous contracts explicitly identified that configuration. A 2023 award worth $83.1 million covered upgrades to air vehicles B9 and B10, along with a main operating base, to the multi-intelligence standard.The latest contract also resembles earlier work on air vehicle B5. In late 2025, the Navy exercised a $45.75 million option covering engineering, tooling, and labor to complete IFC-4 changes on that aircraft. That work had the same geographic split and a June 2029 completion target.Sensors expand Triton’s intelligence roleIFC-4 introduced signals intelligence capabilities to Triton through additional sensors for electronic intelligence and communications intelligence, according to Northrop Grumman.The sensors brought stricter requirements for protecting collected data, prompting hardware and software changes across the aircraft and its ground systems. The Navy first flew a Triton in the IFC-4 configuration on July 29, 2021.Other surveillance equipment includes the AN/ZPY-3 Multi-Function Active Sensor, an X-band electronically scanned radar mounted beneath the fuselage, and the Raytheon AN/DAS-3 electro-optical and infrared turret.Triton’s structure also differs substantially from the RQ-4 Global Hawk on which it is based. Northrop strengthened the airframe and wings and added de-icing equipment and lightning protection.Those changes allow the unarmed aircraft to descend from approximately 50,000 feet to around 10,000 feet to identify ships before returning to its higher patrol altitude.Further fleet changes take shapeThe latest contract follows another October order worth $66 million to install 17 U.S. Navy and 16 Australian engineering changes on operational Tritons.Separately, Naval Air Systems Command posted an October 22 notice outlining plans for a sole-source contract with Northrop Grumman covering engineering, software and cyber sustainment, logistics, and engineering change proposals.That proposed agreement would support both the U.S. Navy and Royal Australian Air Force, with an award expected in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.Australia acquires Tritons through a cooperative program covering development, production, and sustainment. Meanwhile, the B7 installation remains narrowly defined in the public announcement: a funded upgrade to one aircraft, with its precise technical scope and resulting configuration still undisclosed by the Navy.

title: Robotic moth grows its own sensors with UV light and artificial blood
content: Imagine sending a robot into an unfamiliar environment without knowing what it might encounter. If it comes across something its existing sensors cannot detect, it would normally need to return to a workshop for new equipment. But what if it could instead grow a new sensor right where it needs one?A team of researchers has demonstrated a step toward this possibility with a moth-shaped robot that uses an artificial circulatory system to transport chemical ingredients through its body and grow a functioning light sensor wherever ultraviolet (UV) light strikes. “I’m working on giving robots a circulatory system, so they can transport molecular building blocks across the whole body and create the hardware they need, on site, where and when it’s needed,” Kadri-Ann Pankratov, lead researcher and a PhD student at the University of Tartu in Estonia, said.The experiment suggests that robots could eventually adapt not just by changing how they use existing hardware, but by chemically creating entirely new capabilities within their bodies.Taking a cue from how insects circulate materialsMost robots leave the factory with their hardware already decided. Engineers must anticipate which sensors they will need and where to install them. Although adaptive software can help robots respond to unexpected situations, it cannot compensate for a missing physical sensor. Adding entirely new capabilities after deployment remains a significant engineering challenge.The researchers from the University of Tartu in Estonia and the Italian Institute of Technology explored whether a robot could overcome this limitation by borrowing an idea from nature: circulation. In insects, an open circulatory system pumps hemolymph, a blood-like fluid, through the body, allowing it to reach different organs and tissues.The team took inspiration from moths, particularly the blue underwing (Catocala fraxini). Its relatively flat wings offered a convenient model because their circulation happens largely in a single plane, simplifying the robot’s internal plumbing.The researchers 3D-printed a transparent plastic body using polyethylene terephthalate glycol (PETG). Each of its two wings covered 86 square centimeters and contained millimeter-wide channels resembling veins. Smaller gaps between the printed plastic lines formed a network of microchannels, allowing liquids to penetrate about 10 micrometers into the material. A single pump circulated around 3 milliliters (ml) of liquid throughout the robot, distributing chemical ingredients across its body.UV light turns part of robot into a sensorTo create a light receptor, the researchers circulated an artificial hemolymph containing pyrrole, a light-activated chemical initiator, and a cellulose-based additive called cellulose acetate propionate (CAP). The mixture entered the plastic’s internal microchannels and infused the surrounding material.When UV light struck a particular area for approximately one minute, it triggered a chemical reaction that converted pyrrole into polypyrrole, an electrically conductive polymer. The previously transparent plastic gradually turned black wherever the reaction occurred, providing visible evidence of the newly formed material.Using a stencil, the researchers could control the sensor’s shape and position with a precision of 0.3 millimeters.The resulting material responded to UV exposure by temporarily changing its electrical properties. When UV light hit it, its electrical impedance dropped, allowing an onboard microcontroller to detect the signal. The robot could then respond by flapping its wings using a shape-memory wire or flashing an LED.In other words, the robot acquired a sensing ability it did not possess when it was manufactured.“You can, of course, use a ready-made photodiode, but you’d have to know quite precisely where to put it. That can be difficult to know beforehand as robots go into more dangerous and complicated environments. Growing the receptor on site means the environment itself can pattern the robot, based on what is actually happening at that time,” ,” Pankratov said.The researchers also noticed something unexpected: the sensor became increasingly sensitive with repeated UV exposure. Residual pyrrole continued polymerizing, creating additional polypyrrole structures and changing the sensor’s electrical properties. The team interprets this as a form of material memory, in which the sensor’s physical structure retains a record of its previous experiences. Remarkably, the sensors remained functional after more than four months of storage.Will robots grow their own hardware?The demonstration is still a proof of concept. It relies on a single predetermined chemical reaction, and sensor formation is irreversible. Researchers also controlled when the chemical mixture entered the robot and used a stencil to determine where the sensor developed. Plus, the robot cannot yet independently decide which new hardware it needs or invent a way to manufacture it.Nevertheless, the approach could eventually help robots operating in unfamiliar environments, from forests and collapsed buildings to underwater locations and other planets. The same circulatory network could transport different chemicals to produce materials for corrosion protection, electromagnetic shielding, or even interfaces with living tissue. Researchers also hope to explore chemical systems that could be reversible.The next challenge is making the process less dependent on predetermined instructions. “Right now, the robot’s central intelligence knew which component was coming. How do we make it so that it doesn’t have to be predetermined? We don’t yet have a good source of inspiration in biology for that,” Pankratov said.Pankratov hopes that artificial blood and circulatory systems could become an established option in robotics within the next decade, potentially allowing machines to develop capabilities in response to the environments they encounter.The study is published in the journal Advanced Science.
